      - **extended-community** `string[]`: Apply only to a route whose EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute carries this value.
        The EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 4360, type 16. The value takes the form target:ASN:NN or origin:ASN:NN, or it is a hex string.
      - **large-community** `string[]`: Apply only to a route whose LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute carries this value.
        The LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 8092, type 32. The value takes the form GA:LD1:LD2, for example 65001:100:200.
    - **set** `container`: Attributes Ze sets on a matching route.
      Ze applies only the leaves that are present in this container, and keeps every other attribute unchanged.
      - **as-path-prepend** `uint8`: Prepend the local AS to AS_PATH this many times.
        Ze prepends the local-as of the peer, which the session config holds. The range 1 to 32 stops the path from growing without a limit.
      - **community-add** `string[]`: Standard community values to add (ASN:VAL format).
        Ze adds the values to the COMMUNITIES attribute of RFC 1997 and keeps every community already on the route. Ze reads each value at config load, and refuses the modifier when one does not parse.
      - **community-remove** `string[]`: Standard community values to remove (ASN:VAL format).
        Ze removes only the values named here, and keeps every other community of the route. A value the route does not carry costs nothing. Ze reads each value at config load, and refuses the modifier when one does not parse.
      - **extended-community-add** `string[]`: Extended community values to add (target:ASN:NN or hex).
        The EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 4360, type 16, and each value is 8 bytes. target names a Route Target and origin names a Route Origin. A hex string writes the 8 bytes Ze has no keyword for.
      - **extended-community-remove** `string[]`: Extended community values to remove (target:ASN:NN or hex).
        Ze removes only the values named here, and leaves the standard and large communities of the route untouched. A value the route does not carry costs nothing.
      - **large-community-add** `string[]`: Large community values to add (GA:LD1:LD2 format).
        The LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 8092, type 32, and it carries three 4-byte fields. A 4-byte ASN therefore fits, which a standard community cannot hold.
      - **large-community-remove** `string[]`: Large community values to remove (GA:LD1:LD2 format).
        Ze removes only the values named here, and leaves the standard and extended communities of the route untouched. A value the route does not carry costs nothing.
      - **local-preference** `uint32`: Set LOCAL_PREF attribute (RFC 4271 type 5).
        Ze replaces the value the route carried. RFC 4271 Section 5.1.5 forbids the attribute in an UPDATE to an external peer, so the value serves the local decision process and the internal peers. The leaf is mutually exclusive with increment local-preference and decrement local-preference.
      - **med** `uint32`: Set MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute (RFC 4271 type 4).
        Ze replaces the metric the route carried, and writes one on a route that carried none. The leaf is mutually exclusive with del med, increment med and decrement med, and Ze refuses a modifier that carries two of them.
      - **next-hop** `ip-address`: Set the NEXT_HOP attribute of the route.
        NEXT_HOP is RFC 4271 type 3, and it carries an IPv4 address only. An IPv6 next-hop travels in the MP_REACH attribute instead, so this leaf does not set one.
      - **origin** `enumeration`: Set ORIGIN attribute (RFC 4271 type 1).
        The decision process reads the attribute at step 3, after LOCAL_PREF and the AS_PATH length. igp wins over egp, and egp wins over incomplete. Ze replaces whatever the route carried.
        - `egp`: The route came from the retired EGP protocol.
        - `igp`: The route started inside the local AS.
        - `incomplete`: The route came from another source, such as redistribution.
  - **prefix-list <name>** `list`: Named prefix-list filter instance.
    Each list holds an ordered set of match entries. Ze evaluates the entries in order, and the first match wins. A route prefix that matches no entry is denied.
    - **entry <prefix>** `list`: Ordered match entry. First match wins per route prefix.
      Ze judges each prefix of an UPDATE on its own. An UPDATE whose prefixes are all accepted passes unchanged, and one whose prefixes are all rejected is dropped. A mixed UPDATE is rewritten to carry the accepted prefixes only. An UPDATE that carries no prefix is accepted.
      - **action** `enumeration`: Action applied when this entry matches a route prefix.
        The first entry that matches a route prefix decides it, and no later entry is read for that prefix. A prefix that matches no entry is rejected, so a list needs no closing reject entry.
        - `accept`: Accept route prefixes matching this entry.
        - `reject`: Reject route prefixes matching this entry.
      - **ge** `uint8`: Minimum match length (greater-than-or-equal). Defaults to the prefix length of this entry.
        Ze refuses a value of more than 32 on an IPv4 entry, and more than 128 on an IPv6 entry. Ze also refuses a ge greater than the le of the same entry. Write 0.0.0.0/0 with ge 8 and le 24 to accept every route between /8 and /24.
      - **le** `uint8`: Maximum match length (less-than-or-equal). Defaults to 32 for IPv4 or 128 for IPv6.
        The default accepts every length inside the entry, so an entry with no le and no ge matches the prefix and everything under it. Ze refuses a value greater than the family maximum rather than letting the entry match nothing.
  - **reject-asn <name>** `list`: Named list of ASNs rejected by their position in the AS_PATH.
    Every ASN written under the list is looked for in the AS_PATH of the route. The keyword it sits under decides which positions reject it. The list is an unordered reject set, so any keyword that matches rejects the route and no keyword wins over another. Ze reads the positions first and the patterns after them.
    - **anywhere** `asn[]`: Reject these ASNs at any position: direct, transit and origin together.
      The keyword is the union of the other three, so it rejects the ASN wherever it sits. The reject log line still names which of the three caught the route.
    - **direct** `asn[]`: Reject these ASNs where they are the peer we are talking to, prepends collapsed.
      The position is the leading run of tokens equal to the ASN of the sending peer, so four prepends are one direct position. On export no ASN is direct, because the filter input carries the destination peer rather than the sender. A path that starts with another ASN is a leak, and direct does not catch it.
    - **indirect** `asn[]`: Reject these ASNs anywhere they are NOT the peer we are talking to.
      The keyword covers transit and origin together. It is the leaf an operator writes for RFC 7454 Section 9. The route reached you through the ASN, and a direct session with that ASN is still fine. On export the sender is unknown, so indirect covers the whole path.
    - **nth <index>** `list`: Reject the listed ASNs at one collapsed position of the AS_PATH.
      Ze counts the positions from us, and 1 is the ASN we are talking to. A run of consecutive identical ASNs counts once, so a peer cannot move your rule by a prepend. The keyword cuts across the other five, because an ASN at position 2 CAN also be transit.
      - **asn** `asn[]`: The ASNs this position rejects.
        The completion of the leaf offers a curated table of transit-free networks, and that table constrains nothing. Every ASN the type admits stays valid, and an ASN the table never held is accepted with no warning. show bgp reject-asn known transit-free prints the table.
    - **origin** `asn[]`: Reject these ASNs where they are the last ASN of the AS_PATH.
      The last ASN of the path announced the route. The leading run of the sender wins over that last position, so a lone ASN sent by the peer that owns it is direct rather than the origin.
    - **regex** `string[]`: Go RE2 patterns matched against the whole space-separated AS_PATH string.
      No position applies to a pattern. Ze matches it against the flat path, so a pattern reaches an ASN inside an AS_SET and meets no bracket. The 512-character bound is the bound bgp-filter-aspath applies to a regex. Ze reads the patterns only when no position matched.
    - **transit** `asn[]`: Reject these ASNs where they sit past the peer and are not the last ASN of the AS_PATH.
      A token is transit when it sits neither inside the leading run of the sender nor at the end of the path. Ze gives every token exactly one of direct, transit and origin.
  - **remove-private-as <name>** `list`: Named action filter that removes RFC 6996 Private Use ASNs.
    Ze rewrites AS_PATH and AS4_PATH, and the filter runs on an import chain and on an export chain. A path that carries no Private Use ASN passes through unchanged.
    - **replace-with** `enumeration`: Replacement mode. When absent, Private Use ASNs are stripped.
      RFC 6996 Section 5 gives the ranges, which are 64512 to 65534 and 4200000000 to 4294967294. An absent leaf strips each of those ASNs, so the path loses one hop for each. peer-as writes the ASN of the peer in its place, so the path keeps its length.
      - `peer-as`: Replace Private Use ASNs with the neighbor peer ASN.
- **rib** `container`: RIB plugin state and operations.
  The subtree is read-only, so the CLI refuses set on every node under it. No code answers a read of it today. show bgp rib status reports the live per-peer counts, and show bgp rib reports the routes. request bgp rib inject and request bgp rib withdraw change what the RIB holds.
  - **adj-rib-in** `container`: Routes received from peers.
    RFC 4271 Section 3.2 states that the Adj-RIBs-In "contains unprocessed routing information that has been advertised to the local BGP speaker by its peers". show bgp rib received reports those routes, and clear bgp rib in <peer> discards the routes of one peer. No code answers a read of this subtree.
    - **peer <address>** `list`: Per-peer Adj-RIB-In.
      One entry for each peer that holds a route, keyed by the peer address. show bgp rib status answers the same numbers under route-counts, which carries an in value and an out value for each peer address.
      - **route-count** `uint32`: Number of routes from this peer.
        The count covers every address family of the peer. show bgp rib status answers it as the in value under route-counts, where a family filter scopes the number to one family.
  - **adj-rib-out** `container`: Routes sent to peers.
    RFC 4271 Section 3.2 states that the Adj-RIBs-Out "stores information the local BGP speaker selected for advertisement to its peers". show bgp rib sent reports those routes. No code answers a read of this subtree.
    - **peer <address>** `list`: Per-peer Adj-RIB-Out.
      One entry for each peer that holds a route, keyed by the peer address. show bgp rib status answers the same numbers under route-counts, which carries an in value and an out value for each peer address.
      - **route-count** `uint32`: Number of routes to this peer.
        The count covers every address family of the peer. show bgp rib status answers it as the out value under route-counts, where a family filter scopes the number to one family.
- **route-server** `container`: Route server plugin tuning parameters
  The route server forwards an UPDATE from one client to every other client. Each source peer gets its own worker, and the worker stops after 5 seconds with no work. A peer joins the client set with the rs-client leaf of its session, not with this container.
  - **worker-queue-size** `uint32`: Worker channel capacity per source peer, overridden by ze.bgp.route-server.worker-queue-size.
    Per-source-peer worker channel capacity. The ze.bgp.route-server.worker-queue-size environment variable overrides this value.
- **router-id** `ipv4-address`: BGP Router ID for this speaker. The leaf is required.
  RFC 6286 Section 2.1 defines the BGP Identifier as a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer. Ze therefore rejects 0.0.0.0. A peer that implements RFC 6286 Section 2.2 answers an OPEN that carries 0.0.0.0 with Bad BGP Identifier.
- **rpki** `container`: RPKI origin validation of a received route (RFC 6811).
  The container carries presence. Ze validates a route only when cache-server holds at least one entry, so an empty container validates nothing. The container also holds the validation timeout, the origin-validation actions, and the ASPA block. A peer and a group override an action leaf of their own. Neither can name a cache server, because the RTR transport is global.
  - **action** `container`: Global origin-validation actions.
    RFC 6811 Section 3 makes the action of each validation state configurable by the operator.
    - **invalid** `validation-action`: Action Ze applies to a route in the Invalid validation state.
      The default is reject, which excludes the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.
      - `accept`: Keep the route and write no log line.
      - `log-only`: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.
      - `reject`: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.
    - **not-found** `validation-action`: Action Ze applies to a route in the NotFound validation state.
      The default is accept, which keeps the route and writes no log line.
      - `accept`: Keep the route and write no log line.
      - `log-only`: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.
      - `reject`: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.
  - **aspa** `container`: AS_PATH verification against the ASPA records, and the action of each result.
    validation turns the verification on and its default is false. Ze reads an ASPA record over version 2 of the RTR protocol alone. A session Ze downgrades to version 1 carries none. Ze refuses an ASPA PDU on a version 1 session as a protocol violation. action holds the action of each path state, and a peer or a group overrides those two leaves.
    - **action** `container`: Global action Ze applies for each ASPA path state.
      invalid holds the action of an ASPA Invalid path and unknown that of an ASPA Unknown path. Both apply only while aspa validation is true. A peer or a group overrides each leaf.
      - **invalid** `validation-action`: Action Ze applies to a route in the ASPA Invalid path state.
        The default is log-only, which keeps the route, marks it with its state, and writes a log line.
        - `accept`: Keep the route and write no log line.
        - `log-only`: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.
        - `reject`: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.
      - **unknown** `validation-action`: Action Ze applies to a route in the ASPA Unknown path state.
        The default is accept, which keeps the route and writes no log line.
        - `accept`: Keep the route and write no log line.
        - `log-only`: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.
        - `reject`: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.
    - **validation** `boolean`: Verify the AS path of a route against the ASPA records.
      Ze reads the ASPA records over version 2 of the RTR protocol.
  - **cache-server <address>** `list`: RTR cache servers Ze reads the validated ROA and ASPA records from.
    The list key is the address, which is an IP address or a hostname. Ze opens one RTR session to every entry at the same time, and merges what the entries send into one cache. A second entry gives redundancy. Each entry carries the port, the preference and the source address. An empty list leaves validation off.
    - **port** `uint16`: TCP port of the RTR cache server.
      Ze opens a TCP connection to this port on the cache server. The default is 323.
    - **preference** `uint8`: Preference of this cache server.
      Ze runs a session to every cache server at the same time and selects none of them, so the value changes no behavior today. show bgp rpki status reports it for each server.
    - **source-address** `ip-address`: Source IP address of an outbound RTR connection.
      Set this leaf when the RTR connection MUST leave the box from one specific local address.
  - **validation-timeout** `uint16`: Fail-open timeout of a route whose validation is pending.
    The default is 30 seconds. A longer timeout holds a route in the pending state for longer.
- **session** `container`: Global BGP session defaults
  A group value overrides this global value, and a peer value overrides the group value. The container holds the local ASN and the shared-router-id switch.
  - **allow-shared-router-id** `boolean`: Accept a peer whose BGP Identifier duplicates another established peer in the same AS.
    The default is false, which enforces AS-wide uniqueness: Ze rejects the second OPEN with Bad BGP Identifier. RFC 6286 Section 2.1 makes AS-wide uniqueness a SHOULD alone, so a shared identifier is conformant. Set the leaf true when the duplication is intentional, for example one anycast speaker (AS112) that peers over both IPv4 and IPv6 with the same router-id. When the leaf is true, Ze skips the AS-wide uniqueness claim alone. RFC 6286 Section 2.2 validation still applies, and it rejects a zero identifier, and this speaker's own identifier from an internal peer. Section 2.3 connection collision resolution is implemented, and this leaf does not disable it.
  - **asn** `container`: AS number configuration
    At this global level the container holds the local ASN alone. The same container under a group or a peer also holds remote and local-options.
    - **local** `asn`: Local Autonomous System Number (required)
      Ze sends the value as My Autonomous System in OPEN. A group or a peer can override it. Ze keeps this global value for the local-as modifiers, which need the real AS number.
- **update** `list`: Native Ze route announcements
  Ze announces every route of the block to the peers the block applies to. The block is written at the global level, the group level, and the peer level, and the three accumulate.
  - **attribute** `container`: Path attributes for routes in this block
    Every NLRI of the block takes the same attributes. To announce two prefixes that carry different attributes, write two update blocks.
    - **aggregator** `string`: AGGREGATOR attribute (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.7). The format is AS:IP.
      The attribute identifies the AS and the router that formed the aggregate.
    - **as-path** `string[]`: AS_PATH segments prepended to the route, as space-separated ASNs.
      The list is an ordered sequence. A repeated ASN is a prepend that counts, so Ze does not deduplicate it (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.2). AS_PATH decides loop detection, and it decides path selection, where the shorter path is preferred.
    - **atomic-aggregate** `boolean`: ATOMIC_AGGREGATE flag (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.6).
      The flag signals that aggregation formed the route, and that AS_PATH information was lost.
    - **attribute** `string[]`: Raw BGP attributes in hex encoding, as flags:type:hex-value.
      The list carries an attribute that no named field covers.
    - **bgp-prefix-sid** `container`: Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 8669).
      The attribute carries an MPLS label index for Segment Routing. A node can therefore advertise its SID without a per-prefix label allocation.
    - **bgp-prefix-sid-srv6** `container`: SRv6 Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 9252).
      The attribute carries SRv6 SID information for IPv6 Segment Routing, and it includes the SRv6 L3 Service TLVs.
    - **cluster-list** `ipv4-address[]`: CLUSTER_LIST for route reflection (RFC 4456).
      Each reflector prepends its cluster ID. The list detects a loop between reflectors.
    - **community** `string[]`: Standard BGP communities (RFC 1997).
      The format is AS:value, for example 65000:100. A well-known name is also accepted, such as no-export or no-advertise.
    - **extended-community** `string[]`: Extended communities (RFC 4360). The format is type:admin:value.
      An extended community carries a route target, a site-of-origin, or VPN semantics.
    - **label** `string`: MPLS label value for a labeled unicast route (RFC 3107). The value is a number.
      Ze accepts a decimal number from 0 to 1048575, which is the 20-bit label field. It accepts no keyword. Write the labels leaf-list for a stack of more than one label.
    - **labels** `string[]`: MPLS label stack for a multi-label route (RFC 8277).
      The list is an ordered sequence from bottom to top. Ze keeps a repeated label, and it does not deduplicate the stack.
    - **large-community** `string[]`: Large BGP communities (RFC 8092). Format: global:local1:local2. Supports 4-byte ASNs natively.
      Each value is three 32-bit numbers separated by colons, which is 12 octets on the wire. The global part holds a 4-byte ASN, which a standard community of RFC 1997 cannot hold.
    - **local-preference** `uint32`: LOCAL_PREF value for iBGP best-path selection. The higher value wins.
      LOCAL_PREF has a meaning inside a single AS alone (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.5). The default is 100.
    - **med** `uint32`: Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED). The lower value is preferred.
      MED influences the inbound path selection that an external peer makes (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4).
    - **next-hop** `union`: Next hop address or 'self'
      self resolves at send time to the local address of the session, so each peer reads its own next hop. An IP address reaches every peer of the block unchanged. Ze refuses an IPv6 link-local address here, because RFC 2545 Section 3 puts the global address in that field.
      - `self`: Resolve the next hop at send time to the local address of each session.
    - **origin** `enumeration`: ORIGIN attribute (RFC 4271 Section 4.3)
      RFC 4271 Section 4.3 gives three values. igp is reachability interior to the originating AS. egp is reachability learned through the EGP protocol. incomplete is reachability learned by some other means, for example a redistributed static route.
      - `egp`: Exterior Gateway Protocol
      - `igp`: Interior Gateway Protocol
      - `incomplete`: Incomplete origin
    - **originator-id** `ipv4-address`: ORIGINATOR_ID for route reflection (RFC 4456).
      The reflector sets the attribute to the router ID of the originating router. The attribute prevents a loop.
    - **path-information** `string`: ADD-PATH path identifier (RFC 7911).
      The identifier separates the several paths that one peer sends for the same prefix.
    - **rd** `route-distinguisher`: Route Distinguisher (RFC 4364). The format is ASN:nn or IP:nn.
      Ze prepends the Route Distinguisher to the prefix, which makes a unique VPN route.
    - **split** `string`: Split one prefix into more-specific prefixes for the announcement.
      The format is /length. For example, /24 splits a /16 into 256 prefixes of /24.
  - **name** `string`: Optional label for this update block (display only)
    The list carries no key, so the CLI and the web UI show this label in place of one. The label reaches no BGP message.
  - **nlri <name>** `list`: Routes this update block announces, one entry for each address family.
    Every entry takes the attribute block of the update block. The key is the family name, and content carries the operation keyword and the prefixes. An update block that declares no nlri entry is refused at config load.
    - **content** `string`: Operation, qualifiers, and payload
      The form is an operation keyword, then an optional rd and label, then one or more prefixes. add, del and eor are the operation keywords, and one of them is required. A block that carries del or eor announces nothing at config load.
  - **watchdog** `container`: Watchdog-controlled route - held until 'bgp watchdog announce <name>'
    The bgp-watchdog plugin owns every route of the block, so the BGP engine holds none of them as a static route. The plugin sends a route that is not withdrawn when the session reaches Established.
    - **name** `string`: Watchdog group name
      request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces every route that carries the name, and request bgp watchdog withdraw <name> withdraws them. Ze skips a block whose name is empty.
    - **withdraw** `boolean`: Start in withdrawn state (default true)
      The bgp-watchdog plugin reads the PRESENCE of the leaf and not its value, so withdraw false starts every route of the block withdrawn exactly as withdraw true does. Delete the leaf to announce the routes as soon as the session reaches Established. request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces a withdrawn route.
- **update-delay** `container`: Hold the first advertisement at startup until the RIB settles.
  An absent container is the default, and it keeps the behavior Ze had before the container existed: each peer advertises as soon as it reaches Established. The container holds max-delay, which enables the feature and bounds the wait, and establish-wait, which can end the wait early. While Ze holds, sessions negotiate, reach Established and receive UPDATE messages as usual. Ze sends no UPDATE and no End-of-RIB marker until the hold ends. RFC 4724 Section 4.1 prescribes the same deferral for a speaker that restarts, and requires the configurable upper bound max-delay supplies. The hold applies at startup alone: a reload validates a changed value and Ze keeps the hold it already armed, or none, so a new value takes effect at the next restart. Ze does not enforce a relation between max-delay and the Restart Time it advertises in its graceful-restart capability, so keep max-delay below that number yourself. A neighbor whose own restart timer expires first discards the routes it kept for Ze. Read `show bgp update-delay` to see whether a speaker is holding and what it waits for.
  - **establish-wait** `uint16`: Seconds after which the peers that are held end the hold. Must not exceed max-delay.
    The leaf is optional, and an absent leaf lets only max-delay and full convergence end the hold. When these seconds elapse and one or more peers are held, Ze ends the hold and advertises to them, whether or not they sent an End-of-RIB marker. When no peer is held, Ze keeps waiting until max-delay, because there is no peer to advertise to yet. Ze refuses a configuration where this value is more than max-delay.
  - **max-delay** `uint16`: Seconds to hold the first advertisement. 0 disables the hold.
    0 is the default and disables the feature. A value of more than 0 arms the hold when the daemon starts its peers. The hold ends when every configured peer sends its End-of-RIB marker, or when establish-wait ends it early, or when these seconds elapse, whichever comes first. Ze waits for the marker and not for Established, because Established says only that the neighbor answered. RFC 4724 Section 4.1 excludes a peer that advertised no graceful-restart capability and a peer that is itself restarting, and Ze excludes the same two. A peer that never comes up cannot extend the wait past this number.

## class-of-service

*Provided by `cos` ([ze-cos-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/cos/yang/ze-cos-conf.yang))*

Named class-of-service profiles.

A profile maps the 3-bit PCP field of an 802.1Q header to an internal priority, in the ingress direction and in the egress direction. An interface leaf and a unit leaf name the profile they use.

- **ieee-802.1p <name>** `list`: An 802.1p QoS profile.
  The profile defines the mapping between the 3-bit PCP field in the 802.1Q header and the internal priorities. It covers the ingress direction and the egress direction.
  - **egress** `container`: Priority-to-PCP mapping of a transmitted tagged frame.
    Ze reads this mapping when it stamps the PCP field of a frame it transmits.
    - **priority <value>** `list`: Map one internal priority to a transmitted PCP value.
      The list key is the internal priority, so the list holds at most one entry for each of the eight priorities.
      - **pcp** `uint8`: PCP value Ze stamps in the 802.1Q header.
        IEEE 802.1Q defines the Priority Code Point field, which is 3 bits wide and holds a value from 0 to 7.
  - **ingress** `container`: PCP-to-priority mapping of a received tagged frame.
    Ze reads this mapping when it takes the internal priority of a frame it receives.
    - **pcp <value>** `list`: Map one received PCP value to an internal priority.
      The list key is the PCP value, so the list holds at most one entry for each of the eight values.
      - **priority** `uint8`: Internal priority Ze gives to a matching frame.
        The value runs from 0 to 7.

## connected

*Provided by `connected` ([ze-connected-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/connected/yang/ze-connected-conf.yang))*

Connected route redistribution. Presence enables the plugin.

The container carries no leaf, so writing it is the whole configuration. The plugin watches each interface address event and emits the network prefix of that address on the redistribute event bus. It counts the addresses of one prefix, so two addresses in one subnet announce the prefix once. The withdrawal waits for the last address of that prefix. The plugin registers the connected route source, and a redistribute statement names that source.


## control-plane-protection

*Provided by `copp-input-chain` ([ze-copp-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/copp/yang/ze-copp-conf.yang))*

Control-plane policing configuration.

Ze compiles the containers under it into one nftables table named ze_copp, which carries a base input chain at priority 0. The ze_ prefix is what makes the firewall backend own that table and withdraw it when you delete the configuration. The bgp container is the only policy Ze builds today.

- **bgp** `container`: Rate-limit new TCP connections to the BGP listen port.
  The container carries presence, so Ze builds the ze_copp table when you write it and removes the table when you delete it. The chain accepts an established or related connection first, then a connection from each trusted-source prefix, and applies the rate to what is left.
  - **burst** `uint32`: Burst size (packets or bytes matching the rate unit).
    The unit follows the unit of rate: a packet count where rate counts packets, and a byte count where rate names a byte unit. The leaf has no default, and Ze gives the kernel a burst of 0 when it is absent.
  - **over-limit-policy** `enumeration`: What Ze does with the packets that exceed the rate limit.
    accept, the default, counts the over-limit packets and lets them through. The limit then reports load and stops nothing. drop discards a new TCP connection to a protected port once the rate is exceeded. Either setting reaches the over-limit packets alone. The input chain keeps an accept policy, so SSH, ICMP and every service this table never names stay reachable. The first term accepts an established session before the limit is read, so drop never closes a session that is already up.
    - `accept`: Accept over-limit packets (safe default).
    - `drop`: Drop over-limit packets.
  - **protected-port** `uint16[]`: TCP port(s) the control-plane policing rules protect, 179 (BGP) by default.
    TCP port(s) to protect. Ze uses 179, the BGP port, when this leaf is omitted. Set a different value when the BGP listener uses another port.
  - **rate** `rate-spec`: Rate limit for new connections (e.g., 100/second).
    The leaf is mandatory, so Ze refuses the container without it. The value is a count, an optional byte unit, and a time unit, as in 100/second or 1mbytes/second. The limit reaches a new TCP connection to a protected port alone, because the chain accepts an established connection before it.
  - **trusted-source** `string[]`: Source prefixes that bypass the rate limit. Typically the addresses of configured BGP peers.
    Ze adds one accept term for each prefix, above the rate limit term. The term matches TCP from that source to a protected port, so a trusted peer never meets the limit. Ze refuses a value that is not an IPv4 prefix or an IPv6 prefix.

## ddos

Distributed denial-of-service detection and mitigation subsystem.

Distributed denial-of-service detection and mitigation subsystem. This module declares the container, and the flowtriq, observe, local and flowspec plugins each augment it. The detect subtree decides that an attack is present, and a responder under one of those subtrees acts on the event.

- **detect** `container`: Detect a volumetric attack from the traffic Ze already sees.
  *Provided by `ddos-detect-flow-source` ([ze-ddos-detect-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ddos/detect/yang/ze-ddos-detect-conf.yang))*
  Detection is separate from mitigation: this container decides that an attack is happening and emits an event. A responder under flowspec or local is what acts on that event, and none is armed by default.
  - **absolute-floor** `uint32`: Minimum threshold in PPS regardless of baseline.
    Minimum threshold in PPS regardless of baseline, default 5000. A quiet link cannot trigger on a small burst, because the threshold never falls under this value. Five times this value is also the packet-rate escape from startup-grace, so a rate over 25000 PPS triggers at the default while the grace period runs.
  - **baseline-window** `uint32`: Rolling baseline window size in samples.
    Rolling baseline window size in samples, and one sample is one evaluation, so one check-interval. The window p99 is recalculated every 10 admitted samples, so a cold detector runs on absolute-floor alone for its first 10 evaluations. A sample taken while the rate is over the threshold is refused, so an attack cannot raise the threshold that detects it. One sample in 3600 consecutive refused samples is admitted, which lets a lasting rise in traffic move the baseline. A persisted baseline is restored only when it carries 50 samples or more.
  - **bps-floor** `uint64`: Minimum bandwidth in bits/sec below which the BPS trigger is inert.
    Minimum bandwidth in bits/sec below which the BPS trigger is inert. The default is 50 Mbps. The value is expressed in bits/sec, which is the operator unit. The detector's internal rate is bytes/sec, and it converts the value.
  - **bps-threshold-multiplier** `decimal-2`: Baseline p99 multiplier for the bandwidth (BPS) trigger.
    Baseline p99 multiplier for the bandwidth (BPS) trigger. The trigger catches low-PPS, high-bandwidth amplification, such as NTP, memcached and CLDAP, that the packet-rate threshold misses.
  - **bps-trigger-enable** `boolean`: Enable the bandwidth (BPS) trigger beside the PPS threshold.
    Enable the bandwidth (BPS) trigger alongside the PPS threshold. When this leaf is false, only the packet-rate threshold can trigger detection.
  - **characterize-enable** `boolean`: Run Stage-2 flow characterization on a detected attack.
    Run Stage-2 flow characterization. The stage classifies the family and the narrowest vector from the flow-export recent-flow ring, and emits AttackCharacterized. When this leaf is false, the detector still emits the coarse AttackDetected target from traffic-usage.
  - **characterize-timeout** `uint16`: Milliseconds budget for the on-trigger queries.
    Milliseconds budget for the on-trigger traffic-usage and flow-recent queries. On timeout, the detector falls back to the best available target.
  - **characterize-window** `uint16`: Seconds of recent flows to consider when characterizing an attack.
    Seconds of recent flows to consider when characterizing. Flows last seen before this window are ignored. Flows with no timestamp are always kept.
  - **check-interval** `uint16`: Seconds between detection evaluations.
    Seconds between detection evaluations. Both rate feeds publish once a second: the traffic-statistics service, and the interface rate collector Ze falls back to when that service is absent. The detector folds this many samples and evaluates their PEAK, so a flood shorter than the interval still reaches the threshold. Every leaf that counts ticks against the threshold counts evaluations, so its wall-clock meaning is multiplied by this value. The default 1 evaluates every second.
  - **clear-consecutive-checks** `uint16`: Consecutive evaluations below threshold before clearing.
    The count of consecutive evaluations under the threshold that ends an attack. The first one under the threshold moves an active detector to the clearing state and counts as the first check. The default 10 therefore holds the attack live for ten evaluations, which is ten seconds at the default check-interval. One evaluation back over the threshold returns the detector to active and drops the count.
  - **confirm-duration** `uint16`: Consecutive evaluations above threshold before triggering.
    The count of consecutive evaluations over the threshold that arms the detector. One evaluation is check-interval seconds, one second at the default. The default 3 needs three unbroken evaluations over the threshold. A value of 0 or 1 triggers on the first one. One evaluation back under the threshold returns the detector to idle and restarts the count.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the DDoS detector.
    Enable the DDoS detector. Left false, the detector subscribes to no rate feed, so it takes no sample and its baseline stays cold. A commit rebuilds the detector and restores the persisted baseline either way, and the subscription is what this leaf controls.
  - **entropy-threshold** `decimal-2`: Source-address Shannon entropy in bits that marks an attack distributed.
    Source-address Shannon entropy (bits) at or above which an attack is logged as distributed or spoofed. A value of 0 is a single source, and a higher value is more sources.
  - **policy** `container`: Allow and deny traffic policy applied to a detected attack.
    Allow/deny traffic policy applied to detected attacks, indexed by prefix. Ze evaluates the policy by longest-prefix match, where the most specific rule wins, and not by config order. The policy replaces the removed per-responder allowlists. The detector enforces it once and encodes the exempt or mitigate decision on the emitted event, so the responders obey it with no config read.
    - **default-action** `enumeration`: Disposition when no rule matches the attack.
      Disposition when no rule matches. deny means defend, which is detection plus mitigation. allow means exempt from detection entirely.
      - `allow`: Exempt an attack no rule matches from detection entirely.
      - `deny`: Detect and mitigate an attack no rule matches.
    - **rule <prefix>** `list`: One allow or deny rule matched against an attack, keyed by prefix.
      One allow/deny rule matched against an attack, keyed by prefix. Precedence is longest-prefix match, so a /24 rule beats a covering /16 with no ordering.
      - **action** `enumeration`: allow exempts matching traffic and deny subjects it to DDoS handling.
        allow exempts the matched traffic and deny subjects it to DDoS handling. The scope leaf decides how far each one reaches. allow at mitigation scope records the incident and installs no block, and allow at detection scope suppresses the incident. deny at detection scope also records without a block, and deny at mitigation scope is full handling.
        - `allow`: Exempt the matched traffic, as far as the scope leaf reaches.
        - `deny`: Subject the matched traffic to DDoS handling, as far as the scope leaf reaches.
      - **match** `enumeration`: Whether the prefix matches the attack source, the destination, or either.
        Whether the prefix matches the attack source, the victim destination, or either. A source rule takes effect once the attack sources are characterized.
        - `any`: Match the prefix against the attack sources or the destination.
        - `destination`: Match the prefix against the victim destination.
        - `source`: Match the prefix against the attack sources, once they are characterized.
      - **scope** `enumeration`: Stage the action governs, mitigation or detection.
        Stage the action governs. mitigation means detect and record, and for allow it does not block. detection means that for allow the incident is suppressed entirely.
        - `detection`: The action governs detection, so allow suppresses the incident entirely.
        - `mitigation`: The action governs mitigation, so the incident is recorded and allow blocks nothing.
  - **startup-grace** `uint16`: Seconds after startup where only extreme spikes trigger.
    Seconds after startup where only extreme spikes trigger, default 90. The count follows the rate feed, one per second, so check-interval does not change it. A cold baseline warms during the grace period, and the grace stops that warm-up from firing on itself. Two things still trigger: a packet rate over five times absolute-floor, and the bandwidth trigger once its own baseline is ready.
  - **threshold-multiplier** `decimal-2`: Baseline p99 multiplier for the dynamic threshold.
    Baseline p99 multiplier for the dynamic threshold. The threshold is the larger of two numbers: the window p99 multiplied by this leaf, and absolute-floor. The default 3.00 therefore triggers at three times the p99 of normal traffic. A changed value reaches the threshold at the next recalculation, which is within 10 admitted samples.
  - **top-n-sources** `uint16`: Maximum number of attacker source addresses ranked into TopSources by packet volume.
    Maximum number of attacker source addresses ranked into TopSources by packet volume, default 10. Ties are broken by address. The same ranked list is what a source-matching policy rule reads, and every address in it has to fall inside the rule prefix before that rule matches.
- **flowspec** `container`: Answer a detected attack by announcing a BGP FlowSpec rule.
  *Provided by `ddos-flowspec` ([ze-ddos-flowspec-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ddos/flowspec/yang/ze-ddos-flowspec-conf.yang))*
  The rule is announced to a peer, so the traffic is dropped upstream and never reaches this router. It needs a peer that accepts FlowSpec, which is what separates it from the local responder.
  - **action** `enumeration`: FlowSpec traffic-action: discard or rate-limit. Mandatory, with no default.
    Neither discard nor rate-limit is universally safe, so this leaf has no default. discard announces an RFC 8955 traffic-rate of 0, which drops the characterized attack flow. rate-limit announces a byte rate, and it requires an explicit rate-limit-bytes. A rate-limit-bytes of 0 is a valid choice, and it is equivalent to discard on the wire.
    - `discard`: Announce a traffic-rate of 0, which drops the attack flow.
    - `rate-limit`: Announce a traffic-rate of rate-limit-bytes, which that leaf must then carry.
  - **announce-rate-limit** `uint16`: Maximum FlowSpec announcements per minute.
    The most FlowSpec announcements Ze sends in any 60 second window. An announcement over the limit is refused and logged, and the responder stays idle, so the next attack characterization inside the window announces nothing upstream and the one after the window rolls does. The limit protects the BGP sessions the rule goes to: a peer that drops the session over announce churn loses every rule it holds. 10 is the default, and the range is 1 to 600.
  - **backoff-cap** `uint32`: Maximum hold-down after exponential backoff.
    Each probe that saturates doubles the current hold-down, and this value stops the doubling. Ze refuses a backoff-cap under hold-down, and the upper bound is 604800 seconds. 3600 is the default, which stops the wait at one hour.
  - **blackhole-fallback** `boolean`: Announce an immediate upstream discard on a critical-severity AttackDetected.
    When true, a critical-severity AttackDetected (a peak of 5x the threshold or more) engages an immediate upstream discard, in the style of RTBH, and it does not wait for characterization. When false, the default, ze announces the upstream rule only from AttackCharacterized. The rule is then precise before the box goes blind behind the filter.
  - **confidence-min** `uint8`: Minimum incident confidence (0-100) to announce an upstream rule from a characterized attack.
    The default is 0, which accepts any confidence. The blackhole-fallback fast path never applies this minimum, because AttackDetected carries no confidence.
  - **hold-down** `uint32`: Minimum seconds before the first leak-probe after announcement.
    The responder counts one second for each AttackOngoing event the detector emits, and the detector emits one for each traffic sample. The rule stays at full strength for this long, and the first leak-probe follows. A probe that saturates doubles the wait, up to backoff-cap. The range is 1 to 86400 seconds, and 300 is the default.
  - **max-mitigation-duration** `uint32`: Maximum seconds a FlowSpec rule stays announced (0 = no cap).
    The responder measures this against the wall clock, and not against the probe. An attack that goes quiet stops the AttackOngoing events the probe counts, which is the case the probe cannot see. 0 removes the cap, so the rule then stays until a probe withdraws it. 3600 is the default, and the range is 0 to 604800 seconds.
  - **probe-interval** `uint16`: Seconds between leak-probe attempts after hold-down.
    After the hold-down ends the responder waits this long. It then narrows the rule to probe-rate and watches what arrives. 60 is the default, and the range is 1 to 3600 seconds. A shorter interval finds the end of an attack sooner, and it also lets more attack traffic through each time.
  - **probe-rate** `uint32`: Bits per second to allow during a leak-probe.
    The responder compares the rate it measures behind the filter against this value. At or above it, the attack still runs: the rule is tightened again and the hold-down doubles. Under it for a whole probe-window, the rule is withdrawn. 1000000 bits per second is the default, and the value must be 1 or more.
  - **probe-window** `uint16`: Seconds to observe leaked traffic during a probe.
    The responder withdraws the rule when the observed rate stays under probe-rate for this whole window. One second at or above probe-rate ends the probe at once, and the rule goes back to full strength. 10 is the default, and the range is 1 to 300 seconds.
  - **rate-limit-bytes** `uint64`: Bytes per second announced in the RFC 8955 traffic-rate extended community.
    This leaf is required, and validated, when action is rate-limit. It has no default, because no rate is universally safe. A value of 0 is valid, and it encodes the same traffic-rate-0 as discard. Ze does not read the leaf when action is discard. Set it to the per-flow rate you accept toward the victim during mitigation.
  - **response-level** `enumeration`: Action on attack detection: alert (log only) or enforce (announce FlowSpec).
    alert is the default. The responder then logs the announcement it would make, and announces nothing. enforce is the value that puts a rule on the wire. The leaf gates every announce path, the blackhole-fallback fast path included.
    - `alert`: Log the FlowSpec rule the responder would announce, and announce nothing.
    - `enforce`: Announce the FlowSpec rule to the peer.
- **flowtriq** `container`: Feed detected attacks to the FlowTriq reporting service.
  *Provided by `ddos-flowtriq` ([ze-ddos-flowtriq-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ddos/flowtriq/yang/ze-ddos-flowtriq-conf.yang))*
  It reports and mitigates nothing on its own. The traffic still needs a responder under flowspec or local to be stopped.
  - **api-base** `string`: Flowtriq API base URL.
    Ze appends a path to this value, so a trailing slash gives a double slash in the request. /agent/incidents opens and closes an incident, and /agent/heartbeat reports the baseline. Each request has a timeout of 10 seconds. After 5 failures Ze stops posting for 60 seconds, then tries again.
  - **api-key** `string`: Flowtriq API bearer token.
    Ze sends the value in the Authorization header of each request, as a Bearer token. The length is 1 to 512 characters. The leaf is required when enabled is true, and Ze refuses the config without it. The leaf is marked sensitive, so every display path prints a placeholder in place of the token. A $9$-encoded value written by hand is decoded on read. Ze does not encode it for you, so a token typed into the editor is written to the config file as you typed it.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable reporting DDoS incidents to the Flowtriq cloud API.
    false is the default, and the reporter then posts nothing. true makes api-key and node-uuid required, and Ze refuses the config when either one is empty. The reporter answers an attack with one HTTP POST, and it stops no traffic.
  - **node-uuid** `string`: Node UUID for Flowtriq agent identification.
    Ze sends the value in the X-Node-UUID header of each request, which is how the service tells this router from another. The length is 1 to 128 characters. The leaf is required when enabled is true.
- **local** `container`: Answer a detected attack with a firewall rule on this router.
  *Provided by `ddos-local` ([ze-ddos-local-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ddos/local/yang/ze-ddos-local-conf.yang))*
  The rule drops the traffic where it arrives, so the link into this router still carries the attack. Announce a FlowSpec rule instead to have it dropped upstream.
  - **confidence-min** `uint8`: Minimum incident confidence, from 0 to 100, to install a drop rule.
    Ze installs a drop rule from a characterized attack only when the confidence of the incident reaches this value. The default is 0, which disables the check. A higher value stops mitigation on a borderline detection.
  - **forward-mitigation** `boolean`: Drop the traffic of a remote transit victim on the netfilter FORWARD hook.
    The default is false. The responder then guards only a local victim, one the box owns, on the netfilter INPUT hook. The responder leaves a remote victim to the flowspec upstream announce. Set this leaf to true to protect a downstream host as well. The ddos/detect policy makes the exempt decision and the mitigate decision.
  - **max-mitigation-duration** `uint32`: Maximum seconds a drop rule stays installed (0 = no cap).
    A drop rule that reaches this age is removed, and the plugin checks the age once a second. The clock starts when the rule goes in and a narrowing of the same rule does not restart it. The cap is the second removal trigger: the first is the AttackCleared event, and the cap is what bounds a rule when that event never arrives. Set the leaf to 0 for no cap, and the rule then stays until the attack clears. The leaf of the same name under ddos flowspec caps the upstream announce in the same way.
  - **response-level** `enumeration`: Action on attack detection: alert (log only) or enforce (install drop rule).
    alert is the default. The responder then logs the rule it would install, and installs nothing. enforce is the value that puts a drop rule in nftables, on a base chain at priority -200. The traffic policy of ddos/detect can still exempt a target from the action.
    - `alert`: Log the drop rule the responder would install, and install nothing.
    - `enforce`: Install the drop rule in nftables.
- **observe** `container`: Keep a ring of recent incidents for an operator to read back.
  *Provided by `ddos-observe` ([ze-ddos-observe-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ddos/observe/yang/ze-ddos-observe-conf.yang))*
  The ring is bounded and in memory, so it holds recent incidents and not a history, and a restart empties it.
  - **incident-ring-size** `uint32`: Maximum number of incidents to retain in memory.
    The ring holds this many incidents. A new incident past the bound deletes the oldest closed one. When every incident in the ring is still open, the oldest open one is deleted instead. 1000 is the default, and the range is 1 to 100000.
  - **stale-incident-timeout** `uint32`: Seconds before an open incident without a clear event is auto-finalized.
    The value reaches the incident store as its stale timeout, and no worker of ddos observe applies that timeout. The store closes an incident on the AttackCleared event that matches it. An incident that gets no clear event stays open until incident-ring-size evicts it. The default is 3600 seconds and the range is 1 to 86400. A value other than the default changes no behavior.

## environment

*Provided by `bgp-bmp` ([ze-bmp-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/bgp/plugins/bmp/yang/ze-bmp-cmd.yang), [ze-bmp-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/bgp/plugins/bmp/yang/ze-bmp-conf.yang)); `ntp` ([ze-ntp-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ntp/yang/ze-ntp-cmd.yang), [ze-ntp-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ntp/yang/ze-ntp-conf.yang))*

Environment settings for API transports

The api-server container under it is the shared parent of the REST and gRPC transports. ze-rest-conf and ze-grpc-conf merge their rest and grpc containers into it, so a transport compiled out leaves no container to configure.

- **api-server** `container`: API engine settings (shared parent for the REST/gRPC transports)
  The token leaf here is shared by both transports. Each transport starts only when its own enabled leaf is true, or when ze.api-server.rest.enabled or ze.api-server.grpc.enabled starts it. Ze parses the addresses, the CORS origin and the TLS pair even when the transport stays off.
  - **grpc** `container`: gRPC API transport. Authenticated non-loopback listeners require tls-cert and tls-key.
    A listen address that is not loopback must carry authentication and TLS, and Ze refuses to start the server without them. Without TLS the bearer token that gates each call crosses the network in clear. Ze accepts TLS 1.2 as its lowest version.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable gRPC API server
      The default is false, so config starts no gRPC listener until the leaf is true. The environment variable ze.api-server.grpc.enabled starts the transport with no leaf written. Ze parses the addresses and the TLS pair even when the transport stays off.
    - **server <name>** `list`: gRPC API listen endpoints
      The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation collects each endpoint and refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and address. An empty list still binds one endpoint, 0.0.0.0 port 50051, from the refine defaults under it.
      - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
        The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
      - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
        The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
    - **tls-cert** `string`: Path to TLS certificate file for gRPC
      Write tls-cert and tls-key together. Ze refuses to start the server when one of the two is written and the other is not. Ze reads the pair from disk at start, so a path that names no file stops the server with an error.
    - **tls-key** `string`: Path to TLS private key file for gRPC
      The leaf names the file that holds the private key of tls-cert, and Ze reads the two together at start. Ze marks the leaf ze:sensitive, so ze config dump prints the value $9$-encoded.
  - **rest** `container`: REST and HTTP transport for the API server.
    A plain HTTP listener is restricted to loopback. To reach the API from another host, put a TLS terminator in front of the listener.
    - **cors-origin** `string`: CORS allowed origin (empty disables CORS headers)
      Ze copies the value into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header of each API answer, and validates nothing in it. An empty leaf sends no CORS header, and a preflight request then gets 204 with no header. A preflight answer permits GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS, permits the Authorization and Content-Type headers, and holds for 86400 seconds.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable REST API server
      The default is false, so config starts no REST listener until the leaf is true. The environment variable ze.api-server.rest.enabled starts the transport with no leaf written. Ze parses the addresses and the CORS origin even when the transport stays off.
    - **server <name>** `list`: REST API listen endpoints
      The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation collects each endpoint and refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and address. An empty list still binds one endpoint, 0.0.0.0 port 8081, from the refine defaults under it.
      - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
        The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
      - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
        The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **token** `string`: Bearer token for API authentication.
    When the token is set, a client MUST send the header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Leave the leaf empty to allow unauthenticated access.
- **bgp** `container`: BGP protocol environment settings, applied before any peer-level config.
  The container controls the OPEN wait timeout and the initial announce delay.
  - **announce-delay** `string`: Delay between reactor Ready and first UPDATE (duration, 0s-1h)
    The environment variable ze.bgp.announce.delay overrides the leaf. Ze holds every peer start for the delay after the reactor is otherwise Ready, which staggers route emission over a restart.
  - **openwait** `int32`: Seconds to wait for peer OPEN after TCP connect
    The environment variable ze.bgp.openwait overrides the leaf. Ze arms the hold timer with the value after it sends OPEN. Ze resets that timer to the negotiated hold time when the peer OPEN arrives.
- **bmp** `container`: BMP receiver settings
  The receiver starts only when enabled is true and the server list holds one entry at least. Ze stores each Route Monitoring message it accepts in the BMP RIB, and show bmp rib reads that RIB.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable BMP receiver
    The default is false. The receiver needs this leaf true and one server entry at least, so enabled true on its own binds no address.
  - **max-sessions** `uint16`: Maximum concurrent BMP sessions
    The default is 100 and the range is 1 to 1000. The count is per listener, so two server entries admit twice this number of sessions. Over the limit Ze closes the new connection and logs a warning, and the sessions already open keep running.
  - **route-action** `enumeration`: Action for received BMP Route Monitoring messages
    monitor is the default and is the only action Ze performs. redistribute is accepted by the schema and is not implemented: Ze writes a warning in the log and acts as monitor. Under monitor the routes of a BMP Route Monitoring message go to the BMP RIB, which show bmp rib reads. They reach neither BGP best-path selection nor the FIB.
    - `monitor`: Store in BMP RIB for visibility (show bmp rib), isolated from BGP best-path and FIB
    - `redistribute`: Store in BMP RIB and redistribute into BGP best-path selection
  - **server <name>** `list`: BMP receiver listen endpoints
    The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and address. Ze opens one TCP listener for each entry. A bind that fails is logged, and the other entries keep their listener. An empty list binds nothing, because the receiver has no default endpoint.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
- **chaos** `container`: Chaos fault injection settings
  Ze wraps the clock, the dialer and the listener factory with a fault injector while seed is not 0. The block exists to test Ze against slow timers and failed connections. A production config leaves the block out.
  - **rate** `string`: Fault probability per operation (0.0-1.0)
    0.1 injects a fault into one operation in ten. Ze uses 0.1 for a value that is not a number, and for a value outside 0.0 to 1.0. The leaf does nothing while seed is 0.
  - **seed** `int64`: PRNG seed (0 = disabled)
    Ze builds the fault injector only while the seed is not 0. The same seed replays the same sequence of faults, so a failed run can be repeated. A seed of -1 takes the seed from the clock, and Ze logs the value it took. Ze applies the ze command line after the config load, so a seed given there replaces the seed in this leaf.
- **cli** `container`: CLI session settings
  The container holds the default output format and the transcript switch. Both leaves apply to every CLI session this daemon serves.
  - **format** `container`: Default output format settings
    The container holds the default leaf alone. A session overrides it with set cli format, which changes that one session and no other.
    - **default** `enumeration`: Default output format when no pipe operator is specified
      text writes space-aligned columns, table draws a box around them, json pretty-prints, yaml writes YAML, and ndjson writes one JSON object on each line. A format operator on the command line, such as | json, wins over this leaf, and so does set cli format. Ze falls back to text for a value it does not know.
      - `json`: JSON output (pretty-printed)
      - `ndjson`: Newline-delimited JSON (one object per line)
      - `table`: Nushell-style table with box-drawing characters
      - `text`: Space-aligned columns without box-drawing
      - `yaml`: YAML output
  - **transcript** `enumeration`: CLI session transcript recording to $XDG_DATA_HOME/ze/transcripts/
    enabled writes one file for each session, named transcript-DATE-TIME-PID.log, with mode 0600 in a directory with mode 0700. Each entry holds the time, the command with its pipe operators, and the answer. Ze writes under $HOME/.local/share while XDG_DATA_HOME is unset, and it reports a directory it cannot create on stderr.
    - `disabled`: No transcript recording
    - `enabled`: Record CLI session commands and output to local transcript file
- **daemon** `container`: Daemon settings
  The container holds the path of the PID file and the user Ze changes to. Ze reads both leaves at startup, in that order, and neither one changes a running daemon.
  - **pid** `string`: PID file path
    Ze writes its own process ID to this path at startup and removes the file at a clean shutdown. The create refuses an existing file, so a second daemon that names the same path stops at startup with an error. When the user leaf is also set, Ze gives the file to that user, because the shutdown path runs after the change of user. Ze writes no PID file while the leaf is absent.
  - **user** `string`: System user for privilege drop
    Ze starts as root to bind port 179, then changes to this user before it starts a plugin or accepts a connection. A user name and a numeric UID are both accepted, and the user's primary group is used. Ze keeps root while the leaf is absent.
- **exabgp** `container`: ExaBGP compatibility settings for the migration bridge
  The bridge runs an unchanged ExaBGP API program against Ze, and the container holds the settings of the channel to that program.
  - **api** `container`: ExaBGP bridge API settings
    The container holds the ack leaf alone. The bridge reads the leaf once, when it starts, so a change reaches the bridge at the next daemon start.
    - **ack** `boolean`: Emit done/error ack lines on plugin stdin after each dispatched command
      true matches ExaBGP, and it lets the program wait for done before it sends the next command. false keeps the bridge silent, and a program that waits for done then stops. The bridge reads false, 0, no, off, disable and disabled as false, and every other value as true.
- **gnmi** `container`: Settings of the gNMI server.
  gNMI is the gRPC Network Management Interface. The Ze gNMI server answers Get, Set, Subscribe and Capabilities over gRPC.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Start the gNMI server.
    The default is false, so Ze opens no gNMI listener until this leaf is true.
  - **server <name>** `list`: Listen endpoints of the gNMI server.
    Each entry binds one address and one port. The address defaults to 0.0.0.0 and the port defaults to 9339.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **tls** `container`: TLS certificate of the gNMI gRPC transport.
    The container holds the certificate file and the private-key file that the gRPC transport presents to a client.
    - **cert** `string`: Path to the PEM-encoded certificate file.
      The file CAN hold one certificate or a chain of them.
    - **key** `string`: Path to the PEM-encoded private-key file.
      The key belongs to the certificate that the cert leaf names.
  - **token** `string`: Bearer token that authenticates a gNMI client.
    Ze hashes the token with sha256 and compares the hash through subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, so the comparison takes constant time. An empty token means that the gNMI server does no authentication.
- **hide-version** `boolean`: Hide the X-Ze-Version banner on every HTTP response (ze.hide-version)
  The web interface and the looking glass both stamp X-Ze-Version on a response. The banner gives the release, the git commit, the Go version and the OS, which tells a client the exact build it speaks to. With true, neither server sends the header, and no other header changes. The default false keeps the banner, so a tool that reads it continues to operate. Ze reads the leaf at startup, so a new value applies at the next daemon start.
- **l2tp** `container`: L2TP listener endpoints
  The container holds the UDP endpoints the L2TP subsystem listens on, and nothing about a tunnel. A change to an endpoint is restart-only. The reload logs that it ignored the change and asks for a restart, and Ze keeps the socket it holds.
  - **server <name>** `list`: L2TP server listen endpoints (UDP)
    Each entry is one UDP socket Ze binds for L2TPv2, and RFC 2661 assigns port 1701. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port where their addresses overlap. `ze doctor` tries to bind each entry and names the one the host refuses.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
- **log** `container`: Logging settings
  A name this container does not declare becomes a subsystem level: bgp.routes debug sets the level of the bgp.routes subsystem alone. Ze reads a subsystem level from the longest matching name to the shortest, so bgp covers bgp.fsm until bgp.fsm is set too.
  - **backend** `enumeration`: Log output backend (default: stderr)
    syslog reads the destination leaf for its address, and it is the one value that does not write to a file descriptor. Ze writes to stderr when the syslog dial fails, and also while the leaf is absent.
    - `stderr`: Standard error output
    - `stdout`: Standard output
    - `syslog`: Syslog daemon
  - **color** `boolean`: Force color log output on (true) or off (false). When unset, auto-detected from terminal.
    NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb win over this leaf, and each one removes color whatever the leaf holds. While neither is set and the leaf is absent, Ze writes color only when the log writer is a terminal.
  - **destination** `string`: Syslog address used when backend is syslog: empty, a socket path, or host:port
    An empty value reaches the local syslog daemon. A value that starts with / names a Unix socket. Any other value is a UDP address, so 127.0.0.1:514 sends to a collector on this host. Ze writes to stderr when the dial fails. The crash log reads the same address, and it reads it once at startup.
  - **level** `string`: Base log level for all subsystems: disabled, debug, info, warn, or err (case-insensitive)
    warn is the level Ze uses while no config leaf and no environment variable set one. warning, error and err name the same two levels, and disabled silences every subsystem. Ze refuses any other word with a warning on stderr and keeps the level it already has. A subsystem name written beside this leaf overrides it for that subsystem alone.
  - **relay** `string`: Plugin stderr relay level: disabled, debug, info, warn, or err (case-insensitive)
    A plugin runs as its own process and writes to its own stderr. Ze relays a line at this level or above into its own log, and drops the rest. warn is the level Ze uses while the leaf is absent, and disabled silences a plugin's stderr completely.
- **looking-glass** `container`: Looking glass HTTP server settings.
  The container holds the enable switch, the listen endpoints, the TLS switch and the bearer token.
  - **certificate** `string`: PKI store certificate served on the looking-glass listener (ze.looking-glass.certificate).
    The listener sends the leaf certificate and every intermediate certificate the store entry holds, so a client can build the full chain. When this leaf is not set, ze generates a self-signed certificate and serves that. If the store holds no entry with that name, or the entry holds no private key, ze exits with an error and rejects a reload. ze never falls back to a self-signed certificate for a configured name. A named certificate needs no blob storage, because the material comes from the pki container. Environment variable: ze.looking-glass.certificate.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the looking glass.
    The looking glass does not start while this leaf is false, and false is the default.
  - **server <name>** `list`: Looking glass listen endpoints.
    Each entry names one listen endpoint. The default endpoint is 0.0.0.0 on port 8443.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **tls** `boolean`: Enable TLS. Override with the ze.looking-glass.tls variable.
    TLS needs blob storage for the certificates. The default true holds because the looking glass binds 0.0.0.0 and publishes route data. Set it to false to serve plaintext, for example when a proxy in front of Ze serves TLS.
  - **token** `string`: Bearer token checked on every /api/ and /lg/ route (ze.looking-glass.token).
    Ze compares the token in constant time, with sha256 and subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. An empty token leaves the looking glass open, and that is the default: a looking glass is a public read-only surface.
- **mcp** `container`: Settings of the MCP server.
  MCP is the Model Context Protocol. The Ze MCP server is the interface an AI assistant uses to read state from Ze and to control it.
  - **auth-mode** `enumeration`: Authentication strategy for the MCP server.
    In oauth mode, Ze validates a token locally against the JWKS of the configured authorization server. If the token leaf is set and the auth-mode leaf is absent, Ze infers 'bearer' for backward compatibility. In every other case the default is 'none'. bearer is the legacy mode, which reads one shared token from the token leaf. bearer-list replaces it: each entry of the identity list names one principal and carries its own token.
    - `bearer`: One shared bearer token, read from the token leaf.
    - `bearer-list`: One bearer token for each entry of the identity list.
    - `none`: No authentication, permitted on a loopback bind only.
    - `oauth`: OAuth 2.1 resource server.
  - **bind-remote** `boolean`: Allow the MCP server to bind to a non-loopback address.
    The default is false, which keeps the Phase 1 clamp. That clamp forces every server entry to 127.0.0.1. When this leaf is true, Ze honors the ip the operator configured, and auth-mode MUST be set to a value other than 'none'. The verify step rejects a config that does not meet that condition.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Start the MCP server.
    The default is false, so Ze opens no MCP listener until this leaf is true.
  - **identity <name>** `list`: Per-identity bearer entries, for auth-mode=bearer-list.
    The token of each entry grants access to the named principal. Authentication runs on every request, so the name and the scopes of the matching entry ride that one authenticated request. A change takes effect on the next request.
    - **scope** `string[]`: Scopes Ze carries on a request this identity authenticates.
      This leaf-list is optional. An empty leaf-list carries no scope.
    - **token** `string`: Bearer token value of this identity.
      Ze compares the token in constant time, so the duration of a comparison tells an attacker nothing about the value.
  - **oauth** `container`: OAuth 2.1 resource-server settings, for auth-mode=oauth.
    Ze does not run an authorization server. Ze validates a bearer token that the external authorization server issued.
    - **audience** `string`: Canonical URL that identifies this MCP endpoint (RFC 8707).
      Ze rejects a token whose 'aud' claim does not match this URL. Set this leaf explicitly. Ze never derives the value from the Host header of the request.
    - **authorization-server** `string`: HTTPS URL of the authorization server.
      The resource server reads the metadata of the authorization server from <url>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414), and discovers the jwks_uri there.
    - **required-scopes** `string[]`: Scopes an accepted token MUST carry.
      Ze rejects a token that does not carry every scope in this list. An empty leaf-list accepts any valid token.
  - **server <name>** `list`: Listen endpoints of the MCP server.
    Each entry binds one address and one port. The address defaults to 127.0.0.1 and the port defaults to 8080. The bind-remote leaf decides whether an address other than loopback is kept.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **tls** `container`: TLS certificate that serves the MCP endpoint over HTTPS.
    This container is required when auth-mode is oauth and a listen endpoint is not a loopback address. ze config verify rejects a config that leaves the cert leaf empty in that case, and one that sets cert without key.
    - **cert** `string`: Path to PEM-encoded certificate file (or a chain).
      Ze serves the endpoint over HTTPS only when cert and key are both set, and over HTTP when one of the two is empty. Ze reads the pair at start and accepts TLS 1.2 as its lowest version. A pair that fails to load stops the MCP server, and Ze prints the reason. ze doctor reads the file and reports it missing, or near its expiry date.
    - **key** `string`: Path to PEM-encoded private-key file.
      Ze refuses a key file that group or other can read, and refuses a symbolic link, when it runs as a user other than root. The MCP server does not start in that case. Under root Ze reads the file whatever its mode, because root reads every file anyway.
  - **token** `string`: Bearer token for auth-mode=bearer.
    When this leaf is set and no auth-mode leaf is present, Ze infers auth-mode 'bearer'. Leave this leaf empty for bearer-list mode and for oauth mode.
- **ntp** `container`: Settings of the NTP client.
  The presence of these settings does not start the client. Set the enabled leaf to true.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Synchronize the system clock with an NTP server.
    The default is false, so Ze leaves the system clock alone until this leaf is true.
