The default 254 ranks a learned default below a static default and below a protocol-learned one, the way rib distance ranks connected 0, static 10 and ebgp 20. Write 0 to put a learned default on the kernel metric that an operator's static default also uses. The two then share one kernel route, and the last writer owns it. A value above 0 also makes ze own the IPv6 default routes of the interface: ze sets accept_ra_defrtr=0 and installs the ::/0 routes itself.
    - **sysctl-profile** `node-name[]`: Named sysctl profiles to apply to this unit.
      The built-in profiles are dsr, router, hardened, multihomed and proxy. A user-defined profile comes from a sysctl { profile ... } config block. Ze applies the profiles in order, and the last one wins on a key that two profiles both set.
    - **vlan-id** `uint16`: VLAN identifier
      The range is 1 to 4094, which is what IEEE 802.1Q allows. Ze creates a kernel 802.1Q subinterface named <parent>.<vlan-id>. An L3 tunnel refuses a unit that carries this leaf, because only gretap and ip6gretap carry Ethernet frames.
    - **vrf** `string`: Not implemented. Ze refuses a config that sets this leaf.
      Ze creates no VRF device and enslaves no interface, so a unit cannot use a routing table other than the main table. The leaf stays in the schema so that the refusal can say why. It becomes functional when VRF support ships.

## isis

*Provided by `isis` ([ze-isis-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/isis/yang/ze-isis-cmd.yang), [ze-isis-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/isis/yang/ze-isis-conf.yang))*

IS-IS routing instance configuration.

The presence of this container starts the IS-IS component. At least one `net` leaf MUST be set for the engine to run. A commit with no net is accepted, and the engine then stays idle, opens no circuit and originates no LSP.

- **hostname** `string`: Dynamic hostname this IS-IS instance advertises (RFC 5301 section 3).
  Dynamic hostname to advertise (RFC 5301 section 3). Printable 7-bit ASCII only, from space (0x20) to tilde (0x7e). Each dot-separated label is 1 to 63 octets and the whole name is at most 255 octets, including the separators (RFC 2181 section 11). One trailing dot is permitted. A non-ASCII name is refused, not converted.
- **interfaces** `container`: IS-IS-enabled interfaces.
  Only an interface with an entry here runs IS-IS. Ze opens no circuit on an interface that this list omits, so no adjacency forms on it and its connected prefixes reach no LSP.
  - **interface <name>** `list`: Per-interface IS-IS configuration.
    Ze opens one circuit for each entry that is enabled and not passive. A link that comes up after start opens its circuit at that moment, and a link that goes down closes it. The connected prefixes of an enabled entry become TLV 135 and TLV 236 reachability in the node's own LSP.
    - **address-family <af>** `list`: Per-interface address families on this circuit (single-topology; both ride the shared SPF tree).
      Ze reads this list for one decision: does the circuit carry IPv6. An ipv6-unicast entry adds the IPv6 NLPID to TLV 129 and makes the hello carry TLV 232. TLV 129 carries the IPv4 NLPID on every circuit. Both families ride one SPF tree, because this IS-IS is single-topology.
    - **circuit-type** `enumeration`: Circuit type.
      broadcast, the default, runs the DIS election and sources a pseudo-node LSP when this IS wins. It advertises the LAN as one TLV 22 entry that points at the pseudo-node. It also sources a periodic CSNP while this IS is DIS. point-to-point runs no election and no pseudo-node. It sends a point-to-point hello with TLV 240 and one initial CSNP when the adjacency reaches Up.
      - `broadcast`: LAN broadcast circuit (DIS election).
      - `point-to-point`: Point-to-point circuit.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: IS-IS enabled on this interface.
      The default is true, so an entry runs IS-IS without this leaf. A false value keeps the entry in the configuration and opens no circuit. It also stops the connected prefixes of the interface from reaching the node's own LSP, which a passive interface still advertises.
    - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval.
      Ze sends an IIH on this circuit at this period. The IIH carries a holding time of this value multiplied by `hold-multiplier`, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. A neighbor drops the adjacency when no IIH arrives inside the holding time it was told. A shorter interval detects a dead neighbor faster and costs more packets on the link. `level-1/hello-interval` and `level-2/hello-interval` replace it at one level.
    - **hold-multiplier** `uint8`: Hold time = hello-interval * hold-multiplier.
      Ze advertises `hello-interval` multiplied by this value as the holding time in each IIH, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. The default of 3 lets two hellos be lost before a neighbor drops the adjacency. The clamp means that no configuration can advertise a holding time of 0, which would time the adjacency out at once. `level-1/hold-multiplier` and `level-2/hold-multiplier` replace it at one level.
    - **level** `enumeration`: Per-interface level override.
      This narrows the instance `level` for one circuit. l1 forms only a Level-1 adjacency on the circuit, l2 only a Level-2 adjacency, and l1-l2 forms both. The circuit floods LSPs and advertises its reachability only at the levels it forms. A level the instance `level` does not hold stays off whatever this leaf says.
      - `l1`: Form only a Level-1 adjacency on this circuit.
      - `l1-l2`: Form both adjacencies on this circuit, the default.
      - `l2`: Form only a Level-2 adjacency on this circuit.
    - **level-1** `container`: Level-1 per-interface overrides.
      The leaves here replace the circuit-wide value for Level-1 only. One circuit can then carry a different cost, a different DIS preference, a different Hello period or a different holding time at each level. A leaf that is not set keeps the circuit-wide value. A circuit that does not form Level-1 ignores the whole container.
      - **auth-key-chain** `string`: L1 per-interface (IIH) key-chain reference.
        The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies the Level-1 IIH on this circuit with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'IS-IS Hello PDUs SHALL use the Link Level Authentication String'. This leaf covers the hello only. The LSP, CSNP and PSNP take the chain that `isis/level-1/auth-key-chain` names.
      - **hello-interval** `uint16`: L1 hello-interval override.
        Ze sends the Level-1 IIH at this period, in place of the circuit-wide `hello-interval`. A broadcast circuit runs one Hello timer for each level it forms, because the Level-1 and the Level-2 LAN IIH are separate PDUs sent to separate multicast groups. A point-to-point circuit sends one IIH that serves both levels, so it runs one Hello timer, and that timer takes this pair whenever the circuit forms Level-1. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
      - **hold-multiplier** `uint8`: L1 hold-multiplier override.
        Ze multiplies the Level-1 hello interval by this value and advertises the product as the holding time in each Level-1 IIH, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. It replaces the circuit-wide `hold-multiplier` for Level-1. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
      - **metric** `uint32`: L1 wide metric override.
        Ze advertises this cost for the circuit in the Level-1 LSP, in place of `metric`. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide metric. The value also becomes the metric of the connected prefixes the circuit contributes at Level-1.
      - **priority** `uint8`: L1 DIS priority override.
        Ze uses this priority in the Level-1 DIS election, in place of `priority`. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide priority, and so does the value 0: Ze reads an override only when it is more than 0. To ask for the lowest preference, set the circuit-wide `priority` to 0.
    - **level-2** `container`: Level-2 per-interface overrides.
      The leaves here replace the circuit-wide value for Level-2 only. One circuit can then carry a different cost, a different DIS preference, a different Hello period or a different holding time at each level. A leaf that is not set keeps the circuit-wide value. A circuit that does not form Level-2 ignores the whole container.
      - **auth-key-chain** `string`: L2 per-interface (IIH) key-chain reference.
        The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies the Level-2 IIH on this circuit with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'IS-IS Hello PDUs SHALL use the Link Level Authentication String'. This leaf covers the hello only. The LSP, CSNP and PSNP take the chain that `isis/level-2/auth-key-chain` names.
      - **hello-interval** `uint16`: L2 hello-interval override.
        Ze sends the Level-2 IIH at this period, in place of the circuit-wide `hello-interval`. A broadcast circuit runs one Hello timer for each level it forms, because the Level-1 and the Level-2 LAN IIH are separate PDUs sent to separate multicast groups. A point-to-point circuit sends one IIH that serves both levels, so it runs one Hello timer, and that timer takes this pair only on a circuit that forms Level-2 alone. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
      - **hold-multiplier** `uint8`: L2 hold-multiplier override.
        Ze multiplies the Level-2 hello interval by this value and advertises the product as the holding time in each Level-2 IIH, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. It replaces the circuit-wide `hold-multiplier` for Level-2. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
      - **metric** `uint32`: L2 wide metric override.
        Ze advertises this cost for the circuit in the Level-2 LSP, in place of `metric`. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide metric. The value also becomes the metric of the connected prefixes the circuit contributes at Level-2.
      - **priority** `uint8`: L2 DIS priority override.
        Ze uses this priority in the Level-2 DIS election, in place of `priority`. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide priority, and so does the value 0: Ze reads an override only when it is more than 0. To ask for the lowest preference, set the circuit-wide `priority` to 0.
    - **metric** `uint32`: Wide metric (RFC 5305).
      The circuit advertises this cost in TLV 22, and its connected prefixes advertise it in TLV 135 and TLV 236. RFC 5305 section 3 states that 'The metric octets are encoded as a 24-bit unsigned integer', which is the 1 to 16777215 range here. SPF adds the value once for each hop, so a lower value makes the circuit preferred. `level-1/metric` and `level-2/metric` replace it at one level.
    - **passive** `boolean`: Advertise the interface but form no adjacencies.
      Ze opens no circuit for a passive interface, so it sends no hello and forms no adjacency. The connected prefixes of the interface still become TLV 135 and TLV 236 entries in the node's own LSP, at the metric `metric` sets. Use it on a loopback and on a customer LAN, where the prefix MUST be reachable and no IS-IS neighbor exists.
    - **priority** `uint8`: DIS election priority (broadcast circuits).
      The value rides in each LAN hello and decides the DIS election on a broadcast circuit. The highest priority wins, and the highest SNPA MAC address breaks a tie. A priority of 0 is valid and only lowers the preference, so it does not stop this IS from winning an election it is alone in. The leaf changes nothing on a point-to-point circuit.
- **key-chains <name>** `list`: Named authentication key chains for hitless key rotation.
  A chain holds the keys that sign and verify IS-IS PDUs. Ze authenticates nothing until an `auth-key-chain` leaf names the chain. A key whose algorithm token Ze does not know, or whose secret does not decode, is dropped from the chain and signs nothing.
  - **key <key-id>** `list`: Keys in this chain.
    Ze reads the keys in configuration order, which is key-id order. The first key whose send lifetime holds the current time signs a PDU. Every key whose accept lifetime holds that time is accepted on receive, up to 16 keys, which is what makes a rotation lose no adjacency.
    - **accept-lifetime** `container`: When this key is accepted on receive (hitless rotation).
      Ze accepts a received PDU signed with any key whose accept window holds the current time, up to 16 keys in one chain. Open the accept window of the new key before its send window. Every neighbor then accepts the new key before any of them signs with it.
      - **end** `string`: RFC3339 end timestamp.
        The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the end open. Keep the accept window of the old key open until every neighbor signs with the new key.
      - **start** `string`: RFC3339 start timestamp.
        The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the start open, so the key is accepted from the moment it is committed. A value Ze cannot parse also leaves the start open.
    - **algorithm** `enumeration`: Authentication algorithm.
      cleartext sends the secret in the PDU as auth type 1, so it detects a misconfiguration and stops no attacker. hmac-md5, the default, is auth type 54 (RFC 5304). The five SHA choices are auth type 3 (RFC 5310) and range from HMAC-SHA-1 to HMAC-SHA-512. Ze drops a key whose token it does not know, so a typo here leaves that key out of the chain.
      - `cleartext`: Cleartext password (auth type 1).
      - `hmac-md5`: HMAC-MD5 (auth type 54, RFC 5304).
      - `hmac-sha-1`: HMAC-SHA-1 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).
      - `hmac-sha-224`: HMAC-SHA-224 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).
      - `hmac-sha-256`: HMAC-SHA-256 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).
      - `hmac-sha-384`: HMAC-SHA-384 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).
      - `hmac-sha-512`: HMAC-SHA-512 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).
    - **secret** `string`: Shared secret, masked and $9$-encoded at rest.
      The commit encodes the value with the reversible $9$ encoding, the same one PPPoE and WireGuard use, and the configuration output masks it. Ze decodes it in memory to derive the HMAC key. A value that does not decode drops the key from the chain. Both ends of an adjacency MUST hold the same plaintext secret under the same key-id.
    - **send-lifetime** `container`: When this key may be used to sign (hitless rotation).
      Ze signs with the first key in the chain whose send window holds the current time. A key with no send-lifetime signs from the moment it is committed. When no key in the chain has an open send window, Ze sends the PDU unsigned, and a neighbor under authentication rejects it.
      - **end** `string`: RFC3339 end timestamp.
        The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the end open, so the key signs forever. Set the end of the old key after the start of the new one, so the two windows overlap and the rotation loses no adjacency.
      - **start** `string`: RFC3339 start timestamp.
        The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the start open. A value Ze cannot parse also leaves the start open, and it does not drop the key.
- **level** `enumeration`: Routing level of this Intermediate System.
  l1 holds only the Level-1 database and keeps this IS inside its own area. l2 holds only the Level-2 database and makes this IS a backbone router. l1-l2, the default, holds both databases and originates one LSP set at each level. A circuit forms an adjacency only at a level this leaf keeps.
  - `l1`: Level-1 (intra-area) only.
  - `l1-l2`: Both Level-1 and Level-2.
  - `l2`: Level-2 (backbone) only.
- **level-1** `container`: Level-1 (area) per-level configuration.
  The leaves here apply to Level-1 across the whole instance, and not to one circuit. RFC 5304 section 2 calls the key they select the Area Authentication string.
  - **auth-key-chain** `string`: L1 per-level (LSP/SNP, area key) key-chain reference.
    The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies every Level-1 LSP, CSNP and PSNP with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'Level 1 Sequence Number PDUs SHALL use the Area Authentication string as in Level 1 Link State PDUs'. The IIH is separate and takes the per-interface chain.
- **level-2** `container`: Level-2 (domain) per-level configuration.
  The leaves here apply to Level-2 across the whole instance, and not to one circuit. RFC 5304 section 2 calls the key they select the domain authentication string.
  - **auth-key-chain** `string`: L2 per-level (LSP/SNP, domain key) key-chain reference.
    The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies every Level-2 LSP, CSNP and PSNP with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'Level 2 Sequence Number PDUs SHALL use the domain authentication string as in Level 2 Link State PDUs'. The IIH is separate and takes the per-interface chain.
- **lsp-lifetime** `uint16`: Maximum LSP remaining lifetime.
  The value stamps the Remaining Lifetime of every LSP this IS originates. A neighbor purges the LSP when that field reaches 0, so a refresh MUST land first. The default of 1200 seconds pairs with the 900-second refresh default. This value also bounds the refresh. A refresh of 0, or one that is not less than this value, falls back to half of it.
- **lsp-refresh-interval** `uint16`: LSP refresh interval.
  Ze re-originates its own LSP set at this period, which bumps the sequence number and resets the Remaining Lifetime to `lsp-lifetime`. Without the refresh a quiet node ages out of every neighbor's database and disappears from the topology. A value of 0, or a value that is not less than `lsp-lifetime`, falls back to half of `lsp-lifetime`. A refresh then always lands before the purge.
- **net** `string[]`: Network Entity Title(s) of this IS-IS instance, at least one.
  Network Entity Title(s), for example 49.0001.0000.0000.0001.00. At least one is required. The System ID is the 6 octets before the NSEL.
- **overload** `boolean`: Set the overload bit (RFC 3787).
  The bit goes into the type block of this node's own LSP number zero. RFC 3787 section 4 states that 'Section 7.2.8.1 of ISO 10589 instructs other systems not to use the overloaded IS as a transit router'. Ze's own SPF obeys the bit the same way. It settles an overloaded node, so the prefixes that node advertises stay reachable. It expands none of that node's links, so no path runs through the node. Set the bit to hold transit traffic away while BGP converges after a restart.
- **system-id** `string`: 6-byte System ID (xxxx.xxxx.xxxx); derived from NET if unset.
  When this leaf is not set, Ze takes the System ID from the 6 octets before the NSEL of the first `net`. When it is set, the value MUST equal that derived value. A mismatch refuses the commit with 'system-id does not match the system id derived from net'.

## kernel

*Provided by `kernel` ([ze-kernel-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/kernel/yang/ze-kernel-conf.yang))*

Kernel route redistribution. Presence enables the plugin.

The container carries no leaf, so writing it is the whole configuration. The plugin watches the kernel routing table and emits each route on the redistribute event bus. A route whose netlink protocol is RTPROT_KERNEL or RTPROT_REDIRECT is dropped, so a connected subnet route and an ICMP redirect route never reach BGP. The plugin registers the kernel route source, and a redistribute statement names that source.


## l2tp

*Provided by `l2tp-auth-local` ([ze-l2tp-auth-local-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/l2tp/plugins/authlocal/yang/ze-l2tp-auth-local-conf.yang)); `l2tp-auth-radius-servers` ([ze-l2tp-auth-radius-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/l2tp/plugins/authradius/yang/ze-l2tp-auth-radius-conf.yang)); `l2tp-pool` ([ze-l2tp-pool-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/l2tp/plugins/pool/yang/ze-l2tp-pool-conf.yang)); `l2tp-shaper` ([ze-l2tp-shaper-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/l2tp/plugins/shaper/yang/ze-l2tp-shaper-conf.yang))*

L2TPv2 tunnel subsystem settings (RFC 2661).

L2TPv2 tunnel subsystem settings (RFC 2661). Presence of this block with any content implies the subsystem is enabled. Use 'enabled false' to disable it explicitly, or 'enabled true' as a filler when no other settings are needed.

- **allow-no-auth** `boolean`: Allow PPP LCP to finish with no Auth-Protocol, false by default.
  Allow PPP LCP authentication negotiation to proceed without an Auth-Protocol. The default is false, so a peer that rejects all configured authentication methods is disconnected, instead of being accepted as no-auth.
- **auth** `container`: PPP authentication for L2TP subscriber sessions.
  The container holds the backend that answers a credential. The l2tp-auth-local plugin fills the local container under it, and the l2tp-auth-radius plugin fills the radius container. The timing of the PPP authentication phase sits under l2tp authentication instead.
  - **local** `container`: Authenticate a subscriber against users declared in this config.
    Ze rejects every session while no user is declared here, and it logs that no user is configured. A session is matched against the list by its PPP username, and an unknown username is rejected. Local authentication answers PAP and CHAP-MD5, and it rejects MS-CHAPv2.
    - **user <name>** `list`: One subscriber account, keyed by its PPP username.
      Ze looks the PPP username up in this list and rejects a username no entry carries. An empty list rejects every session. The match is exact, so user and user@example.net are two accounts.
      - **password** `string`: Shared secret for PAP cleartext and CHAP-MD5/MS-CHAPv2 challenge-response.
        PAP compares the SHA-256 of the received password with the SHA-256 of this value, in constant time. CHAP-MD5 computes MD5 over the identifier, this value and the challenge, which RFC 1994 Section 4.1 defines. CHAP needs the secret in clear, so this leaf holds no hash.
  - **radius** `container`: Authenticate and account subscriber sessions against a RADIUS server.
    Authentication and accounting are separate exchanges to the same server. A session is authorized by an Access-Accept, and the Accounting-Request packets that follow report its traffic.
    - **acct-interval** `uint16`: Accounting interim-update interval in seconds.
      RFC 2869 Section 2.1 states that a locally configured value on the NAS MUST override the value found in an Access-Accept. A leaf that is set pins the cadence of every session, and the Acct-Interim-Interval attribute (type 85) of an Access-Accept then changes nothing. This leaf has no default. An unset leaf is the absent case, and it lets each Access-Accept set the cadence of that session. A session runs at 300 seconds when neither side states an interval.
    - **attributes** `container`: Which optional RADIUS attributes Ze puts in the packets it sends.
      Ze sends every attribute it can build, which is what a billing system usually wants, so this container is empty in most deployments. It names the attributes one deployment does not want on the wire. Nothing here reaches Acct-Status-Type, Acct-Session-Id or the NAS identity: RFC 2866 Section 5.13 counts the first two as 'Exactly one instance of this attribute MUST be present', and its Note 1 requires either NAS-IP-Address or NAS-Identifier, so an Accounting-Request without them is not a conformant record and Ze offers no way to write one.
      - **exclude** `container`: Attributes Ze does not send, each with the record types it is held back from.
        Name an attribute to hold it back from every record type that would carry it. Add packet-type under it to hold it back from some record types and keep it in the others. Each attribute accepts only the record types Ze can put it in, so a line naming a record type that never carries the attribute is refused when the configuration is committed rather than ignored at run time.
        - **acct-delay-time** `container`: Do not send Acct-Delay-Time (attribute 41).
          RFC 2866 Section 5.2 reports how many seconds the client has been trying to send this record, and Ze rewrites the value on each retransmission. A record that carries no Acct-Delay-Time is replayed byte for byte instead, under the same Identifier, which is what an Access-Request does. accel-ppp ships this attribute off by default.
          - **packet-type** `enumeration[]`: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.
            Ze puts Acct-Delay-Time in the three accounting records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds the attribute back from all three.
            - `accounting-interim`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.
            - `accounting-start`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.
            - `accounting-stop`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.
        - **acct-terminate-cause** `container`: Do not send Acct-Terminate-Cause (attribute 49).
          RFC 2866 Section 5.10 states that the attribute 'can only be present in Accounting-Request records where the Acct-Status-Type is set to Stop', so the Stop record is the only one this reaches. A pipeline that keys on its own teardown signal does not need it. FreeRADIUS defaults it to NAS-Reboot in its accounting queries.
          - **packet-type** `enumeration[]`: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.
            RFC 2866 Section 5.10 admits Acct-Terminate-Cause in a Stop record alone, so accounting-stop is the one value this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds the attribute back from the Stop record, which is the same thing said with fewer words.
            - `accounting-stop`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.
        - **calling-station-id** `container`: Do not send Calling-Station-Id (attribute 31).
          RFC 2865 Section 5.31 carries the number the call came from, which is the L2TP Calling Number of the session, or the subscriber MAC address on the PPPoE relay path. Some operators do not store it. Check the server first: FreeRADIUS matches its IP pool queries on this attribute with no fallback value, so a pool it serves keeps leases that never expire once the attribute stops arriving.
          - **packet-type** `enumeration[]`: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.
            Ze puts Calling-Station-Id in the three accounting records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds the attribute back from all three.
            - `accounting-interim`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.
            - `accounting-start`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.
            - `accounting-stop`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.
        - **event-timestamp** `container`: Do not send Event-Timestamp (attribute 55).
          RFC 2869 Section 5.3 records the second at which the event happened on the NAS. A server that stamps its own receive time does not need it. FreeRADIUS falls back to the server clock in its default accounting queries, so a record without the attribute is still stored with a time.
          - **packet-type** `enumeration[]`: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.
            Ze puts Event-Timestamp in the three accounting records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds the attribute back from all three.
            - `accounting-interim`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.
            - `accounting-start`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.
            - `accounting-stop`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.
        - **framed-ip-address** `container`: Do not send Framed-IP-Address (attribute 8).
          RFC 2865 Section 5.8 reports the IPv4 address the session negotiated, and RFC 2866 Section 4.1 requires that a record which carries the attribute carries the real address. An operator whose addressing is reported by another system can hold it back. A session with no IPv4 address sends no attribute either way, which is a different case and is not configurable.
          - **packet-type** `enumeration[]`: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.
            Ze puts Framed-IP-Address in the three accounting records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds the attribute back from all three.
            - `accounting-interim`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.
            - `accounting-start`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.
            - `accounting-stop`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.
        - **nas-port-id** `container`: Do not send NAS-Port-Id (attribute 87).
          RFC 2869 Section 5.17 names the access port in text, and the nas-port-id-format leaf is the template Ze resolves for it. Clearing that leaf also sends no attribute, on every packet at once. This container is the finer instrument: it holds the attribute back from the record types you name while the template stays configured for the rest.
          - **packet-type** `enumeration[]`: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.
            Ze puts NAS-Port-Id in the Access-Request and in the three accounting records, so all four are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds the attribute back from all four.
            - `access-request`: Hold the attribute back from the Access-Request that authenticates the session.
            - `accounting-interim`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.
            - `accounting-start`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.
            - `accounting-stop`: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.
    - **coa-port** `uint16`: UDP port of the RADIUS CoA and Disconnect listener, usually 3799.
      The listener implements RFC 5176. This leaf has no default on purpose. An unset leaf keeps the listener off, so an existing deployment does not start to accept CoA on upgrade. Ze accepts a request only from a configured RADIUS server address.
    - **nas-identifier** `string`: NAS-Identifier sent in RADIUS requests.
      Ze sends this text as the NAS-Identifier attribute in each Access-Request and each Accounting-Request. RFC 2865 Section 4.1 requires either NAS-IP-Address or NAS-Identifier in an Access-Request. With this leaf empty and source-address empty, Ze sends the hostname, and the plugin name where the host carries none.
    - **nas-port-id-format** `string`: Template for the NAS-Port-Id attribute sent in RADIUS requests.
      Ze sends the NAS-Port-Id attribute (RFC 2869 Section 5.17) in an Access-Request packet and in an Accounting-Request packet. The placeholders are {nas-id}, {tunnel-id} and {session-id}. Ze copies every other character. All three values are known before the session has an interface. One session therefore sends one text in its Access-Request and in all its accounting records. A billing system can join them on it. The 253-octet limit is the largest value a RADIUS attribute can carry (RFC 2865 Section 5). The commit refuses an unknown placeholder, it refuses a {nas-id} when nas-identifier is unset, and it refuses a template whose widest resolution passes 253 octets because the nas-identifier it expands is long. An unset leaf sends no attribute.
    - **require-message-authenticator** `boolean`: Discard a CoA-Request or a Disconnect-Request that carries no Message-Authenticator.
      RFC 5176 Section 3.4 makes the Message-Authenticator attribute optional, so the default is false. Ze then processes a request without the attribute once its Request Authenticator verifies against the shared secret. Set this leaf to true when every Dynamic Authorization Client sends the attribute. The attribute is an HMAC-MD5 keyed with the shared secret, and it is the mitigation for the Blast-RADIUS class of attack (CVE-2024-3596), which forges a RADIUS UDP packet with a chosen-prefix MD5 collision against the authenticator. A client that sends no attribute gets no answer while this leaf is true.
    - **retries** `uint8`: Number of retransmit attempts per server.
      The default is 3 and the range is 1 to 10. Ze sends the request that many times to one server, then moves to the next entry of the list. An Access-Request is replayed byte for byte. An Accounting-Request gets a new identifier and a new Acct-Delay-Time on each attempt, which RFC 2866 Section 4.1 requires.
    - **server <name>** `list`: One RADIUS server Ze sends requests to, tried in the order written.
      The operator orders the list. Ze tries the first entry, and moves to the next one when that server does not answer. Write the closest server first.
      - **address** `string`: RADIUS server IP address or hostname.
        The leaf is mandatory, and Ze refuses a server entry without it. Ze joins the value to port to reach the server. The first entry of the list is the one Ze tries first, so write the closest server first.
      - **port** `uint16`: RADIUS server UDP port.
        The default is 1812 and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze sends the Access-Request packets and the Accounting-Request packets of this server to this one port, because a server entry carries no second port.
      - **shared-key** `string`: RADIUS shared secret.
        RFC 2865 Section 3 states that the secret MUST NOT be empty, that is length 0, because an empty secret makes a forged packet easy to build.
    - **source-address** `ipv4-address`: Source IPv4 address for outbound RADIUS packets.
      Ze binds the outbound RADIUS socket to this address, so every request leaves with it. Ze also sends the address as NAS-IP-Address, which is one of the two attributes RFC 2865 Section 4.1 accepts to name the NAS. With the leaf empty, the kernel picks the source address and Ze names the NAS with NAS-Identifier instead.
    - **timeout** `uint8`: Per-request timeout in seconds.
      The default is 3 seconds and the range is 1 to 30. The first attempt waits this long, and each attempt after it waits twice the wait before it. With the default of 3 seconds and 3 retries, a server that never answers costs 21 seconds before Ze tries the next server.
- **auth-method** `enumeration`: PPP Auth-Protocol method first advertised in LCP Configure-Request.
  PPP Auth-Protocol method first advertised in LCP Configure-Request. The default requires CHAP-MD5. Set the leaf to none only together with allow-no-auth true.
  - `chap-md5`: Advertise CHAP with the MD5 algorithm (RFC 1994), the default.
  - `ms-chap-v2`: Advertise MS-CHAP-V2 (RFC 2759).
  - `none`: Advertise no Auth-Protocol, so the session opens with no PPP authentication phase.
  - `pap`: Advertise PAP (RFC 1334), which carries the password in clear text.
- **authentication** `container`: PPP authentication phase settings for L2TP sessions.
  The container holds the timing of the PPP authentication phase, and nothing else. The backend that answers a credential sits under the auth container, which the l2tp-auth-local plugin and the l2tp-auth-radius plugin fill. Both leaves here hot-apply: a new value reaches the next session, and a session that is already up keeps the value it started with.
  - **reauth-interval** `uint32`: Periodic re-authentication interval in seconds, 0 by default.
    Periodic re-authentication interval in seconds, for CHAP and MS-CHAPv2 only. Zero disables re-auth. A value of 1 to 4 is rejected, to prevent re-auth storms. The default is 0, which is disabled.
  - **timeout** `uint16`: PPP auth-phase timeout in seconds, 30 by default.
    PPP auth-phase timeout in seconds. A session that does not complete authentication within this window is torn down. The default is 30 seconds.
- **cqm-enabled** `boolean`: Enable the CQM (Customer Quality Monitor) observer.
  Enable the CQM (Customer Quality Monitor) observer. When this leaf is true, Ze pre-allocates per-session event rings and per-login sample rings at subsystem start. Ze also overrides the PPP echo interval to 1s for RTT measurement.
- **enabled** `boolean`: Enable L2TP subsystem. Defaults to true when the l2tp block is present; set to false to disable.
  The l2tp block itself starts the subsystem. This leaf stops the subsystem where the block must stay, and it is filler where no other setting is needed. A change is restart-only. The reload logs that it ignored the flip and asks for a restart, and the running state stays as it is.
- **event-ring-size-per-session** `uint16`: Number of events in each per-session event ring. When full, oldest events are overwritten.
  Ze pre-allocates one ring for each session the subsystem can hold, and each ring holds this many slots. The value therefore multiplies into the memory the subsystem takes at startup. A full ring overwrites its oldest event. A session therefore keeps its most recent events and loses the older ones. A change is restart-only, and the reload logs that it ignored it.
- **hello-interval** `uint16`: Seconds of peer silence before Ze sends HELLO.
  Seconds of peer silence before sending HELLO. RFC 2661 recommends 60s. A value more than 3600, which is one hour, is rejected, because it disables keepalive.
- **hello-retries** `uint8`: Unanswered HELLO intervals tolerated before the peer is declared dead.
  Dead-peer detection threshold: consecutive unanswered HELLO keepalive intervals tolerated before an established tunnel's peer is declared dead and the tunnel is torn down. The effective detection time is hello-retries x hello-interval, measured from the last proof of peer liveness. That proof is a delivered control message, or an acknowledgement of one of our messages, including a ZLB ACK of a HELLO. A value of 0 disables dead-peer detection, and reliable-transport retransmit exhaustion, about 31s, is then the only teardown signal. The default is 2.
- **max-logins** `uint32`: Maximum concurrent PPP logins the CQM observer tracks.
  Maximum concurrent PPP logins tracked by the CQM observer. The value controls the size of the pre-allocated sample ring pool. When the maximum is exceeded, the least recently used login's data is evicted.
- **max-sessions** `uint16`: Maximum concurrent sessions per tunnel.
  Maximum concurrent sessions per tunnel. The default is a finite deployment safety cap. A value of 0 explicitly requests unbounded admission on each tunnel. A new ICRQ or OCRQ beyond a positive limit is rejected with CDN Result Code 4 (no resources).
- **max-tunnels** `uint16`: Maximum concurrent L2TP tunnels.
  Maximum concurrent L2TP tunnels. The default is a finite deployment safety cap. A value of 0 explicitly requests unbounded admission by this leaf. The 65535 ceiling imposed by RFC 2661's 16-bit Tunnel ID field still applies. A new SCCRQ beyond a positive limit is rejected with StopCCN Result Code 2.
- **ncp** `container`: NCP (Network Control Protocol) settings for L2TP sessions.
  NCP is the phase after PPP authentication, where each side negotiates one network-layer protocol. The two enable leaves choose which protocols Ze offers, and the timeout leaf bounds the phase. Each leaf hot-applies to a new session, and a session that is already up keeps what it negotiated.
  - **enable-ipcp** `boolean`: Enable the IPCP NCP (RFC 1332) for new L2TP sessions. When false, no IPv4 address is negotiated.
    IPCP (RFC 1332) is what gives the subscriber an IPv4 address. The default true offers it on each new session. Set it false and Ze sets DisableIPCP on the kernel PPP channel of a new session. That session then gets no IPv4 address, and only IPv6CP can succeed. The leaf hot-applies, and a running session keeps the address it holds.
  - **enable-ipv6cp** `boolean`: Enable the IPv6CP NCP (RFC 5072) for a new L2TP session.
    Enable the IPv6CP NCP (RFC 5072) for new L2TP sessions. When this leaf is false, no IPv6 interface identifier is negotiated.
  - **timeout** `uint16`: NCP negotiation timeout in seconds, 30 by default.
    NCP negotiation timeout in seconds. A session that does not complete NCP within this window is torn down. The default is 30 seconds.
- **pool** `container`: Address and prefix pools handed to L2TP PPP sessions.
  A pool is bitmap-backed, so an address is released when the session goes down and is handed to the next session that asks.
  - **ipv4** `container`: The IPv4 range and the DNS servers a PPP session receives.
    The gateway is the NAS-side address every session sees as its IPCP peer, and it MUST NOT fall inside the start-to-end range.
    - **dns-primary** `ipv4-address`: Primary DNS server pushed to subscribers.
      Ze offers the address as the IPCP Primary DNS option, and it offers no such option while the leaf is absent. A subscriber that asks for another address gets a Configure-Nak carrying this one. Ze drops the option from its later requests when the subscriber rejects it.
    - **dns-secondary** `ipv4-address`: Secondary DNS server pushed to subscribers.
      Ze offers the address as the IPCP Secondary DNS option, and it offers no such option while the leaf is absent. The leaf is independent of dns-primary, so a pool can name one, both, or neither.
    - **end** `ipv4-address`: Last address in the pool range (inclusive).
      The range is inclusive, so this address is handed to a session as well. Ze refuses an end before the start, and it refuses the block that names end without start. A session that arrives after the last free address is refused with pool exhausted.
    - **gateway** `ipv4-address`: NAS-side IP for all PPP sessions (IPCP local address). Must not overlap the pool range.
      Each session sees this address as its IPCP peer, so it is the next hop the subscriber routes through. Ze refuses an address that falls inside the range from start to end, and it refuses an address that is not IPv4.
    - **start** `ipv4-address`: First address in the pool range.
      Ze refuses the ipv4 block that names start without end, and it refuses a start after the end. The range is inclusive at both ends, and the bitmap holds one bit for each address in it. Ze releases an address when the session goes down, and hands it to the next session that asks.
  - **ipv6-pd** `container`: IPv6 prefix delegation pool for subscribers.
    The pool allocates one prefix of the configured length to each subscriber, taken from the configured block, for DHCPv6 prefix delegation. RFC 3633 defines that delegation.
    - **block** `string`: Prefix block to allocate from, for example 2001:db8::/32.
      Ze cuts the block into prefixes of the delegated length and hands one to each subscriber. The block must be native IPv6, so an IPv4-mapped address is refused. The delegated length can be at most 24 bits longer than the block, which bounds one pool at 16 million prefixes.
    - **delegation-length** `uint8`: Prefix length delegated to each subscriber (e.g. 56 for /56 prefixes).
      Ze cuts the block into prefixes of this length, and delegates one to each subscriber over DHCPv6 IA_PD (RFC 3633). Ze installs a route to that prefix on the PPP interface. The length is 48 to 64, and it must be at least as long as the block. It must be at most 24 bits longer than the block, which caps one pool at 16 million prefixes. The default is 56, and Ze logs a warning when the leaf is absent. A session RADIUS answers with a Delegated-IPv6-Prefix takes that prefix and reaches no pool, so this length does not apply to it.
  - **named-ipv6-pool <name>** `list`: Named IPv6 prefix pools selected by RADIUS Framed-IPv6-Pool attribute (RFC 6911 attr 100).
    The Framed-IPv6-Pool attribute RADIUS returns for a session names one of these pools. Each pool holds its own block and its own bitmap, and none of them is tied to the ipv6-pd pool. The name is the list key.
    - **block** `string`: Prefix block to allocate from, for example 2001:db8::/32.
      The leaf is required here, and the ipv6-pd pool leaves it optional. Ze refuses a block that is not native IPv6, and names the pool in the error. Ze does not compare the block of one pool against the block of another, so two blocks that overlap can delegate one prefix twice.
    - **delegation-length** `uint8`: Prefix length delegated to each subscriber.
      The leaf is required here, and the ipv6-pd pool falls back to 56 when it is absent. Each named pool cuts its own block into prefixes of its own length, so two pools can delegate different lengths. The length is 48 to 64, and it must be at least as long as the block of this pool. It must be at most 24 bits longer than that block, which caps the pool at 16 million prefixes. A session RADIUS answers with a Delegated-IPv6-Prefix takes that prefix and reaches no pool.
  - **named-pool <name>** `list`: Named IPv4 pools selected by RADIUS Framed-Pool attribute.
    The Framed-Pool attribute RADIUS returns for a session names one of these pools. Ze then uses the gateway and the DNS servers of that pool. Ze refuses the session when the attribute names a pool this list does not hold, and it does not fall back to the ipv4 pool. The ipv4 pool serves a session with no Framed-Pool.
    - **dns-primary** `ipv4-address`: Primary DNS server pushed to subscribers.
      A session RADIUS sends to this pool receives this address, and not the one the ipv4 pool holds. Ze offers no Primary DNS option while the leaf is absent, even when the ipv4 pool names one.
    - **dns-secondary** `ipv4-address`: Secondary DNS server pushed to subscribers.
      A session RADIUS sends to this pool receives this address, and not the one the ipv4 pool holds. Ze offers no Secondary DNS option while the leaf is absent, even when the ipv4 pool names one.
    - **end** `ipv4-address`: Last address in the pool range (inclusive).
      The range is inclusive, so this address is handed to a session as well. A session that arrives after the last free address of this pool is refused with pool exhausted. Ze does not move that session to another pool.
    - **gateway** `ipv4-address`: NAS-side IP for sessions using this pool.
      A session RADIUS sends to this pool sees this address as its IPCP peer, and not the gateway of the ipv4 pool. Ze refuses an address that falls inside the range from start to end of this pool.
    - **start** `ipv4-address`: First address in the pool range.
      The leaf is required here, and the ipv4 pool leaves it optional. Ze refuses a start after the end. Ze does not compare the range of one pool against the range of another. Two ranges that overlap can therefore hand one address to two sessions.
- **relay <service>** `list`: PPPoE-to-L2TP relay bindings for the LAC role.
  PPPoE-to-L2TP relay bindings (LAC role). A subscriber whose PADI or PADR carries a matching PPPoE Service-Name is relayed into an L2TP incoming call toward the named remote, instead of terminating PPP locally on this box. Removing a binding restores local termination for that service.
  - **remote** `string`: Name of the L2TP remote that matching subscribers are relayed to.
    Name of the L2TP remote (dial target) that matching subscribers are relayed to. It MUST reference a remote declared under l2tp/remote, and an unknown name is rejected at config validation.
- **remote <name>** `list`: L2TP dial targets, the remote LNS or LAC endpoints Ze dials.
  L2TP dial targets: remote LNS/LAC endpoints ze initiates tunnels toward, and sends SCCRQ to. They are referenced by name from 'request l2tp outgoing-call remote <name>' and from PPPoE relay bindings. Declaring a remote grants no dial by itself. An operator action (RPC) or a relay binding drives the dial.
  - **address** `ip-address`: Remote control-plane IP address to dial. The SCCRQ destination (RFC 2661 Section 6.1).
    Ze sends the SCCRQ to this address, with the port leaf beside it. The leaf is mandatory, so a remote without one is refused at commit. Ze parses the address and the port into one UDP endpoint when it loads the config. A value it cannot parse is refused there, and not at dial time.
  - **outgoing-calls** `boolean`: Permit LNS-side outgoing calls toward this remote, false by default.
    Permit LNS-side outgoing calls ('request l2tp outgoing-call') toward this remote. The default is false. The remote must be explicitly enabled for dial-out before an operator can place a call, so a mistyped remote name is rejected rather than dialed.
  - **port** `uint16`: Remote UDP port for the control channel, 1701 by default.
    Remote UDP port for the control channel. RFC 2661 assigns 1701, and this leaf overrides it for a non-standard peer.
  - **shared-secret** `string`: Per-remote CHAP-MD5 tunnel-authentication secret (RFC 2661).
    Per-remote CHAP-MD5 tunnel-authentication secret (RFC 2661 Section 5.1.1). It overrides the subsystem-level shared-secret for tunnels dialed to this remote. When it is empty, this dial carries no Challenge AVP. The value is masked in CLI output.
- **sample-retention-seconds** `uint32`: Duration of CQM sample retention per login, in seconds.
  Duration of CQM sample retention per login, in seconds. The duration is divided by the 100-second bucket interval to determine ring capacity. The default of 86400, which is 24 hours, gives 864 buckets.
- **shaper** `container`: Traffic shaping applied to each L2TP subscriber interface.
  Ze installs the queueing discipline and the ingress policer on the pppN interface when the session starts. The queueing discipline carries the download rate and the policer carries the upload rate. A rate changed here reaches the sessions that start after the change. A running session keeps the rate it was given, and a RADIUS CoA changes it.
  - **default-rate** `rate`: Default download rate applied to a new session.
    Default download rate applied to new sessions. The format is a number followed by a suffix, for example 10mbit or 100kbit. Ze enforces it with the queueing discipline it installs on the pppN interface, which shapes what leaves the interface toward the subscriber.
  - **qdisc-type** `enumeration`: Queueing discipline type for subscriber interfaces.
    The default is tbf, and the value reaches every subscriber interface. With tbf Ze installs one class that carries the rate of the session. With htb Ze installs one default class whose rate and ceiling are both that rate, so the class cannot borrow. Ze refuses a token that is not tbf or htb.
    - `htb`: Hierarchical Token Bucket (classful).
    - `tbf`: Token Bucket Filter (single rate limiter).
  - **upload-rate** `rate`: Default upload rate. When omitted, defaults to default-rate.
    The format is a number and a suffix, for example 5mbit, and the suffixes are bit, kbit, mbit, gbit, bps, kbps, mbps and gbps. Ze enforces it with a policer on the pppN interface ingress hook, which drops what the subscriber sends above the rate. A queueing discipline cannot carry this direction, because the ingress hook holds no queue to delay a packet into. Ze applies default-rate instead when the leaf is absent. A RADIUS Filter-Id of the form rate:20mbit/5mbit replaces both this rate and the download rate on that session, and a RADIUS CoA changes both on a running session. The 'show l2tp shaper' command reports the rate in force.
- **shared-secret** `string`: Shared secret that computes CHAP-MD5 Challenge Responses (RFC 2661).
  Shared secret used to compute CHAP-MD5 Challenge Responses (RFC 2661 Section 5.1.1, and the AVPs are defined in Section 4.4.3). When the leaf is unset and a peer sends a Challenge AVP, the subsystem rejects the tunnel with StopCCN Result Code 4 (Not Authorized). The value is masked in CLI output and cleared from the process environment after the first read.

## ldp

*Provided by `ldp-port` ([ze-ldp-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ldp/yang/ze-ldp-cmd.yang), [ze-ldp-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ldp/yang/ze-ldp-conf.yang))*

Label Distribution Protocol configuration

The engine stays idle until lsr-id carries an address, and it says so in the log. Ze then sends Hello messages to 224.0.0.2 port 646 and opens a TCP session on port 646 to each neighbor it discovers.

- **hello-hold-time** `uint16`: Hello adjacency hold time
  The default is 15 seconds, which is 3 hello intervals. Ze advertises this value in each Hello, and a neighbor drops the adjacency when no Hello arrives inside it. Keep it more than hello-interval, because a hold time under one interval drops the adjacency between two Hellos.
- **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello message interval
  The default is 5 seconds and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze sends one Hello for each interface at this period. A shorter interval finds a neighbor faster and puts more packets on the link.
- **interfaces** `string[]`: Interfaces on which LDP discovery is enabled
  Ze runs one discovery listener for each interface of this list. An empty list runs one listener that the system assigns to an interface itself. A reload starts discovery on an interface added to the list and stops it on one removed, and it leaves the other interfaces alone. The connected prefixes of these interfaces are the FECs this LSR is egress for.
- **keepalive-time** `uint16`: Session keepalive interval.
  The default is 60 seconds and the range is 1 to 65535. RFC 5036 section 3.5.3 carries the KeepAlive Time in the Common Session Parameters of the Initialization message. The receiving LSR MUST calculate the KeepAlive Timer from 'the smaller of its proposed KeepAlive Time and the KeepAlive Time received in the PDU'. The lower of the two proposals wins. Ze proposes this value to each neighbor it opens a session to. Ze sends a KeepAlive every third of the negotiated value and closes the session when no PDU arrives inside three times it. The exchange happens one time, at the start of the session, so a session that is up keeps the value it negotiated. A change here applies to the sessions that open after it.
- **lsr-id** `string`: LSR identifier (IPv4 address format)
  Ze refuses a value that is not an IP address, and stays idle while the leaf is empty. The first 4 bytes of every LDP PDU header carry this identifier. Ze also originates a label binding for the address itself, so a neighbor can reach this LSR by its identifier.
- **transport-address** `string`: Transport address for TCP sessions
  Ze advertises this address in the transport address TLV of each Hello, which is the address a neighbor connects to. Ze also binds it as the source address of the TCP connection it opens. With the leaf empty, the Hello carries no transport address TLV and the kernel picks the source address.

## mrt

*Provided by `mrt` ([ze-mrt-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/mrt/yang/ze-mrt-conf.yang))*

MRT dump configuration.

The container holds the extended-timestamp switch, the add-path switch, the peer filter, the direction, and the three dump streams.

- **add-path** `boolean`: Force add-path subtypes even when not negotiated with the peer.
  The default is false. When the leaf is true, Ze writes the ADD-PATH subtypes of RFC 8050. A BGP4MP record then carries subtype 9, and a TABLE_DUMP_V2 dump carries the ADD-PATH RIB subtypes. Ze writes the ADD-PATH subtype whether or not the session negotiated ADD-PATH, so the record declares a path identifier that the message can lack.
- **all** `container`: All BGP messages and state changes, written as BGP4MP records.
  The stream carries every BGP message: OPEN, UPDATE, NOTIFICATION, KEEPALIVE and ROUTE_REFRESH. It carries the FSM state transitions too. Ze writes them as BGP4MP records.
  - **file** `string`: Output file path, with strftime patterns for rotation.
    The strftime codes in the path decide when Ze opens a new file. The supported codes are %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day), %H (hour), %M (minute), %S (second), %s (unix timestamp) and %N (table name).
  - **interval** `uint32`: File rotation interval in seconds. Zero disables rotation.
    The value 0 keeps one file open until the daemon stops. A value of more than 0 makes Ze close the file once it has been open that many seconds. Ze then opens the next one, and the strftime codes in file give the new name. A file of - writes to standard output, which never rotates.
- **direction** `enumeration`: Which direction of BGP messages to record.
  The default is both, and both records each direction. received keeps the messages the peer sent to Ze, and sent keeps the messages Ze sent to the peer. The filter reaches the BGP messages alone, so a state change record is written whatever the value.
  - `both`: Record the BGP messages of each direction.
  - `received`: Record the BGP messages the peer sent to Ze alone.
  - `sent`: Record the BGP messages Ze sent to the peer alone.
- **extended-timestamp** `boolean`: Use BGP4MP_ET (type 17) with microsecond resolution instead of BGP4MP (type 16).
  The default is false, so each record header carries type 16, BGP4MP. RFC 6396 Section 5.3 names type 17 as BGP4MP_ET, and that header carries 4 more bytes for the microsecond field. The switch reaches all three streams at once.
- **peer-filter** `string[]`: If set, only record messages from/to these peer addresses. Empty list means record all peers.
  Ze compares each entry with the peer address of the message, so a message of another peer reaches no file. The filter reaches the BGP messages alone: Ze writes a state change record for every peer, whatever this list holds.
- **routes** `container`: Periodic RIB snapshots, written as TABLE_DUMP_V2 records.
  Each dump writes one PEER_INDEX_TABLE record, and then the RIB entries for every address family. Ze writes them as TABLE_DUMP_V2 records.
  - **file** `string`: Output file path with strftime patterns.
    The strftime codes in the path name the file Ze opens, exactly as they do in a dump stream. Ze writes this stream only when the path is set and interval is more than 0. A path of - writes to standard output.
  - **interval** `uint32`: RIB dump interval in seconds. Minimum 60.
    The default is 3600 seconds and the range is 60 to 86400. Each dump writes one PEER_INDEX_TABLE record and then the RIB entries of every address family, which RFC 6396 Section 4.3.1 requires in that order.
- **updates** `container`: BGP UPDATE message stream (BGP4MP records).
  The stream carries the UPDATE messages alone. The all stream beside it carries every message type.
  - **file** `string`: Output file path, with strftime patterns for rotation.
    The strftime codes in the path decide when Ze opens a new file. The supported codes are %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day), %H (hour), %M (minute), %S (second), %s (unix timestamp) and %N (table name).
  - **interval** `uint32`: File rotation interval in seconds. Zero disables rotation.
    The value 0 keeps one file open until the daemon stops. A value of more than 0 makes Ze close the file once it has been open that many seconds. Ze then opens the next one, and the strftime codes in file give the new name. A file of - writes to standard output, which never rotates.

## ospf

*Provided by `ospf` ([ze-ospf-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ospf/yang/ze-ospf-cmd.yang), [ze-ospf-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/ospf/yang/ze-ospf-conf.yang))*

OSPFv2 routing instance configuration.

The presence of this container starts the OSPFv2 engine, which RFC 2328 defines. The address-family container adds the OSPFv3 families of RFC 5340, and each one runs as a separate engine instance.

- **address-family** `container`: More OSPF address families.
  The IPv6 family is OSPFv3 (RFC 5340). It runs as a second engine instance over the ospfv3 transport, which uses ff02::5 and ff02::6. It shares the FSM, the flooding and the SPF machinery with the IPv4 family.
  - **ipv4-multicast** `container`: The IPv4-multicast address family over OSPFv3.
    RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the Instance ID range as 96 to 127. Ze computes reachability in the unicast shape. Ze does not implement the MOSPF tree computation.
    - **areas** `container`: OSPFv3 areas for this address family.
      RFC 5838 section 1 maps each address family to a separate Instance ID and a separate OSPFv3 instance. Ze starts one engine instance for each configured family. An area declared here belongs to that instance alone.
      - **area <area-id>** `list`: Per-area OSPFv3 configuration.
        The list is keyed by area-id. All routers in an area MUST agree on the configuration of that area. RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 states that a disagreement stops an adjacency from forming between two routers.
        - **area-type** `enumeration`: Area type.
          RFC 5340 Appendix C.2 excludes every AS-external-LSA from a stub area and from an NSSA. A router inside a stub area reaches an external destination through the default inter-area route alone. The backbone MUST NOT be a stub area or an NSSA, and a virtual link MUST NOT cross either one.
          - `normal`: Flood AS-external-LSAs into this area.
          - `nssa`: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and import external routes as Type 7 LSAs.
          - `stub`: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.
        - **virtual-link <remote-router-id>** `list`: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.
          RFC 5340 section 4.2 defines the virtual link. The link belongs to the backbone area. Its cost is the SPF path cost across the transit area, and it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an NSSA.
          - **dead-interval** `uint16`: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.
            Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
          - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval on the virtual link.
            RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
          - **retransmit-interval** `uint16`: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.
            RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
          - **transmit-delay** `uint16`: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 5340 / RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).
            RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
    - **instance-id** `uint8`: OSPFv3 Instance ID of this address family.
      RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the IPv4-multicast range as 96 to 127.
    - **interfaces** `container`: OSPFv3-enabled interfaces for this address family.
      RFC 5838 section 2.4 requires a router that takes part in an address family to discard a Hello whose AF-bit is clear. The base IPv6-unicast family is the one exception. An interface listed here takes part in this family only.
      - **interface <name>** `list`: Per-interface OSPFv3 configuration.
        The list is keyed by the interface name. The same interface CAN appear in the list of another address family, with its own cost and its own adjacencies.
        - **area** `string`: Declared area this interface belongs to.
          Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area ID.
        - **bfd** `container`: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPFv3 interface.
          RFC 5880 and RFC 5881 define single-hop BFD. When this container enables it, a Full adjacency opens an IPv6 single-hop BFD session over the link-local pair. A failure that BFD detects declares the neighbor down much faster than the router-dead interval does.
          - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.
            A BFD session that goes Down or AdminDown declares the OSPFv3 neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is 40 seconds by default.
          - **min-rx** `uint32`: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).
            The far system sends no faster than this value. RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min TX Interval of the far system.
          - **min-tx** `uint32`: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).
            RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed transmit interval as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
          - **multiplier** `uint8`: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).
            RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 states that Detect Mult is the number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The detection time is this value multiplied by the agreed transmit interval.
        - **cost** `uint16`: Interface output cost.
          RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 requires an interface output cost of more than 0, and Ze advertises the value as the cost of this link. An absent leaf takes cost 1, whatever the speed of the link is.
        - **dead-interval** `uint16`: Router-dead interval.
          Ze declares the neighbor dead after this long with no Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match. Appendix C.3 gives 4 times the hello-interval as the sample value.
        - **enabled** `boolean`: OSPFv3 enabled on this interface.
          A false value drops the interface from the OSPFv3 instance. Ze then sends no Hello on the link, and this router advertises no link for it.
        - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval.
          RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose HelloInterval does not match the configured value, so every router on the link MUST hold the same value. A smaller value detects a failure faster and sends more protocol traffic.
        - **ipsec** `container`: Manual IPsec that protects the OSPFv3 packets of this interface.
          RFC 4552 defines manual IPsec, with AH or with ESP, for an OSPFv3 interface. When the interface comes up, Ze installs a transport-mode kernel Security Association and a proto-89 policy. The kernel applies AH or ESP below the socket. It discards an unprotected OSPF packet, and one whose integrity check fails, with no message (RFC 4552 §3 and §4). This authentication path is distinct from the RFC 7166 authentication trailer, and it is mutually exclusive with a per-interface authentication key-chain. RFC 4552 §7 permits manual keying only, because IKE cannot key the multicast group. The inbound SA and the outbound SA share one key.
          - **algorithm** `enumeration`: HMAC-SHA integrity algorithm.
            The value sets the length the key leaf takes: 40 hex characters for sha1, 64 for sha256, 96 for sha384, and 128 for sha512. Both routers MUST configure the same algorithm. RFC 4552 section 3 requires the receiver to discard a packet that fails the check, with no message.
            - `sha1`: HMAC-SHA-1 with a 40 hex character key.
            - `sha256`: HMAC-SHA-256 with a 64 hex character key.
            - `sha384`: HMAC-SHA-384 with a 96 hex character key.
            - `sha512`: HMAC-SHA-512 with a 128 hex character key.
          - **encryption-algorithm** `enumeration`: ESP confidentiality algorithm.
            RFC 4552 §4 offers confidentiality with ESP only, never with AH. Leave this leaf absent, or set it to null, for an ESP that authenticates the packet and does not encrypt it.
            - `aes128`: Encrypt with AES and a 128-bit key.
            - `aes256`: Encrypt with AES and a 256-bit key.
            - `null`: Authenticate the packet and do not encrypt it.
          - **encryption-key** `string`: ESP encryption key, written in hex characters.
            The length MUST match the encryption-algorithm leaf. aes128 takes 32 hex characters, and aes256 takes 64.
          - **key** `string`: Integrity key, written in hex characters.
            The length MUST match the algorithm. sha1 takes 40 hex characters, sha256 takes 64, sha384 takes 96, and sha512 takes 128.
          - **protocol** `enumeration`: IPsec protocol that protects the OSPFv3 packets.
            esp is RFC 4303, and an implementation MUST support authentication with it. ah is RFC 4302, and an implementation MAY support it.
            - `ah`: Authentication Header (RFC 4302): integrity with no encryption.
            - `esp`: Encapsulating Security Payload (RFC 4303): integrity, with optional encryption.
          - **replay-window** `uint8`: Anti-replay window, counted in packets.
            The window applies to ah and to esp alike. RFC 4302 §3.4.3 and RFC 4303 §3.4.3 let the receiver enable or disable anti-replay for each SA, and this leaf is that switch. The value 0 disables it. 0 is the default because every OSPFv3 SA is manually keyed (RFC 4552 §7), and RFC 4302 §5 says that a compliant implementation SHOULD NOT provide anti-replay with a manually keyed SA. A non-zero window is 32 or more, which is the minimum RFC 4302 §3.4.3 requires. That section prefers 64.
          - **spi** `uint32`: Security Parameters Index (RFC 4303 §2.1 reserves 0..255).
            RFC 4552 section 7 gives the inbound SA and the outbound SA the same SPI, because a manually keyed group negotiates nothing. Give each protected interface its own SPI. The kernel identifies the state by the destination, the SPI and the protocol, so two interfaces that share an SPI collide.
        - **ldp-sync** `container`: LDP-IGP synchronization of the IPv6 family.
          RFC 5443 and RFC 6138 define LDP-IGP synchronization. The IPv6 family reuses the address-family-neutral state machine on the shared interface model.
          - **enable** `boolean`: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization on this interface.
            RFC 5443 section 1 states that a blackhole exists when one link on the shortest path carries no LDP session. A false value leaves the cost of the link unchanged while LDP converges. Traffic can then be lost on a link whose label bindings do not exist yet.
          - **holddown** `uint16`: Seconds Ze waits before it declares the link synchronized.
            The wait starts when the LDP session is established (RFC 5443 section 2).
        - **nbma-neighbor <router-id>** `list`: A statically configured NBMA neighbor.
          RFC 2328 Appendix C.6 defines the neighbor list. The list is required for network-type nbma and for the non-broadcast point-to-multipoint variant. Ze keys an IPv6 neighbor by Router ID.
          - **link-local** `string`: IPv6 link-local address of the neighbor.
            The address is the unicast Hello destination. Ze learns it from the first Hello of the neighbor when this leaf is absent.
          - **priority** `uint8`: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.
            The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it and never elects it.
        - **network-type** `enumeration`: Network type of this interface.
          broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll Hellos (RFC 5340). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links, with one /128 host route for each neighbor and no DR.
          - `broadcast`: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.
          - `nbma`: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.
          - `point-to-multipoint`: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.
          - `point-to-point`: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.
        - **passive** `boolean`: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.
          Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps advertising the link.
        - **poll-interval** `uint16`: NBMA poll interval.
          Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
        - **priority** `uint8`: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.
          The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.
    - **segment-routing** `container`: Segment Routing over the MPLS dataplane.
      RFC 8665 defines Segment Routing for OSPFv2, and RFC 8666 for OSPFv3. Ze advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the SRGB label range, the SRLB label range, and one Prefix-SID for each configured prefix. Ze installs label-switched forwarding through the shared mpls-fib. Segment Routing is off by default.
      - **enable** `boolean`: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.
        When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
      - **prefix-sid <prefix>** `list`: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.
        The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
        - **explicit-null** `boolean`: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
          The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
        - **index** `uint32`: SID index into the SRGB.
          The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
        - **no-php** `boolean`: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
          The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
        - **node-sid** `boolean`: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).

        When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
      - **prefix-sid <prefix>** `list`: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.
        The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
        - **explicit-null** `boolean`: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
          The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
        - **index** `uint32`: SID index into the SRGB.
          The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
        - **no-php** `boolean`: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
          The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
        - **node-sid** `boolean`: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).
          RFC 7684 section 2.1 sets the N-Flag when the prefix identifies the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore the flag when the prefix length is not a host prefix.
