        The SRGB is the contiguous global MPLS label range this node owns, which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
        - **lower-bound** `uint32`: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).
          Ze reads the SRGB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
        - **upper-bound** `uint32`: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.
          The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
      - **srlb** `container`: Segment Routing Local Block of this node.
        The SRLB is the local MPLS label range that Ze allocates an Adjacency-SID from (RFC 8665 section 3.3). The SRLB MUST NOT overlap the SRGB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
        - **lower-bound** `uint32`: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).
          Ze reads the SRLB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
        - **upper-bound** `uint32`: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.
          The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
      - **srms-preference** `uint8`: SR Mapping-Server preference of this node.
        Ze advertises the value in the SRMS-Preference TLV (RFC 8665 section 3.4). An unset leaf advertises no TLV.
  - **ipv6-multicast** `container`: The IPv6-multicast OSPFv3 address family.
    RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the Instance ID range as 32 to 63. Ze computes reachability in the unicast shape. Ze does not implement the MOSPF tree computation.
    - **areas** `container`: OSPFv3 areas for this address family.
      RFC 5838 section 1 maps each address family to a separate Instance ID and a separate OSPFv3 instance. Ze starts one engine instance for each configured family. An area declared here belongs to that instance alone.
      - **area <area-id>** `list`: Per-area OSPFv3 configuration.
        The list is keyed by area-id. All routers in an area MUST agree on the configuration of that area. RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 states that a disagreement stops an adjacency from forming between two routers.
        - **area-type** `enumeration`: Area type.
          RFC 5340 Appendix C.2 excludes every AS-external-LSA from a stub area and from an NSSA. A router inside a stub area reaches an external destination through the default inter-area route alone. The backbone MUST NOT be a stub area or an NSSA, and a virtual link MUST NOT cross either one.
          - `normal`: Flood AS-external-LSAs into this area.
          - `nssa`: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and import external routes as Type 7 LSAs.
          - `stub`: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.
        - **virtual-link <remote-router-id>** `list`: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.
          RFC 5340 section 4.2 defines the virtual link. The link belongs to the backbone area. Its cost is the SPF path cost across the transit area, and it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an NSSA.
          - **dead-interval** `uint16`: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.
            Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
          - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval on the virtual link.
            RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
          - **retransmit-interval** `uint16`: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.
            RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
          - **transmit-delay** `uint16`: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 5340 / RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).
            RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
    - **instance-id** `uint8`: OSPFv3 Instance ID of this address family.
      RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the IPv6-multicast range as 32 to 63.
    - **interfaces** `container`: OSPFv3-enabled interfaces for this address family.
      RFC 5838 section 2.4 requires a router that takes part in an address family to discard a Hello whose AF-bit is clear. The base IPv6-unicast family is the one exception. An interface listed here takes part in this family only.
      - **interface <name>** `list`: Per-interface OSPFv3 configuration.
        The list is keyed by the interface name. The same interface CAN appear in the list of another address family, with its own cost and its own adjacencies.
        - **area** `string`: Declared area this interface belongs to.
          Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area ID.
        - **bfd** `container`: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPFv3 interface.
          RFC 5880 and RFC 5881 define single-hop BFD. When this container enables it, a Full adjacency opens an IPv6 single-hop BFD session over the link-local pair. A failure that BFD detects declares the neighbor down much faster than the router-dead interval does.
          - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.
            A BFD session that goes Down or AdminDown declares the OSPFv3 neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is 40 seconds by default.
          - **min-rx** `uint32`: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).
            The far system sends no faster than this value. RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min TX Interval of the far system.
          - **min-tx** `uint32`: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).
            RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed transmit interval as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
          - **multiplier** `uint8`: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).
            RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 states that Detect Mult is the number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The detection time is this value multiplied by the agreed transmit interval.
        - **cost** `uint16`: Interface output cost.
          RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 requires an interface output cost of more than 0, and Ze advertises the value as the cost of this link. An absent leaf takes cost 1, whatever the speed of the link is.
        - **dead-interval** `uint16`: Router-dead interval.
          Ze declares the neighbor dead after this long with no Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match. Appendix C.3 gives 4 times the hello-interval as the sample value.
        - **enabled** `boolean`: OSPFv3 enabled on this interface.
          A false value drops the interface from the OSPFv3 instance. Ze then sends no Hello on the link, and this router advertises no link for it.
        - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval.
          RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose HelloInterval does not match the configured value, so every router on the link MUST hold the same value. A smaller value detects a failure faster and sends more protocol traffic.
        - **ipsec** `container`: Manual IPsec that protects the OSPFv3 packets of this interface.
          RFC 4552 defines manual IPsec, with AH or with ESP, for an OSPFv3 interface. When the interface comes up, Ze installs a transport-mode kernel Security Association and a proto-89 policy. The kernel applies AH or ESP below the socket. It discards an unprotected OSPF packet, and one whose integrity check fails, with no message (RFC 4552 §3 and §4). This authentication path is distinct from the RFC 7166 authentication trailer, and it is mutually exclusive with a per-interface authentication key-chain. RFC 4552 §7 permits manual keying only, because IKE cannot key the multicast group. The inbound SA and the outbound SA share one key.
          - **algorithm** `enumeration`: HMAC-SHA integrity algorithm.
            The value sets the length the key leaf takes: 40 hex characters for sha1, 64 for sha256, 96 for sha384, and 128 for sha512. Both routers MUST configure the same algorithm. RFC 4552 section 3 requires the receiver to discard a packet that fails the check, with no message.
            - `sha1`: HMAC-SHA-1 with a 40 hex character key.
            - `sha256`: HMAC-SHA-256 with a 64 hex character key.
            - `sha384`: HMAC-SHA-384 with a 96 hex character key.
            - `sha512`: HMAC-SHA-512 with a 128 hex character key.
          - **encryption-algorithm** `enumeration`: ESP confidentiality algorithm.
            RFC 4552 §4 offers confidentiality with ESP only, never with AH. Leave this leaf absent, or set it to null, for an ESP that authenticates the packet and does not encrypt it.
            - `aes128`: Encrypt with AES and a 128-bit key.
            - `aes256`: Encrypt with AES and a 256-bit key.
            - `null`: Authenticate the packet and do not encrypt it.
          - **encryption-key** `string`: ESP encryption key, written in hex characters.
            The length MUST match the encryption-algorithm leaf. aes128 takes 32 hex characters, and aes256 takes 64.
          - **key** `string`: Integrity key, written in hex characters.
            The length MUST match the algorithm. sha1 takes 40 hex characters, sha256 takes 64, sha384 takes 96, and sha512 takes 128.
          - **protocol** `enumeration`: IPsec protocol that protects the OSPFv3 packets.
            esp is RFC 4303, and an implementation MUST support authentication with it. ah is RFC 4302, and an implementation MAY support it.
            - `ah`: Authentication Header (RFC 4302): integrity with no encryption.
            - `esp`: Encapsulating Security Payload (RFC 4303): integrity, with optional encryption.
          - **replay-window** `uint8`: Anti-replay window, counted in packets.
            The window applies to ah and to esp alike. RFC 4302 §3.4.3 and RFC 4303 §3.4.3 let the receiver enable or disable anti-replay for each SA, and this leaf is that switch. The value 0 disables it. 0 is the default because every OSPFv3 SA is manually keyed (RFC 4552 §7), and RFC 4302 §5 says that a compliant implementation SHOULD NOT provide anti-replay with a manually keyed SA. A non-zero window is 32 or more, which is the minimum RFC 4302 §3.4.3 requires. That section prefers 64.
          - **spi** `uint32`: Security Parameters Index (RFC 4303 §2.1 reserves 0..255).
            RFC 4552 section 7 gives the inbound SA and the outbound SA the same SPI, because a manually keyed group negotiates nothing. Give each protected interface its own SPI. The kernel identifies the state by the destination, the SPI and the protocol, so two interfaces that share an SPI collide.
        - **ldp-sync** `container`: LDP-IGP synchronization of the IPv6 family.
          RFC 5443 and RFC 6138 define LDP-IGP synchronization. The IPv6 family reuses the address-family-neutral state machine on the shared interface model.
          - **enable** `boolean`: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization on this interface.
            RFC 5443 section 1 states that a blackhole exists when one link on the shortest path carries no LDP session. A false value leaves the cost of the link unchanged while LDP converges. Traffic can then be lost on a link whose label bindings do not exist yet.
          - **holddown** `uint16`: Seconds Ze waits before it declares the link synchronized.
            The wait starts when the LDP session is established (RFC 5443 section 2).
        - **nbma-neighbor <router-id>** `list`: A statically configured NBMA neighbor.
          RFC 2328 Appendix C.6 defines the neighbor list. The list is required for network-type nbma and for the non-broadcast point-to-multipoint variant. Ze keys an IPv6 neighbor by Router ID.
          - **link-local** `string`: IPv6 link-local address of the neighbor.
            The address is the unicast Hello destination. Ze learns it from the first Hello of the neighbor when this leaf is absent.
          - **priority** `uint8`: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.
            The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it and never elects it.
        - **network-type** `enumeration`: Network type of this interface.
          broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll Hellos (RFC 5340). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links, with one /128 host route for each neighbor and no DR.
          - `broadcast`: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.
          - `nbma`: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.
          - `point-to-multipoint`: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.
          - `point-to-point`: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.
        - **passive** `boolean`: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.
          Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps advertising the link.
        - **poll-interval** `uint16`: NBMA poll interval.
          Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
        - **priority** `uint8`: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.
          The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.

            The address is the unicast Hello destination. Ze learns it from the first Hello of the neighbor when this leaf is absent.
          - **priority** `uint8`: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.
            The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it and never elects it.
        - **network-type** `enumeration`: Network type of this interface.
          broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll Hellos (RFC 5340). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links, with one /128 host route for each neighbor and no DR.
          - `broadcast`: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.
          - `nbma`: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.
          - `point-to-multipoint`: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.
          - `point-to-point`: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.
        - **passive** `boolean`: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.
          Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps advertising the link.
        - **poll-interval** `uint16`: NBMA poll interval.
          Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
        - **priority** `uint8`: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.
          The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.
    - **segment-routing** `container`: Segment Routing over the MPLS dataplane.
      RFC 8665 defines Segment Routing for OSPFv2, and RFC 8666 for OSPFv3. Ze advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the SRGB label range, the SRLB label range, and one Prefix-SID for each configured prefix. Ze installs label-switched forwarding through the shared mpls-fib. Segment Routing is off by default.
      - **enable** `boolean`: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.
        When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
      - **prefix-sid <prefix>** `list`: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.
        The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
        - **explicit-null** `boolean`: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
          The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
        - **index** `uint32`: SID index into the SRGB.
          The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
        - **no-php** `boolean`: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
          The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
        - **node-sid** `boolean`: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).
          RFC 7684 section 2.1 sets the N-Flag when the prefix identifies the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore the flag when the prefix length is not a host prefix.
      - **srgb** `container`: Segment Routing Global Block of this node.
        The SRGB is the contiguous global MPLS label range this node owns, which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
        - **lower-bound** `uint32`: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).
          Ze reads the SRGB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
        - **upper-bound** `uint32`: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.
          The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
      - **srlb** `container`: Segment Routing Local Block of this node.
        The SRLB is the local MPLS label range that Ze allocates an Adjacency-SID from (RFC 8665 section 3.3). The SRLB MUST NOT overlap the SRGB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
        - **lower-bound** `uint32`: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).
          Ze reads the SRLB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
        - **upper-bound** `uint32`: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.
          The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
      - **srms-preference** `uint8`: SR Mapping-Server preference of this node.
        Ze advertises the value in the SRMS-Preference TLV (RFC 8665 section 3.4). An unset leaf advertises no TLV.
- **areas** `container`: OSPF areas.
  RFC 2328 section 3 states that each area runs a separate copy of the link-state algorithm, so each area holds its own link-state database. A router connected to two or more areas is an area border router.
  - **area <area-id>** `list`: Per-area configuration.
    The list is keyed by area-id. Ze holds one link-state database for each area this router joins. An interface joins the area that its area leaf names.
    - **area-type** `enumeration`: Type of this area.
      The types are normal, stub and nssa. The stub specification and the NSSA specification state what each type does.
      - `normal`: Flood AS-external-LSAs into this area.
      - `nssa`: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and import external routes as Type 7 LSAs.
      - `stub`: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.
    - **authentication** `container`: Area-level authentication defaults.
      An interface whose authentication mode is inherit takes the key chain of its area. An interface that names its own key chain overrides this default.
      - **key-chain** `string`: Default key chain inherited by interfaces.
        The value MUST name an entry of the key-chains list. Ze leaves the interface unauthenticated when the name matches no entry.
    - **default-cost** `uint32`: Default summary metric for stub/NSSA areas.
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 names the value StubDefaultCost. It is the cost of the default summary-LSA this router advertises into the area. The value applies only when this router is an area border router of a stub area or an NSSA.
    - **no-summary** `boolean`: Suppress the Type 3 summaries of a totally-stubby or totally-NSSA area.
      Ze keeps the default summary the area requires, and suppresses every other Type 3 summary.
    - **nssa** `container`: NSSA-specific configuration (applies when area-type is nssa).
      RFC 3101 section 1.3 lets an NSSA import an external route in a limited fashion, which a stub area cannot do. The area carries such a route as a Type 7 LSA, and the elected translator rewrites it into a Type 5 LSA.
      - **default-originate** `boolean`: Originate a Type 7 default route into the NSSA.
        This leaf applies to an internal NSSA router that has a usable forwarding address. An NSSA border router always originates the required default route, so the leaf changes nothing there. It is also inert when the area sets no-summary true: RFC 3101 section 1.3 makes an internal router's Type 7 default and the no-summary option mutually exclusive.
      - **stability-interval** `uint16`: Hysteresis before a translator that lost the role stops translating.
        RFC 3101 section 3.5 defines the interval. A newly elected translator keeps translating for this long after it loses the role.
      - **translate-role** `enumeration`: Role of this router in the Type 7 to Type 5 translation.
        candidate enters the election, which the highest router-id wins. always translates whatever the election decides. never does no translation.
        - `always`: Translate Type 7 LSAs whatever the election decides.
        - `candidate`: Enter the translator election, which the highest Router ID wins.
        - `never`: Do no Type 7 to Type 5 translation.
    - **ranges** `container`: Inter-area summary ranges.
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 advertises at most one summary-LSA for each address range outside the area. A network that no range covers keeps its own summary-LSA.
      - **range <prefix>** `list`: One area summary range.
        The list is keyed by the prefix. Ze advertises one Type 3 summary-LSA for the range, and it suppresses the summary-LSA of every network the range covers.
        - **advertise** `enumeration`: Advertise the aggregate or suppress specifics.
          RFC 2328 section 12.4.3 suppresses the Type 3 summary-LSA when the status is DoNotAdvertise, and the component networks then stay hidden from the other areas. The value advertise sends one summary-LSA for the range instead.
          - `advertise`: Send one summary-LSA for the whole range.
          - `not-advertise`: Send no summary-LSA and hide the component networks from other areas.
        - **cost** `uint32`: Override cost for the aggregate Type 3 LSA.
          RFC 2328 section 12.4.3 gives the range the largest cost of any component network. This leaf replaces that cost with a fixed value.
    - **virtual-link <remote-router-id>** `list`: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.
      RFC 2328 section 15 defines the virtual link. The link belongs to the backbone area. Ze computes its output cost from the SPF over the transit area, and it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an NSSA.
      - **dead-interval** `uint16`: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.
        Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
      - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval on the virtual link.
        RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
      - **retransmit-interval** `uint16`: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.
        RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
      - **transmit-delay** `uint16`: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).
        RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
- **default-information** `container`: Default-route origination as an AS-external LSA.
  Ze originates one Type 5 AS-external LSA for 0.0.0.0/0 (RFC 2328 section 12.4.4). The origination makes this router an AS boundary router, which sets the E-bit in its Router-LSA.
  - **always** `boolean`: Originate even without a default in the RIB.
    Ze then originates the default LSA whatever the Loc-RIB holds. A false value needs a non-OSPF default in the Loc-RIB first.
  - **metric** `uint32`: Default LSA metric.
    The value is the metric of the Type 5 default LSA, and the field is 24 bits wide. With metric-type type-2, the router that advertises the smallest metric attracts the traffic of the whole AS.
  - **metric-type** `enumeration`: External metric type for the default route.
    RFC 2328 section 2.3 adds the distance to the ASBR for a Type 1 metric. A Type 2 metric is compared alone, and the internal distance only breaks a tie.
    - `type-1`: Add the internal distance to the ASBR to the external metric.
    - `type-2`: Compare the external metric alone and break a tie on the internal distance.
  - **originate** `boolean`: Originate a default Type 5 LSA.
    Ze originates the LSA only while the Loc-RIB holds a default route that OSPF did not learn. Ze purges the LSA when that route goes away. The always leaf removes the condition.
- **extended-link** `boolean`: Originate Extended Link Opaque LSAs for the local links.
  RFC 7684 defines the Extended Link Opaque LSA, which is Opaque Type 8. The LSA associates attributes with the links of this router, one LSA for each point-to-point link and each transit link, which mirrors the Router-LSA link. The leaf needs opaque true. The LSA is a container that a link-attribute application fills with sub-TLVs, for example Segment Routing. It is off by default until such a producer needs it. Ze decodes and shows a received Extended Link LSA whatever this leaf holds.
- **extended-prefix** `boolean`: Originate Extended Prefix Opaque LSAs for the local prefixes.
  RFC 7684 defines the Extended Prefix Opaque LSA, which is Opaque Type 7. The LSA associates attributes with the prefixes this router advertises. The leaf needs opaque true. The LSA is a container that a prefix-attribute application fills with sub-TLVs, for example Segment Routing. It is off by default until such a producer needs it. Ze decodes and shows a received Extended Prefix LSA whatever this leaf holds.
- **fast-reroute** `container`: Loop-Free Alternate and TI-LFA IP fast reroute.
  RFC 5286 defines the Loop-Free Alternate. When this container enables fast reroute, SPF pre-computes a loop-free backup next-hop beside each primary next-hop and programs it into the FIB. Ze then repairs a single local link failure, or a single node failure, before the IGP reconverges. TI-LFA mode adds a Segment-Routing repair-list fallback where no directly connected LFA exists, and it needs segment-routing. The container applies to OSPFv2 and to OSPFv3. OSPFv3 gets base-LFA next-hop selection only, because an SR repair label is IPv4 only.
  - **enable** `boolean`: Enable LFA / TI-LFA fast-reroute backup computation and install.
    RFC 5286 section 3.6 selects at most one alternate next-hop for each primary next-hop. A false leaf computes no alternate, so a link failure waits for the SPF run and the FIB update.
  - **mode** `enumeration`: Backup computation mode: base LFA, or LFA with a TI-LFA SR-repair fallback.
    ti-lfa builds a repair list from the Prefix-SID and the Adjacency-SID of the repair path, so it needs segment-routing. lfa uses a directly connected loop-free neighbor alone, and it protects no prefix that has none.
    - `lfa`: Base loop-free alternates only (RFC 5286).
    - `ti-lfa`: Add the Segment-Routing repair-list fallback (TI-LFA).
  - **node-protection** `boolean`: Prefer node-protecting alternates over link-only alternates (RFC 5286 Section 3.6).
    RFC 5286 section 3.2 gives Inequality 3 for a node-protecting alternate N against a primary neighbor E for destination D. Distance_opt(N, D) MUST be less than Distance_opt(N, E) plus Distance_opt(E, D). Section 3.6 takes a link-protecting alternate when no node-protecting one exists.
- **graceful-restart** `container`: Graceful Restart, which keeps forwarding across a control-plane restart.
  RFC 3623 defines Graceful Restart for OSPFv2, and RFC 5187 for OSPFv3. The container is family-neutral and drives both address families. The OSPFv3 family inherits it unless that family configures its own.
  - **helper** `container`: Helper role of this router.
    In this role Ze holds the adjacency to a restarting neighbor and stops LSDB churn for the grace period of that neighbor.
    - **strict-lsa-checking** `boolean`: Stop helper mode when a changed LSA would flood to the restarting router.
      RFC 3623 Appendix B.2 names this value RestartHelperStrictLSAChecking, and section 3.2 states the rule. Ze stops helper mode when it installs a changed LSA that would flood to the restarting router.
    - **support** `boolean`: RFC 3623 Appendix B.2 RestartHelperSupport: act as a helper for a restarting neighbor.
      RFC 3623 section 3.1 enters helper mode on two conditions. This router MUST hold a Full adjacency with the restarting router. The database MUST NOT have changed since that router restarted. A false value refuses helper mode, so the restart drops the adjacency.
  - **restarter** `container`: Restarting-router role of this router.
    In this role Ze originates a Grace-LSA and keeps the FIB across a restart.
    - **restart-interval** `uint16`: Grace period during which a neighbor advertises this router as fully adjacent.
      RFC 3623 Appendix B.1 names this value RestartInterval. Keep it at or under LSRefreshTime, which is 1800 seconds. A longer interval lets the LSAs of this router age out during the restart.
    - **support** `enumeration`: RFC 3623 Appendix B.1 RestartSupport.
      planned names a restart the operator triggered. planned-and-unplanned covers a cold restart too (RFC 3623 section 5), and Ze restricts the unplanned reason to unknown and to redundant-cp.
      - `disabled`: Never originate a Grace-LSA, and restart normally.
      - `planned`: Originate a Grace-LSA on a planned restart only.
      - `planned-and-unplanned`: Originate a Grace-LSA on a planned restart and on an unplanned restart.
- **interfaces** `container`: OSPF-enabled interfaces.
  RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 states that some of these parameters describe the attached network, so they MUST be consistent across every router on that network. The hello-interval, the dead-interval and the authentication are the three that stop an adjacency when they differ.
  - **interface <name>** `list`: Per-interface OSPF configuration.
    The list is keyed by the interface name. Ze enrolls an entry only when its enabled leaf is true and the areas container declares its area.
    - **area** `string`: Declared area this interface belongs to.
      Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area ID.
    - **authentication** `container`: Per-interface authentication settings.
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 states that the AuType MUST be the same for all routers attached to the network. Ze takes the AuType from the algorithm of the keys in the resolved chain.
      - **key-chain** `string`: Key chain reference.
        The value MUST name an entry of the key-chains list. Ze takes the area chain instead when the mode leaf is inherit, even when this leaf names a chain.
      - **mode** `enumeration`: Authentication mode of this interface.
        The value inherit takes the area default.
        - `hmac-sha-1`: HMAC-SHA-1 digest (AuType 2).
        - `hmac-sha-256`: HMAC-SHA-256 digest (AuType 2).
        - `hmac-sha-384`: HMAC-SHA-384 digest (AuType 2).
        - `hmac-sha-512`: HMAC-SHA-512 digest (AuType 2).
        - `inherit`: Take the authentication key chain of the area.
        - `md5`: Keyed MD5 digest (AuType 2).
        - `none`: No authentication (AuType 0).
        - `simple`: Cleartext password (AuType 1).
    - **bfd** `container`: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPF interface.
      RFC 5880 and RFC 5881 define single-hop BFD. When this container enables it, a Full adjacency opens a single-hop BFD session. A failure that BFD detects declares the neighbor down much faster than the router-dead interval does.
      - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.
        A BFD session that goes Down or AdminDown declares the OSPF neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is 40 seconds by default.
      - **min-rx** `uint32`: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).
        The far system sends no faster than this value. RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min TX Interval of the far system.
      - **min-tx** `uint32`: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).
        RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed transmit interval as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
      - **multiplier** `uint8`: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).
        RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 states that Detect Mult is the number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The detection time is this value multiplied by the agreed transmit interval.
    - **cost** `uint16`: Interface output cost.
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 requires an interface output cost of more than 0. Ze advertises the value as the cost of this link in its Router-LSA. An absent leaf takes cost 1, whatever the speed of the link is.
    - **dead-interval** `uint16`: Router-dead interval.
      Ze declares the neighbor dead after this long with no Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match. Appendix C.3 gives 4 times the hello-interval as the sample value.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: OSPF enabled on this interface.
      A false value drops the interface from the OSPF instance. Ze then sends no Hello on the link, and this router advertises no link for it.
    - **hello-interval** `uint16`: Hello interval.
      RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose HelloInterval does not match the configured value, so every router on the link MUST hold the same value. A smaller value detects a failure faster and sends more protocol traffic.
    - **instance-id** `uint8[]`: Multi-Instance Instance IDs this interface takes part in.
      RFC 6549 section 3 defines OSPFv2 Multi-Instance. An absent leaf-list runs the base instance 0 only, which is bit-for-bit compatible with base OSPFv2. Each listed value runs a separate OSPFv2 instance, which Ze demultiplexes on this subnet. Ze discards a received packet whose Instance ID matches none of the listed values (RFC 6549 sections 2 and 3.1).
    - **ldp-sync** `container`: LDP-IGP synchronization of this interface.
      RFC 5443 and RFC 6138 define LDP-IGP synchronization. Ze holds a point-to-point link at maximum cost, and withholds the transit link of a broadcast link that is not a cut edge, until LDP is synchronized. Transit traffic is then not black-holed before the label bindings exist.
      - **enable** `boolean`: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization on this interface.
        RFC 5443 section 1 states that a blackhole exists when one link on the shortest path carries no LDP session. A false value leaves the cost of the link unchanged while LDP converges. Traffic can then be lost on a link whose label bindings do not exist yet.
      - **holddown** `uint16`: Seconds Ze waits before it declares the link synchronized.
        The wait starts when the LDP session is established. RFC 5443 section 2 estimates that every label binding is exchanged by then, and it defines no universal default. The value 0 restores the cost as soon as the session is up, which is permitted and not advised.
    - **mtu-ignore** `boolean`: Skip DD MTU mismatch rejection.
      RFC 2328 Section 10.6 rejects a Database Description packet whose Interface MTU is larger than the receiving interface accepts without fragmentation. A true value skips that check, so the adjacency reaches Full across an MTU mismatch.
    - **nbma-neighbor <address>** `list`: A statically configured NBMA neighbor.
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.6 defines the neighbor list. The list is required for network-type nbma and for the non-broadcast point-to-multipoint variant.
      - **priority** `uint8`: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.
        The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it and never elects it.
    - **network-type** `enumeration`: Network type of this interface.
      broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll Hellos (RFC 2328). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links, with one host route for each neighbor and no DR.
      - `broadcast`: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.
      - `loopback`: Send no Hellos and advertise the interface address as a host route.
      - `nbma`: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.
      - `point-to-multipoint`: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.
      - `point-to-point`: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.
    - **passive** `boolean`: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.
      Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps advertising the link.
    - **poll-interval** `uint16`: NBMA poll interval.
      Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
    - **priority** `uint8`: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.
      The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.
    - **retransmit-interval** `uint16`: LSA retransmit interval.
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names the value RxmtInterval, and it also paces the retransmission of a Database Description packet and a Link State Request. Set it well over the round-trip delay on the link, or needless retransmissions result.
    - **traffic-engineering** `container`: Traffic Engineering link attributes of this interface.
      RFC 3630 and RFC 5392 define the attributes. Ze advertises them in a Type 10 opaque TE LSA, and in a Type 10 or a Type 11 LSA for an inter-as link. The container needs the top-level opaque leaf. The TE metric is independent of the cost.
      - **admin-group** `uint32`: Administrative Group mask of this link.
        RFC 3630 section 2.5.9 defines the Administrative Group, which is also named Resource Class or Color. The mask is 32 bits wide, and the least significant bit is group 0.
      - **enable** `boolean`: Advertise a TE Link LSA for this interface.
        Ze originates one Type 10 opaque LSA for each active TE link, and that LSA carries one Link TLV (RFC 3630 section 2.4.2). Ze skips a link with no usable Link Type and Link ID, for example a broadcast link with no DR yet.
      - **inter-as** `container`: Inter-AS Traffic Engineering link.
        RFC 5392 defines the inter-AS TE link. Ze forms no OSPF adjacency on the link (RFC 5392 section 4), and the ASBR proxies the link into its own AS. The container needs remote-as, and at least one remote-asbr address.
        - **remote-as** `asn`: RFC 5392 sec 3.3.1 Remote AS Number of the neighboring AS the link connects to.
          RFC 5392 section 3.3.1 makes the Remote AS Number sub-TLV REQUIRED in a Link TLV that advertises an inter-AS TE link. The sub-TLV is type 21 and four octets wide, so it carries a 4-byte AS number.
        - **remote-asbr-ipv4** `ipv4-address`: IPv4 Remote ASBR ID of the inter-AS link.
          RFC 5392 section 3.3.2 defines the value, which travels in sub-TLV 22. The RFC recommends the remote TE Router ID.
        - **remote-asbr-ipv6** `ipv6-address`: IPv6 Remote ASBR ID of the inter-AS link.
          RFC 5392 section 3.3.3 defines the value, which travels in sub-TLV 24 and not in sub-TLV 23. Use a stable global IPv6 address.
        - **scope** `enumeration`: Flooding scope of the inter-AS TE LSA.
          RFC 5392 section 3.1.1 defines the policy. area is a Type 10 LSA, held inside the area of the ASBR. as is a Type 11 LSA, flooded across the AS.
          - `area`: Type 10 LSA, held inside the area of the ASBR.
          - `as`: Type 11 LSA, flooded across the AS.
      - **max-bandwidth** `uint64`: RFC 3630 sec 2.5.6 Maximum Bandwidth (true link capacity) in bytes/second.
        RFC 3630 section 2.5.6 carries the value in IEEE floating point form, in a four-octet sub-TLV of type 6. An unset max-reservable-bandwidth takes this value (section 2.5.7).
      - **max-reservable-bandwidth** `uint64`: Maximum Reservable Bandwidth of this link.
        RFC 3630 section 2.5.7 defines the value, in bytes per second. An unset leaf takes max-bandwidth.
      - **te-metric** `uint32`: Traffic Engineering metric of this link.
        RFC 3630 section 2.5.5 defines the metric. It is independent of the OSPF cost, and an unset leaf takes the cost.
    - **transmit-delay** `uint16`: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).
      RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet on this link.
- **key-chains <name>** `list`: Named authentication key chains for hitless rotation.
  A chain rotates the signing key and the adjacency stays up. Ze refuses a chain whose send-lifetime windows leave a gap, because the signing coverage would then lapse.
  - **extended-sequence** `boolean`: Use AuType 3 rather than AuType 2 for this key chain.
    RFC 7474 defines AuType 3, which carries an extended cryptographic sequence number of 64 bits. The leaf applies to the HMAC-SHA algorithms.
  - **key <key-id>** `list`: Keys in this chain.
    The list is keyed by key-id. Ze picks the key that signs from the send-lifetime windows, and it verifies a received packet against every key of the chain.
    - **accept-lifetime** `container`: When this key is accepted on receive.
      RFC 5709 section 3.2 names the two bounds Key Start Accept and Key Stop Accept. RFC 7474 section 4 requires that, for packet reception, 'the key validity interval as defined by AcceptLifetimeStart and AcceptLifetimeEnd must include the current time'. Ze checks that both timestamps parse as RFC 3339 and refuses the configuration when one does not. On receive Ze tries only the keys whose window covers the current time, so a packet made with a key outside its window is dropped and counted under the accept-lifetime reason. A key with no accept-lifetime is accepted at every time. When no key of the chain is in its window, every packet on the interface is dropped. Use `send-lifetime` to control which key signs.
      - **end** `string`: RFC3339 end timestamp.
        The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp. RFC 5709 section 3.2 calls this bound Key Stop Accept, the time at which this router stops accepting a packet made with this key. Keep it later than the `send-lifetime` end, because RFC 5709 section 3.2 states that 'KeyStopGenerate SHOULD be less than KeyStopAccept'. An absent leaf leaves the window open with no end bound.
      - **start** `string`: RFC3339 start timestamp.
        The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. RFC 5709 section 3.2 calls this bound Key Start Accept, the time from which this router accepts a packet made with this key. An absent leaf leaves the window open with no start bound.
    - **algorithm** `enumeration`: Authentication algorithm.
      simple is AuType 1, which sends a cleartext password. The md5 value and the hmac-sha values are AuType 2, which sends a digest. The extended-sequence leaf turns AuType 2 into AuType 3.
      - `hmac-sha-1`: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-1 digest of 20 octets.
      - `hmac-sha-256`: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-256 digest of 32 octets.
      - `hmac-sha-384`: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-384 digest of 48 octets.
      - `hmac-sha-512`: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-512 digest of 64 octets.
      - `md5`: AuType 2, a keyed MD5 digest of 16 octets.
      - `simple`: AuType 1, a cleartext password.
    - **secret** `string`: Shared secret, masked and $9$-encoded at rest.
      Ze masks the value in every output, and it stores the $9$ form at rest. A simple-password secret is at most 8 octets, which RFC 2328 Appendix D sets as the width of the authentication field.
    - **send-lifetime** `container`: Window in which Ze can use this key to sign a packet.
      Ze signs with the key whose window covers the current time. When two windows cover it, the latest-starting key wins. When every window has expired, Ze keeps the most-recently-starting key rather than sending an unauthenticated packet.
      - **end** `string`: RFC3339 end timestamp.
        The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp. An absent leaf leaves the window open with no end bound, so this key signs until a later key starts.
      - **start** `string`: RFC3339 start timestamp.
        The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. An absent leaf leaves the window open with no start bound.
- **max-metric** `container`: Stub-router advertisement of this router.
  RFC 6987 defines the stub router. Ze originates the Router-LSA with MaxLinkMetric, so transit traffic avoids this router.
  - **router-lsa** `container`: Stub-router control of the Router-LSA link costs.
    RFC 6987 section 2 has the stub router announce its Router-LSA with the cost of all non-stub links set to MaxLinkMetric. Section 3 defines MaxLinkMetric as the 16-bit value 0xffff. A stub link keeps its cost, so a directly connected prefix of this router stays reachable. The `always` leaf originates that Router-LSA. The `on-startup` and `on-shutdown` leaves are stored and reported by `show ospf`, and they originate nothing. Any of the three set to a value other than the default raises the stub-router bit in the Router Information LSA of RFC 7770.
    - **always** `boolean`: Always advertise as a stub router.
      Ze sets every non-stub link of its Router-LSA to MaxLinkMetric, which RFC 6987 section 3 defines as 0xffff. A stub link keeps its cost, so a directly connected prefix of this router stays reachable.
    - **on-shutdown** `uint32`: Advertise as a stub router for N seconds during a graceful shutdown (0 disables).
      The unit is seconds, the range is 0 to 86400, and 0 is the default. RFC 6987 defines the MaxLinkMetric advertisement and defines no shutdown timer for it. Ze stores this value and reports it as `on-shutdown-seconds` in `show ospf`. Ze raises the stub-router bit in the Router Information LSA of RFC 7770 when the value is more than 0. Ze starts no timed window: only `always` makes Ze originate the Router-LSA with MaxLinkMetric.
    - **on-startup** `uint32`: Advertise as a stub router for N seconds after startup (0 disables).
      The unit is seconds, the range is 0 to 86400, and 0 is the default. RFC 6987 defines the MaxLinkMetric advertisement and defines no startup timer for it. Ze stores this value and reports it as `on-startup-seconds` in `show ospf`. Ze raises the stub-router bit in the Router Information LSA of RFC 7770 when the value is more than 0. Ze starts no timed window: only `always` makes Ze originate the Router-LSA with MaxLinkMetric.
- **maximum-paths** `uint8`: Maximum ECMP paths per prefix.
  SPF keeps at most this many equal-cost next-hops for one prefix, and it drops the rest. Ze uses 8 when the leaf is absent.
- **opaque** `boolean`: Enable the opaque-LSA capability.
  RFC 5250 defines the opaque LSA. When this leaf is true, the router sets the O-bit in its Database Description packets, which advertises that it will receive and forward an opaque LSA, and it originates an opaque LSA for each registered consumer. Ze stores a received opaque LSA and refloods it by its scope whatever this leaf holds. A false leaf stops the capability advertisement and the origination only.
- **redistribute <source>** `list`: Per-source metric, metric type and tag for redistribution into OSPF.
  This list starts no import. The generic redistribute container enables the import, with a rule of the shape destination ospf import <source>. A source with no entry here takes metric 20 and metric-type type-2.
  - **metric** `uint32`: Injected metric.
    Ze writes the value into the metric field of the AS-external LSA, which is 24 bits wide. A source with no entry in this list takes 20.
  - **metric-type** `enumeration`: External metric type.
    RFC 2328 section 2.3 states that a Type 1 external metric is in the same units as the OSPF cost. A Type 2 metric is an order of magnitude larger than any internal path. A Type 1 route always wins over a Type 2 route.
    - `type-1`: External metric in OSPF cost units, added to the internal distance.
    - `type-2`: External metric larger than any internal path, compared alone.
  - **tag** `uint32`: External route tag.
    RFC 2328 Appendix A.4.5 states that the External Route Tag is not used by the OSPF protocol itself. It carries information between AS boundary routers, and a policy on another router CAN match it.
- **reference-bandwidth** `uint32`: Auto-cost reference bandwidth in Mbps.
  The unit is Mbps, the range is 1 to 4294967, and the default is 100000. Ze divides this bandwidth by the speed of a link to derive the cost of that link, so under the default a 10 Gbit/s link costs 10 and a 1 Gbit/s link costs 100. An interface that sets `interfaces/interface/cost` keeps that cost and is not derived. The quotient is clamped to the range a Router-LSA link metric carries, 1 to 65535, because RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 states that the interface output cost 'must always be greater than 0' and the wire field is two octets wide. A link whose speed the kernel does not report costs 1, which covers a loopback, a dummy, a tunnel and a link with no carrier; a veth reports 10000 and is derived like a real NIC. The speed is read again on each origination pass, so a link that renegotiates re-prices itself. The value is router-wide: every OSPFv3 address family prices a link exactly as the IPv4 family does. A change to this leaf drops no adjacency: Ze re-prices each interface in place and originates the new Router-LSA at the commit.
- **router-address** `ipv4-address`: Traffic Engineering Router Address of this router.
  RFC 3630 section 2.4.1 defines the Router Address. The value is a stable IPv4 address that is always reachable, usually a loopback, and the router advertises it once in its Router-Address TE LSA. An unset leaf takes the Router ID. The leaf needs opaque, and at least one traffic-engineering interface, to take effect.
- **router-id** `string`: OSPF Router ID of this instance, in dotted-quad form.
  Ze derives the Router ID when this leaf is absent. It reads the highest loopback IPv4 address first, then the highest interface IPv4 address.
- **router-information** `container`: Router Information LSA of this router.
  RFC 7770 defines the Router Information LSA, which advertises the optional capabilities of this router. It is opaque type 4 in OSPFv2 and function code 12 in OSPFv3. The container applies to both address families. A top-level container drives the OSPFv3 family unless that family configures its own.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Originate the Router Information LSA.
    The LSA advertises the informational capabilities of this router. OSPFv2 also needs opaque true, because the RI LSA is an opaque LSA.
  - **scope** `enumeration[]`: Flooding scopes at which Ze advertises the RI LSA.
    RFC 7770 section 2.7 defines the scopes. An enabled RI LSA with no scope listed takes area and as.
    - `area`: Area (OSPFv2 opaque type 10, OSPFv3 0xA00C).
    - `as`: AS-wide (OSPFv2 opaque type 11, OSPFv3 0xC00C).
    - `link`: Link-local (OSPFv2 opaque type 9).
- **segment-routing** `container`: Segment Routing over the MPLS dataplane.
  RFC 8665 defines Segment Routing for OSPFv2, and RFC 8666 for OSPFv3. Ze advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the SRGB label range, the SRLB label range, and one Prefix-SID for each configured prefix. Ze installs label-switched forwarding through the shared mpls-fib. Segment Routing is off by default.
  - **enable** `boolean`: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.
    When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
  - **prefix-sid <prefix>** `list`: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.
    The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
    - **explicit-null** `boolean`: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
      The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
    - **index** `uint32`: SID index into the SRGB.
      The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
    - **no-php** `boolean`: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.
      The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
    - **node-sid** `boolean`: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).
      RFC 7684 section 2.1 sets the N-Flag when the prefix identifies the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore the flag when the prefix length is not a host prefix.
  - **srgb** `container`: Segment Routing Global Block of this node.
    The SRGB is the contiguous global MPLS label range this node owns, which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
    - **lower-bound** `uint32`: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).
      Ze reads the SRGB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
    - **upper-bound** `uint32`: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.
      The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
  - **srlb** `container`: Segment Routing Local Block of this node.
    The SRLB is the local MPLS label range that Ze allocates an Adjacency-SID from (RFC 8665 section 3.3). The SRLB MUST NOT overlap the SRGB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
    - **lower-bound** `uint32`: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).
      Ze reads the SRLB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
    - **upper-bound** `uint32`: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.
      The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
  - **srms-preference** `uint8`: SR Mapping-Server preference of this node.
    Ze advertises the value in the SRMS-Preference TLV (RFC 8665 section 3.4). An unset leaf advertises no TLV.
- **timers** `container`: SPF and LSA throttle timers.
  Ze holds the SPF run back after a topology change, so one burst of LSAs costs one run. The three spf leaves shape that backoff. The two ls leaves bound how often one LSA is originated and accepted.
  - **min-ls-arrival-ms** `uint32`: Minimum arrival interval for accepting a new LSA instance.
    RFC 2328 Appendix B names the value MinLSArrival and sets it to 1 second. Ze discards a new instance of one LSA that arrives sooner than this after the last accepted instance.
  - **min-ls-interval-ms** `uint32`: Minimum interval between LSA reoriginations.
    RFC 2328 Appendix B names the value MinLSInterval and sets it to 5 seconds. It is the minimum time between two distinct originations of one LSA.
  - **spf-delay-ms** `uint32`: Initial SPF delay.
    Ze waits this long after the first change before it runs SPF. The delay returns to this value when no change arrived for spf-max-hold-ms.
  - **spf-hold-ms** `uint32`: SPF hold floor.
    A second change inside the backoff window raises the delay to this floor. Each further change doubles the delay, up to spf-max-hold-ms.
  - **spf-max-hold-ms** `uint32`: SPF max hold.
    The doubling stops at this value. A gap longer than this value between two changes resets the delay to spf-delay-ms.

## pki

*Provided by `ipsec-xfrm`*

PKI certificate and key store.

PKI certificate and key store. Presence of this block enables certificate-based authentication for IPsec VPN, TLS, and other subsystems.

- **ca <name>** `list`: Trusted CA certificate.
  Trusted CA certificate. The certificate leaf takes a PEM document, headers and line breaks included, which is what 'ze show pki local-ca pem' prints and what a .crt file holds. Base64-encoded DER with no PEM headers is also read.
  - **certificate** `string`: X.509 CA certificate, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER.
    The trust anchor itself, with no private key. Paste the PEM as it is printed, headers and line breaks included, which is what 'ze show pki local-ca pem' gives you and what a .crt file holds. Base64-encoded DER with no headers is also read, for a config written before PEM was accepted.
  - **crl** `string[]`: Certificate revocation lists this CA issued, each a PEM document or base64-encoded DER.
    Certificate revocation lists this CA issued, each an 'X509 CRL' PEM document or base64-encoded DER. EAP-TLS on TLS 1.3 checks the revocation status of every certificate on a peer's chain except the trust anchor. RFC 9190 Section 5.4 makes that check mandatory. An EAP-TLS peer that validates against this CA and finds no current list here is refused. Publish a fresh list before the nextUpdate of the one here passes: an expired list answers nothing about the present and refuses the same peers. A list that revokes nothing is a valid answer and is what a CA publishes while it has withdrawn no certificate.
- **certificate <name>** `list`: Device certificate with optional private key and intermediate certificates.
  One entry holds the certificate this device presents, the intermediate certificates that lead toward its trust anchor, and the private key that signs with it. The certificate leaf is mandatory and the private container is not, so an entry can hold a certificate Ze sends and cannot sign with. A TLS listener that asks for the key of such an entry is refused, and is never served another certificate in its place. Ze validates every entry when it loads the config. An expired certificate refuses the commit and stops the daemon from starting. A certificate that builds no chain to a ca entry in this block does the same.
  - **certificate** `string`: X.509 device certificate, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER.
    The certificate this node presents. Paste the PEM as it is printed, headers and line breaks included, which is what a .crt file holds. Base64-encoded DER with no headers is also read, for a config written before PEM was accepted. The matching key goes in private key.
  - **intermediate** `string[]`: Intermediate CA certificates, from the issuer toward the trust anchor.
    Intermediate CA certificates, each a PEM document or base64-encoded DER. Give them in order, from the one that issued this certificate toward the trust anchor. Ze stores them beside the device certificate for chain building, and sends them after it in the IKE_AUTH chain. RFC 7296 Section 3.6 requires an implementation be capable of being configured to send up to four X.509 certificates. This device certificate plus three intermediates is that maximum. A single value is still valid.
  - **ocsp-response** `string`: OCSP response about this certificate, stapled to a peer that asks for it.
    An OCSP response the certificate's issuer signed about this certificate, as base64-encoded DER or as an 'OCSP RESPONSE' PEM document. Ze sends it in the certificate message when a peer asks for a Certificate Status Request, which RFC 9190 Section 5.4 makes mandatory for an EAP-TLS server on TLS 1.3. Fetch it from the responder your CA publishes, with 'openssl ocsp -respout'. Ze refuses a response about another certificate. A response carries a nextUpdate: a peer that checks the status refuses this certificate once that time passes, so replace the value before it does. An entry with no response answers a Certificate Status Request with no status, which RFC 6066 Section 8 permits, and the peer then checks revocation against the crl of the ca that issued this certificate.
  - **private** `container`: Private key associated with this certificate.
    The container holds one leaf, key, and the container is optional. An entry with no private key holds a certificate Ze sends and verifies against, and cannot sign with. Ze checks when it loads the config that the key matches the public key of the certificate beside it. Ze refuses the config when it does not, so a mismatched pair never reaches a handshake. The key leaf is marked sensitive. The config file stores it as $9$, Ze decodes it on load, and a display path prints a placeholder in its place.
    - **key** `string`: Private key, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER.
      Private key, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER. The config file stores it as $9$, and Ze decodes it on load. The supported encodings are PKCS8, SEC1 (ECDSA), and PKCS1 (RSA).

## plugin

Plugin configuration

Declares the plugins this daemon runs, and the hub transport they connect back over. A built-in plugin that claims a configured address family starts with no block here, because the engine loads it for that family. Declare an internal block to run a built-in plugin under a name you choose. Declare an external block to run a program of your own. Declare a hub block to set the TLS listener and its secrets. The name of an internal or external block is the name a peer's 'attach process' binding refers to.

- **external <name>** `list`: External plugin process
  Runs a plugin as a separate process. The engine starts the run command with '/bin/sh -c'. The child connects back to the hub listener over TLS. It reads the address, the certificate authority root and its token from its environment. A block that sets use instead of run runs a built-in plugin in this process, with no fork. The block name is the name a peer's 'attach process' binding refers to, and the name the hub binds the connect-back token to.
  - **encoder** `enumeration`: Event encoding format
    Chooses how the engine encodes the events it sends this plugin: 'json' for JSON objects, 'text' for the line format ExaBGP plugins read. 'text' also makes the engine forward every received BGP UPDATE to the plugin. A peer's 'attach process' binding can set an encoding of its own, and that value wins over this one. With no value here and none on the binding, the engine uses 'text'.
    - `json`: JSON encoding
    - `text`: Human-readable text encoding
  - **respawn** `boolean`: Respawn on exit
    States what you expect ze to do when this plugin's process exits. The plugin itself declares whether it may be started again, and this leaf is a request inside that declaration. With no leaf here the plugin's own declaration decides. With 'false' the plugin is left stopped even when it would have been started again. With 'true' against a plugin that declares it must not be restarted, ze refuses to start, and the error names the plugin and the policy it declared: ze honors neither side in silence. The spelling comes from ExaBGP, whose process block carries the same leaf. A restart is bounded at 5 in 60 seconds and 20 in the life of the daemon, after which the plugin is disabled and 'show health' reports plugin-down.
  - **run** `string`: Command to execute plugin as external process (with args)
    The command line that starts the plugin. The engine runs it with '/bin/sh -c', so arguments, quoting and a PATH lookup work as they do in a shell. The directory of the running ze binary is added to PATH as a fallback, so 'ze plugin <name>' finds the binary in a development tree. The child reads ZE_PLUGIN_HUB_HOST, ZE_PLUGIN_HUB_PORT, ZE_PLUGIN_HUB_TOKEN, ZE_PLUGIN_CA_PEM and ZE_PLUGIN_NAME from its environment, and connects back over TLS. A value of the form 'ze.<plugin>' names a built-in plugin, which the engine then runs in this process rather than as a fork. run and use are mutually exclusive, and a block that sets both is refused.
  - **timeout** `string`: Startup timeout (e.g., 10s, 1m)
    Bounds a stall in the plugin startup handshake, and does not bound the handshake itself. The handshake runs in stages across every plugin that starts together. The timer expires only when no plugin of that group completes a stage for this long. Write a duration with a unit, such as 10s or 1m: a value with no unit is refused, and so is a negative value. With no value the engine uses the ze.plugin.stage.timeout environment variable, which defaults to 5s. Raise it for a plugin that needs longer to reach its first stage.
  - **use** `string`: Name of a built-in plugin to run in-process (mutually exclusive with run)
    Names a built-in plugin to run in this process instead of a command. The block then behaves like an internal block: no fork, no TLS connect-back, and an in-memory pipe between the engine and the plugin. run and use are mutually exclusive, and a block that sets both is refused. The use leaf of an internal block is checked against the registered plugin names, and this one is not. An unknown name here fails at startup with 'unknown internal plugin'.
- **hub** `container`: Plugin transport and auth configuration
  Sets the TLS listener that plugin processes connect back to, and the outbound connection this daemon makes to a remote hub for its config. With no server block the daemon opens one on 127.0.0.1, with a kernel-chosen port and a random secret. Each plugin process reads that address and a per-plugin token from its environment. Declare a server block when a process the daemon did not start must connect, such as the plugin CLI or a remote managed client. Declare a client block when this daemon takes its config from a remote hub.
  - **client <name>** `list`: Outbound hub connections (managed client mode)
    Each block is an outbound connection to the hub that holds this daemon's config. The daemon dials the first block only, and never dials a second block. The client validates the hub certificate, sends its name and secret, then fetches its config and commits it. A heartbeat every 30 seconds holds the connection open. It reconnects with a delay that grows from 1 second to 60 seconds, and it stops when this instance is no longer marked as managed. The daemon dials nothing here unless it runs as a managed instance with blob-backed config storage.
    - **ca** `string`: Name of the pki ca entry holding the hub certificate authority root.
      Name of a pki ca entry holding the certificate authority root of the hub this client connects to. The client validates the hub certificate chain against that root and refuses any other chain, so it sends no token to a hub it did not authenticate. Export the root from the hub and paste it into a pki ca block on this client. A leaf the hub reissues still validates, because the root is the anchor and not the certificate.
    - **host** `string`: Remote hub address
      The address of the remote hub, as an IP address or a hostname. It joins the port leaf into the dial address, and it also sets the TLS server name the client verifies. The value MUST therefore appear in the hub certificate. A certificate that names a different host is refused, and the client sends its secret to no such hub.
    - **port** `uint16`: Remote hub port
      The TCP port of the remote hub. It MUST equal the port of the hub server block that carries this client's entry. There is no default: a block with no port dials port 0, and no hub listens there.
    - **secret** `string`: Auth token (min 32 chars)
      The token this daemon sends to the hub at authentication. It holds at least 32 characters and the config is refused below that length. It MUST equal the secret of the matching client entry in the hub's server block, so rotate both sides in one change. The CLI masks the value on display, and the committed config file holds it in the clear.
    - **source-address** `ip-address`: Source IP address for outbound hub connections.
      Binds the outbound hub connection to this local IP address. Set it when the route to the hub leaves an interface whose address the hub does not expect. One example is a hub that accepts one management address only. The address MUST exist on this host, because the connection fails when the kernel cannot bind it. With no value the kernel picks the source address of the outgoing route. 'ze doctor' probes the hub through the same source address, so its verdict matches what the daemon does.
  - **server <name>** `list`: Named hub server instances (TLS listeners)
    Each block is one TLS listener. The plugin acceptor binds the first block in configuration order and no other, so a second block exists for the managed clients it names. Every block that carries client entries also starts the managed config server, which needs blob-backed config storage. Give such a block a port of its own. A block whose address the plugin acceptor already binds fails to listen, and 'ze doctor' reports that collision. Set ip and port to the listen address, and secret to the token a connection presents.
    - **certificate** `string`: Name of the pki certificate the managed-client listener on this block serves.
      Name of a pki certificate the managed-client listener on this block serves. An empty name serves a certificate this daemon's own certificate authority issues, and reissues as it ages. Export that authority root with 'show pki local-ca pem' and name it in each client's pki ca block, so a client validates the chain rather than one certificate.
    - **client <name>** `list`: Accepted remote managed clients
      Each entry names a managed client this hub accepts, and the token that client presents. One entry turns the block into a managed config listener. That listener answers a config fetch. It pushes a change notice when the client's stored config is written. The config it serves is the stored file 'client-<name>.conf', so the entry name is what routes a config to a client. Every server block that carries client entries serves one certificate, and a config that names two different ones is refused.
      - **secret** `string`: Per-client auth token (min 32 chars)
        The token this named client presents at authentication. It holds at least 32 characters, and the config is refused below that length with the client name in the error. An entry with no secret is refused as well. Write the same value in the secret leaf of the client block on the remote daemon. This per-client token is checked before the block secret. The CLI masks the value on display, and the committed config file holds it in the clear.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
    - **secret** `string`: Auth token for plugin connections (min 32 chars)
      The token this listener accepts from a connection whose name matches no plugin this daemon started and no client entry in this block. A plugin the daemon starts receives a random per-name token in its environment instead, so no operator copies this value into a plugin. It holds at least 32 characters and the config is refused below that length. With no server block the daemon generates a random secret at each start, which no process outside it can know. The CLI masks the value on display, and the committed config file holds it in the clear.
- **internal <name>** `list`: Built-in plugin running in-process
  Runs a plugin that ships inside the ze binary as a goroutine of this process. There is no fork, no TLS connect-back and no shell command: the engine and the plugin exchange messages over an in-memory pipe. Each block needs a use leaf naming the built-in plugin, and a block that also sets run is refused. Declare a block here to bind a built-in plugin to a peer with 'attach process', or to run one under a name of your own. A plugin that claims a configured address family loads without a block.
  - **use** `string`: Name of a built-in plugin to run in-process
    Names the built-in plugin this block runs. The value MUST be a plugin registered in this binary. A value that is not registered is refused, and the error prints the registered names. Command completion offers that same list. The leaf is required, and a block with no use is refused with 'internal plugin requires use'.

## policy

*Provided by `policy-routes` ([ze-policyroute-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/policyroute/yang/ze-policyroute-cmd.yang), [ze-policyroute-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/policyroute/yang/ze-policyroute-conf.yang))*

Policy routing configuration.

Ze merges every policy into one nftables table named ze_pr. The chain of that table attaches to the prerouting hook at priority -150. A rule marks the packet, and an ip rule then selects the kernel routing table for that mark. A packet that matches no rule keeps the routing decision of the main table.

- **route <name>** `list`: A named policy route applied to ingress interfaces.
  Ze applies the rules of this policy to packets that arrive on the listed interfaces. A policy that lists no interface matches on any ingress interface. Each rule that selects a table or a next-hop gets its own fwmark from range 0x50000 to 0x5FFFF. An ip rule then maps that mark to the table.
  - **interface** `string[]`: Ingress interfaces to match, where a trailing '*' matches by prefix.
    Name one interface, or several. The entries are an OR: Ze installs one nftables rule for each entry, and a packet that arrives on any one of them matches. A trailing * matches by prefix, so the entry l2tp* matches l2tp0 and l2tp1. Each entry keeps its own wildcard state, so one list holds eth0 and l2tp* together. With no interface named, the policy matches every ingress interface.
  - **rule <name>** `list`: Ordered list of match/action rules.
    Ze sorts the rules by the order leaf, lowest first, and it breaks a tie by name. The position of a rule in the config file does not decide its position in the chain. A rule with no order leaf takes 0 and runs first. Each rule becomes one nftables term for each interface the policy names, and one term when it names none. The terms of one rule stay together, so the order leaf still decides which rule the kernel reads first.
    - **from** `container`: Packet match criteria.
      Ze puts every leaf of this block into one nftables rule, so a packet MUST match all of them. An empty from block matches every packet on the interfaces of the policy. Write the protocol leaf beside a port leaf. Ze reads a port from the transport header at a fixed offset and adds no protocol guard. A port leaf alone also reads those two bytes of another L4 header.
      - **destination-address** `string`: Destination IP prefix or @set reference.
        A value that starts with @ names a firewall set, and Ze matches the destination address of the packet against the elements of that set. Any other value MUST carry a prefix length, because Ze parses it as a prefix. 10.0.0.1 is refused at commit, and 10.0.0.1/32 matches one host.
      - **destination-port** `string`: Destination port or port range.
        The syntax is the syntax of source-port: one port, a range written with a hyphen, or a comma-separated list of both, at most 128 entries. Ze reads the destination port at offset 2 of the transport header, so write the protocol leaf beside it.
      - **protocol** `protocol-name`: L4 protocol to match.
        The value set is the one every firewall backend can lower, so a spelling outside it is refused at commit rather than at the next firewall reconcile.
        - `ah`: Match IPsec AH, IP protocol 51.
        - `esp`: Match IPsec ESP, IP protocol 50.
        - `gre`: Match GRE, IP protocol 47.
        - `icmp`: Match ICMP, IP protocol 1.
        - `icmpv6`: Match ICMPv6, IP protocol 58.
        - `ospf`: Match OSPF, IP protocol 89.
        - `sctp`: Match SCTP, IP protocol 132.
        - `tcp`: Match TCP, IP protocol 6.
        - `udp`: Match UDP, IP protocol 17.
        - `vrrp`: Match VRRP, IP protocol 112.
      - **source-address** `string`: Source IP prefix or @set reference.
        A value that starts with @ names a firewall set, and Ze matches the source address of the packet against the elements of that set. Any other value MUST carry a prefix length, because Ze parses it as a prefix. 10.0.0.1 is refused at commit, and 10.0.0.1/32 matches one host.
      - **source-port** `string`: Source port or port range (e.g. '80,443').
        Ze accepts one port, a range written with a hyphen, or a comma-separated list of both, and it holds at most 128 entries. Two entries that overlap or touch are refused at commit, and so is port 0. Ze compiles more than one entry into an anonymous nftables interval set.
      - **tcp-flags** `string`: Comma-separated TCP flags to match (fin, syn, rst, psh, ack, urg).
        Every flag you list MUST be set in the packet. Ze builds the nftables mask from the same list, so a flag you do not list is not read and its value does not matter. Write syn,ack to match a packet that carries both. A name outside the six is refused at commit, and an empty list is refused too.
    - **order** `uint32`: Evaluation order of this rule, lower values first.
