      Evaluation order (lower values first). Rules with equal order are sorted by name. If omitted, defaults to 0.
    - **then** `container`: Action for matching packets.
      The block carries one terminal action: accept, drop, table, or next-hop. Two terminal actions in one rule are refused at commit, and the error names both. tcp-mss is not terminal, so it combines with one of the four. A then block with no terminal action sets no fwmark, so the packet keeps the main table.
      - **accept** `empty`: Skip this policy (packet routes normally).
        Ze emits the nftables accept verdict and sets no fwmark, so the packet keeps the routing decision of the main table. The verdict ends the ze_pr chain, so no later rule of any policy reads that packet. Put an accept rule in front of a table rule to carve an exception out of it.
      - **drop** `empty`: Drop matching packets.
        Ze emits the nftables drop verdict in the ze_pr chain, which runs at the prerouting hook with priority -150. The kernel discards the packet before it makes a routing decision, and it sends the source no ICMP answer.
      - **next-hop** `string`: Redirect matching packets to this next-hop.
        Ze allocates a kernel routing table from range 2000-2999 for this next-hop. Ze then manages the default route, the fwmark, and the ip rule in that table internally.
      - **table** `uint32`: Route matching packets through this kernel routing table.
        Ze routes each matching packet through the kernel routing table with this number. Range 1000-2999 is reserved for ze internal use, which covers the VRF tables and the policy-routing tables Ze allocates.
      - **tcp-mss** `uint16`: Rewrite the TCP MSS option to this value in bytes.
        Ze writes this value into the TCP MSS option, kind 2, of every matching packet, and it does not read the value already there. A packet that carries no MSS option is not changed. The range is 1 to 65535, and 0 is refused at commit. This action is not terminal, so it combines with accept, drop, table, or next-hop in the same rule.

## pppoe

PPPoE access concentrator settings (RFC 2516).

This block with any content in it enables the subsystem. Use 'enabled false' to disable it explicitly. Use 'enabled true' as a filler when no other settings are needed.

- **ac-name** `string`: Access Concentrator Name advertised in PADO (RFC 2516 Section 5.2).
  The default is ze. Ze writes the value into the AC-Name tag, 0x0102, of each discovery reply it builds. A client that hears several concentrators reads this name to pick one.
- **allow-no-auth** `boolean`: Accept a subscriber whose LCP negotiation ends with no Auth-Protocol option.
  The default is false. A client that rejects the configured method is then disconnected, and it is never admitted unauthenticated.
- **auth-method** `enumeration`: PPP Auth-Protocol method the access concentrator advertises in LCP.
  The access concentrator advertises the method in its LCP Configure-Request (RFC 1661 Section 6.2), for every subscriber that completes PPPoE discovery. The auth handler verifies the credential (l2tp-auth-local or l2tp-auth-radius). The default requires CHAP-MD5 (RFC 1994). Set it to none only together with allow-no-auth true.
  - `chap-md5`: Advertise CHAP with the MD5 algorithm (RFC 1994), the default.
  - `ms-chap-v2`: Advertise MS-CHAP-V2 (RFC 2759).
  - `none`: Advertise no Auth-Protocol, so the session opens with no PPP authentication phase.
  - `pap`: Advertise PAP (RFC 1334), which carries the password in clear text.
- **cookie-timeout** `uint16`: AC-Cookie validity duration in seconds. Cookies older than this are rejected in PADR validation.
  The default is 5 seconds and the range is 1 to 300. The cookie is 20 bytes: 16 bytes of a truncated HMAC-SHA256 over the two MAC addresses, and 4 bytes of Unix timestamp. Each interface holds its own random key, so a cookie of one interface never verifies on another.
- **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the PPPoE subsystem.
  The default is true when the pppoe block is present. Set it to false to disable the subsystem.
- **interface <name>** `list`: Access interfaces on which PPPoE discovery listens.
  Each interface has an independent session ID space.
  - **max-sessions** `uint16`: Per-interface session limit. Defaults to the global max-sessions when unset.
    Ze takes the global max-sessions when this leaf is absent or 0. The session identifiers come from a bitmap over the 16-bit space, and identifier 0 is reserved. A PADR that arrives at the limit gets no session, and Ze reports that the maximum is reached.
  - **max-sessions-per-mac** `uint16`: Per-interface override for max-sessions-per-mac. Defaults to the global value when unset.
    Ze takes the global max-sessions-per-mac when this leaf is absent or 0. A PADR from a MAC already at the cap gets a PADS carrying an error tag and session ID 0x0000 instead of a new session.
  - **service-name** `string[]`: Per-interface Service-Name filter. Overrides the global service-name list when set.
    Ze answers a PADI whose Service-Name tag holds a value of this list, and it answers a PADI whose tag is empty. A PADI naming any other service gets no PADO. An empty list here takes the global list, and an empty global list accepts every Service-Name.
- **max-sessions** `uint16`: Maximum concurrent PPPoE sessions per interface.
  The 16-bit session ID range limits the count to 1 through 65535.
- **max-sessions-per-mac** `uint16`: Maximum concurrent sessions one subscriber MAC address may hold.
  The default is 8 and the range is 1 to 65535. RFC 2516 places no limit on concurrent sessions from one peer MAC, so this bounds replay rather than a legitimate multi-session client: a PADR from a MAC already at the cap gets a PADS carrying an error tag and session ID 0x0000 instead of a new session. The per-interface max-sessions-per-mac overrides this value.
- **padi-rate-limit** `uint16`: Maximum PADI packets accepted per second on one interface.
  The default is 100 and the range is 1 to 10000. Ze counts the PADI packets of one interface inside a one-second window and discards every packet over the count. Ze also discards a second PADI from one source MAC address inside the same second. The range starts at 1, so no configuration turns the limiter off.
- **service-name** `string[]`: Accepted Service-Name values (RFC 2516 Section 5.1).
  An empty list accepts any Service-Name. The per-interface service-name list overrides this global list.

## redistribute

*Provided by `redistribute-orchestrator`*

Route redistribution between protocols.

Each destination protocol has its own container that holds the import rules. To add a destination protocol, add a key here.

- **destination <protocol>** `list`: Destination protocol for redistributed routes.
  Each entry names a consumer that registered itself, for example bgp or ospf.
  - **import <source>** `list`: Import routes from a source into this destination.
    If the family leaf-list is empty, Ze imports every family.
    - **family** `string[]`: Address families Ze imports from this source.
      An empty leaf-list imports every family.
    - **tag** `uint32`: Import only the routes that carry this route tag.
      The route tag is the value the source protocol attached to the route, for example the tag leaf of a static route. A rule that names a tag imports the routes carrying exactly that value and rejects the others. A rule with no tag leaf imports every route from the source, whatever tag it carries. The value 0 is a tag like any other: a route with no tag carries 0, so tag 0 imports the untagged routes alone.

## rib

*Provided by `rib` ([ze-rib-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/sysrib/yang/ze-rib-conf.yang))*

System RIB configuration.

The system RIB takes the best route each protocol offers and selects one system best for each prefix. The FIB plugins program that winner into the kernel with netlink, into VPP, or into a P4 switch. The kernel FIB carries no administrative distance field, so the ranking happens here and only the winner reaches netlink. The distance container below is the one declaration of every protocol's administrative distance. The fib-withhold leaf-list beside it names the protocols whose winners are not programmed. Routes reach the system RIB from the protocols, never from this block.

- **distance** `container`: Administrative distance per protocol.
  Administrative distance ranks one protocol against another for the same prefix, and the lower value wins. It is NOT an IGP metric and NOT the IGP distance to a next hop: those measure a path, this ranks the protocol that offered it. RFC 4271 mandates no values; these follow the Cisco and Juniper convention. This container is the only place any protocol's distance is declared, and every protocol takes its value from here whether or not you write the block.
  - **connected** `uint8`: Directly connected networks.
    A connected route is the prefix an interface address covers. The default 0 is the best distance a route can hold, so a connected route wins the prefix against every protocol that carries a higher value. This is the only distance leaf whose range starts at 0. The other five start at 1. Raise it above another protocol's distance to let that protocol win the same prefix. The value applies whether or not you write the rib block, because sysrib resolves every protocol from these schema defaults when it starts.
  - **ebgp** `uint8`: External BGP routes.
    An eBGP route comes from a peer in another autonomous system. The default 20 ranks eBGP above every IGP declared here and below a static route. The range is 1 to 255. The BGP RIB plugin stamps this value on each path it inserts. The Loc-RIB ranks the paths on what it stamped, so the value decides selection before sysrib sees the route. The seam that carries it is process-global: a BGP RIB running in a forked plugin process keeps its own bootstrap 20 and nothing reports that.
  - **ibgp** `uint8`: Internal BGP routes.
    An iBGP route comes from a peer in the same autonomous system. The default 200 is the highest of the six declared here, so an iBGP route loses the prefix to any other protocol that holds it. The range is 1 to 255. The BGP RIB plugin stamps this value on each path it inserts, and its bootstrap 200 applies until sysrib publishes the declaration. The eBGP distance is a separate leaf, so the two BGP classes rank apart.
  - **isis** `uint8`: IS-IS routes.
    The default 115 ranks IS-IS below OSPF and above iBGP. The range is 1 to 255. The IS-IS SPF installer stamps this value on each path it puts in the Loc-RIB, and its bootstrap 115 applies until sysrib publishes the declaration. One value covers level 1 and level 2: Ze declares no separate distance for each level.
  - **ospf** `uint8`: OSPF routes.
    The default 110 ranks OSPF below eBGP and above IS-IS. The range is 1 to 255. The OSPF SPF installer stamps this value on each path it puts in the Loc-RIB, and its bootstrap 110 applies until sysrib publishes the declaration. One value covers every OSPF route: Ze declares no separate distance for an external LSA.
  - **static** `uint8`: Static routes.
    A static route is one the operator wrote under the static configuration. The default 10 ranks a static route above every dynamic protocol declared here and below a connected route. The range is 1 to 255. sysrib applies the value to each route that arrives under the protocol name static. Raise it to more than 20 to let an eBGP route win the same prefix.
- **fib-withhold** `string[]`: Protocols whose selected routes are not programmed into the FIB. An empty list programs all.
  This list names the protocols Ze does not program. Selection is unchanged: the system RIB ranks the candidates for each prefix on administrative distance and picks one winner. A winner from a protocol named here stays in the RIB, `show rib` reports it, redistribution can offer it to another protocol, and the protocol's own event stream still carries it. Ze declines the write to the kernel, to VPP or to a P4 switch. It holds the prefix off `system-rib/best-change`, the stream every FIB writer reads, so the list applies to every FIB. Ze also releases the next-hop tracking for the prefix, so `show nexthop-table` stops listing it under its next-hop. An empty list withholds nothing, which is the behavior of a router that says nothing here. Withholding is one of the reasons a selected route is not programmed: a route the operating system installs, and a route whose SRv6 SID reaches nothing, are not written either. The values are the protocol names this build registered: the editor completes them, and a name nothing registered is refused at commit.

## routing-table

*Provided by `routing-table` ([ze-routing-table-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/routingtable/yang/ze-routing-table-conf.yang))*

Named routing table definitions. Each entry maps a name to a kernel routing table ID.

Ze builds one registry from these entries, and a static route or a policy route resolves its table name against that registry. The name default is built-in and resolves to table 0, so no entry can carry that name.

- **table <name>** `list`: A named routing table.
  One entry maps one name to one kernel table identifier. Ze refuses an entry named default, and refuses an entry with no id. Two entries CAN carry the same identifier, because the registry keys on the name.
  - **id** `uint32`: Kernel routing table ID. Reserved IDs excluded: 0 (use 'default'), 253-255 (kernel reserved).
    The leaf is mandatory. The range refuses 0 and 253 to 255, because 253 is the kernel default table, 254 is the main table and 255 is the local table. Ze also refuses an identifier this build cannot program through netlink without truncation.

## rsvp-te

*Provided by `rsvp-te-rawsock` ([ze-rsvp-te-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/rsvpte/yang/ze-rsvp-te-cmd.yang), [ze-rsvp-te-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/rsvpte/yang/ze-rsvp-te-conf.yang))*

RSVP-TE traffic engineering configuration

RSVP-TE traffic engineering configuration. Signaling is IPv4 only. Without a router-id the engine stays idle, and no tunnel and no bypass signals. Ze has no IGP and no CSPF, so every path is given as an explicit route.

- **bypass <name>** `list`: Facility-backup bypass LSP from this PLR to a merge point (RFC 4090 Section 3.2).
  Facility-backup bypass LSP (RFC 4090 Section 3.2): an LSP from this PLR to a merge point, explicitly routed to avoid the protected resource. A protected transit LSP is redirected onto this bypass on a local failure. The redirected LSP is one whose next hop (link protection) or next-next hop (node protection) is this bypass's merge point. The route is explicit because Ze has no IGP and no CSPF to compute a backup path.
  - **explicit-route <index>** `list`: Bypass path hops (must avoid the protected resource)
    Bypass path hops. The route has to avoid the link or the node this bypass protects, because a backup that crosses the protected resource fails with it. Ze has no IGP and no CSPF, so the operator gives the hops. The hops are ordered by the numeric index key.
    - **address** `string`: Hop address (IPv4 prefix)
      Hop address, given as an IPv4 prefix such as 10.0.0.8/30. A commit that gives a bare address with no prefix length is rejected. The address and the prefix length both go into the ERO IPv4 prefix subobject of the bypass PATH.
    - **type** `enumeration`: Hop type (strict or loose)
      Hop type. strict is the default and asks that the previous hop reaches this one directly. loose sets the L bit of the ERO subobject and permits other hops between them. Ze reads any value other than loose as strict.
      - `loose`: Set the L bit of the ERO subobject and permit other hops between them.
      - `strict`: The previous hop must reach this one directly, with no hop between them.
  - **merge-point** `string`: Merge point address (IPv4) where this bypass rejoins the protected LSPs.
    Merge point address (IPv4). The address is the protected LSPs' next hop (link protection) or next-next hop (node protection), where this bypass rejoins them.
  - **node-protection** `boolean`: This bypass merges at a next-next hop, so it gives node protection
    This bypass merges at a next-next hop, so it gives node protection. A protected LSP that asked for node protection is armed onto a bypass only when this leaf is true. Left false, the bypass protects the link alone, and a node-protection request finds no bypass at this PLR.
- **interface <name>** `list`: Per-interface RSVP-TE configuration
  Per-interface RSVP-TE configuration. Bandwidth admission control accounts each reservation against one entry of this list. An interface that no entry names carries no limit, so every reservation that resolves onto it is admitted.
  - **address** `string`: Local link prefix in IPv4 CIDR form, for example 10.0.0.4/30.
    Local link prefix (IPv4 CIDR, for example 10.0.0.4/30). When more than one interface is configured, admission control maps an LSP to this interface. The map applies when the neighbor address falls within the prefix.
  - **max-bandwidth** `string`: Maximum link bandwidth (bps)
    Maximum link bandwidth. The value is reported by 'show rsvp-te interface' and it is not an admission limit. Only max-reservable-bandwidth bounds what admission control accepts.
  - **max-reservable-bandwidth** `string`: Maximum reservable bandwidth (bps)
    Maximum reservable bandwidth. Admission control denies a reservation when the accounted total plus the new request is more than this value. A shared-explicit session counts its largest LSP once rather than the sum, so a make-before-break reroute is not double-counted. Left unset, the limit is 0 and every tunnel that requests bandwidth on this interface is denied.
- **refresh-multiplier** `uint8`: Number of missed refreshes before state cleanup
  Number of missed refreshes before state cleanup, 1 to 255, default 3. State expires when the last refresh is older than refresh-period multiplied by this number, which is 90 seconds at the defaults. Expiry releases the reserved bandwidth, the MPLS forwarding entry and the label, then sends an lsp-down event.
- **refresh-period** `uint16`: PATH/RESV refresh interval (RFC 2205 soft-state)
  PATH and RESV refresh interval, 1 to 65535 seconds, default 30. The same 65535-second ceiling caps the period a neighbor advertises in TIME_VALUES. A neighbor therefore cannot hold state alive for years. A reload reaches the running LSPs at the next refresh tick.
- **router-id** `string`: Router identifier (IPv4 address format)
  Router identifier, in IPv4 address format. A commit that gives an IPv6 address is rejected. The address is the PATH sender address, the address the transport socket binds, and the seed of the session key each tunnel and bypass derives. A change after startup is logged and refused, and the running router-id stays in use until the daemon restarts.
- **tunnel <name>** `list`: RSVP-TE LSP tunnel definition
  RSVP-TE LSP tunnel definition. Each entry signals a PATH from the local router-id toward destination. A commit that changes only the explicit route starts a make-before-break reroute (RFC 3209 Section 6.1) and leaves the live tunnel in place.
  - **bandwidth** `string`: Requested bandwidth (bps)
    Requested bandwidth. The value fills the SENDER_TSPEC token rate, token bucket and peak rate. Admission control charges it against the interface entry the LSP neighbor resolves onto, and it denies the LSP when the charge is more than max-reservable-bandwidth.
  - **destination** `string`: Tunnel endpoint (IPv4 address)
    Tunnel endpoint, an IPv4 address. The address is the SESSION tunnel endpoint the PATH carries. A node whose own router-id equals this address acts as the egress and answers with a RESV. Every other node on the path acts as a transit node.
  - **explicit-route <index>** `list`: Explicit route hops
    Explicit route hops. The list becomes the ERO object the PATH carries (RFC 3209 Section 4.3). Ze has no IGP and no CSPF, so the operator gives every hop. A tunnel with no hop here is signaled with no ERO object. A commit that changes the list starts a make-before-break reroute.
    - **address** `string`: Hop address (IPv4 prefix)
      Hop address, given as an IPv4 prefix such as 10.0.0.4/30. A commit that gives a bare address with no prefix length is rejected. The address and the prefix length both go into the ERO IPv4 prefix subobject.
    - **type** `enumeration`: Hop type (strict or loose)
      Hop type. strict is the default and asks that the previous hop reaches this one directly. loose sets the L bit of the ERO subobject and permits other hops between them. Ze reads any value other than loose as strict.
      - `loose`: Set the L bit of the ERO subobject and permit other hops between them.
      - `strict`: The previous hop must reach this one directly, with no hop between them.
  - **fast-reroute** `container`: Fast Reroute (RFC 4090) local protection for this LSP
    Fast Reroute (RFC 4090) local protection for this LSP. The container has presence. Absent, the head-end PATH carries no SESSION_ATTRIBUTE and no FAST_REROUTE object, and no transit PLR arms a backup. Present, it also puts setup-priority, hold-priority and the tunnel name on the wire.
    - **backup** `enumeration`: Backup method: facility (one bypass protects many LSPs) or one-to-one (a detour per LSP)
      Backup method. facility is the default and asks each PLR for one bypass LSP that protects many LSPs (RFC 4090 Section 3.2). one-to-one asks for one detour per LSP (Section 3.1). As a PLR, Ze arms only a facility bypass from its own bypass list. Ze signals a one-to-one request and builds no detour for it.
      - `facility`: Ask each PLR for one bypass LSP that protects many LSPs (RFC 4090 Section 3.2).
      - `one-to-one`: Ask for one detour per LSP (RFC 4090 Section 3.1), which Ze signals and never builds.
    - **bandwidth-protection** `boolean`: Request a backup that guarantees the reserved bandwidth
      Request a backup that guarantees the reserved bandwidth. Ze sets the bandwidth-protection flag in SESSION_ATTRIBUTE (RFC 4090 Section 4.3) and records it in the RESV route object. Ze's own bypass selection does not compare the bypass bandwidth, so the flag is a request to the PLR downstream.
    - **hop-limit** `uint8`: Maximum number of hops the backup path can take
      Maximum number of hops the backup path can take, 0 to 255, default 16. The value goes into the FAST_REROUTE object (RFC 4090 Section 4.1) for the PLR that computes the backup. A Ze facility bypass is routed by its own explicit-route list, so this limit does not shorten it.
    - **node-protection** `boolean`: Request NNHOP (node) protection rather than NHOP (link) protection
      Request NNHOP (node) protection rather than NHOP (link) protection. Ze sets the node-protection flag in SESSION_ATTRIBUTE (RFC 4090 Section 4.3). As a PLR, Ze then arms only a bypass whose merge point is the next-next hop of the explicit route. That bypass also has to set its own node-protection leaf. With no such bypass, the LSP gets no protection.
  - **hold-priority** `uint8`: Hold priority (0 = highest)
    Hold priority, where 0 is the highest and 7 is the default. It states how hard this LSP holds its reservation against a setup of higher priority. Ze signals it beside setup-priority, and only for a tunnel that declares fast-reroute.
  - **setup-priority** `uint8`: Setup priority (0 = highest)
    Setup priority, where 0 is the highest and 7 is the default. Ze signals the value in the SESSION_ATTRIBUTE and FAST_REROUTE objects, and it adds both objects only for a tunnel that declares fast-reroute. Ze preempts no LSP of its own, so the priority acts on the routers downstream.
  - **tunnel-id** `uint16`: Tunnel identifier
    Tunnel identifier, the part of the SESSION that separates this LSP from another to the same endpoint. Ze reserves 61440 to 65535 for the bypass LSPs it derives from a bypass name, and a commit that puts a tunnel in that range is rejected.

## service

*Provided by `as112` ([ze-as112-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/as112/yang/ze-as112-cmd.yang), [ze-as112-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/as112/yang/ze-as112-conf.yang)); `dhcpserver` ([ze-dhcp-server-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/dhcpserver/yang/ze-dhcp-server-conf.yang)); `geodns` ([ze-geodns-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/geodns/yang/ze-geodns-cmd.yang), [ze-geodns-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/geodns/yang/ze-geodns-conf.yang)); `imageserver` ([ze-image-server-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/imageserver/yang/ze-image-server-conf.yang)); `tftpserver` ([ze-tftp-server-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/tftpserver/yang/ze-tftp-server-conf.yang))*

Service settings.

The container holds the settings of each service Ze runs, and the as112 container under it configures the AS112 node.

- **as112** `container`: AS112 anycast DNS node.
  The container holds the enable switch, the address family, the node identification strings, the access list, the BGP settings and the secure listeners.
  - **address-family** `enumeration`: Restrict the service to one address family.
    RFC 7534 Section 3.4 and RFC 7535 Section 3.1 give the single-stack option. The anycast addresses themselves are fixed constants, and an operator never types one.
    - `both`: Serve on both IPv4 and IPv6 anycast addresses. This is the default.
    - `ipv4-only`: Serve on the two IPv4 anycast addresses only.
    - `ipv6-only`: Serve on the two IPv6 anycast addresses only.
  - **allow-from** `ip-prefix[]`: Client-source access list of the queries the node answers.
    An empty list, which is the default, answers every source and matches the standard AS112 public-sink behavior. With one prefix or more, the node answers a query only when its source IP is inside one of those prefixes. It drops every other query and sends no response. A loopback source and an on-box source are always permitted, whatever this list holds, so the 'request as112 healthcheck' probe is never blocked. A set list makes the node non-public. That is correct for a local-use mirror, and wrong for an AS112 contributor the whole internet reaches.
  - **asn** `asn`: Origin AS the AS112 covering prefixes carry when redistributed into BGP.
    The redistribute statement is `redistribute { destination bgp { import as112 } }`. The default is the well-known AS112 number 112 (RFC 7534 Section 3.2), because the redistribute source models an AS112 virtual router. Set an operator ASN, or an RFC 6996 private-use ASN, to originate under a coordinated AS or a local-use AS instead. Ze ignores this leaf unless 'import as112' is configured under redistribute.
  - **community** `string[]`: BGP communities attached to the redistributed AS112 covering prefixes.
    The leaf takes an AA:NN standard community (RFC 1997) and a well-known name such as no-export or nopeer (RFC 3765). Those are the values RFC 7534 Section 3.4 recommends to restrict AS112 route propagation. The type is 'string' rather than the AA:NN-only ze-types community pattern, so a well-known name is accepted. The canonical community parser validates every value at config time. Ze ignores this leaf unless 'import as112' is configured under redistribute.
  - **doh** `container`: DNS-over-HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).
    The listener reuses the certificate material of the tls container. It binds the fixed anycast addresses and the loopback address on 'listen-port', at 'path'.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the DNS-over-HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).
      The default is false. Ze binds DoH on every IP the cleartext listeners use, on listen-port, at path. The listener drives the same handler as cleartext DNS, so allow-from answers a DoH client exactly as it answers a UDP client. A query the handler refuses gets HTTP 403.
    - **listen-port** `port`: TCP port for the DoH HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).
      The default is 443, and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze refuses a port of 0. A GET carries the query base64url-encoded in the dns parameter, and a POST carries it in an application/dns-message body of 65535 bytes at most.
    - **path** `string`: HTTP request path the DoH endpoint answers on.
      RFC 8484 defines the URI Template. The default path is /dns-query.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the AS112 anycast DNS node.
    The AS112 node does not start while this leaf is false, and false is the default.
  - **facility** `string`: Facility name in the HOSTNAME.AS112.NET/ARPA TXT answers.
    The facility name is the name of the site, for example 'Example Datacenter'. It is surfaced beside the location.
  - **hostname** `string`: Node identification string in the HOSTNAME.AS112.NET/ARPA TXT answers.
    RFC 7534 Section 3.5 defines those answers. The string tells an operator which anycast instance answered a query. An empty value omits the TXT string.
  - **ipv4-anycast-listener <name>** `list`: Presence-only anchor for port 53 on the fixed IPv4 anycast addresses.
    as112 always occupies port 53 on its fixed IPv4 anycast addresses while it is enabled. The Go-level default, RegisterListenerDefault, fills in the representative address, because no operator-facing command populates this list.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **ipv6-anycast-listener <name>** `list`: Presence-only anchor for port 53 on the fixed IPv6 anycast addresses.
    as112 always occupies port 53 on its fixed IPv6 anycast addresses while it is enabled.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **location** `string`: City and country in the HOSTNAME.AS112.NET/ARPA TXT answers.
    The location is surfaced beside the facility, for example 'London, UK'.
  - **tls** `container`: DNS-over-TLS listener, and the certificate material it shares with DoH.
    RFC 7858 defines DNS-over-TLS (DoT). When it is enabled, the DoT listener binds the fixed anycast addresses and the loopback address on 'listen-port'. When cert-file and key-file are both unset, Ze uses an ephemeral self-signed certificate, which a strict client cannot validate. Supply an operator PEM file for a node the public trusts.
    - **cert-file** `string`: Path to the PEM server certificate presented on DoT and DoH.
      When this leaf and key-file are both unset, Ze uses an ephemeral self-signed certificate.
    - **certificate** `string`: Name of the PKI store certificate served on DoT and DoH.
      The listeners send the leaf certificate and every intermediate certificate the store entry holds. This leaf excludes cert-file and key-file. Setting both is a configuration error. The PKI store lives in the hub process, so a geodns plugin or an as112 plugin started as an external process cannot resolve the name. The secure listeners then do not start, and Ze logs the error. Cleartext DNS still runs.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the DNS-over-TLS listener (RFC 7858).
      The default is false. Ze binds DoT on every IP the cleartext listeners use, on listen-port. DoT is TCP only, because RFC 7858 Section 3.1 defines no UDP counterpart. When the TLS material fails to load, Ze starts no secure listener and the cleartext listeners keep running.
    - **key-file** `string`: Path to the PEM private key matching cert-file. Must be set together with cert-file.
      Ze reads cert-file and key-file on each apply, so a rotated pair reaches the listener without a restart. One of the two alone stops the secure listeners with an error, and the cleartext listeners keep running. The certificate leaf names a PKI store entry instead, and Ze refuses a config that writes both sources.
    - **listen-port** `port`: TCP port for the DoT listener.
      The RFC 7858 well-known 'domain-s' port is 853.
  - **watchdog** `boolean`: Announce the covering prefixes only while the node serves DNS.
    RFC 7534 Section 3.3 states that a node does not advertise the service prefix while the name server is not running. With true, which is the default, Ze announces the covering prefixes only while the as112 node serves. Ze withdraws them when serving is lost, when the service is disabled, and when the node shuts down. With false, Ze announces as soon as the node is enabled and imported, with no serving-state gate. Ze ignores this leaf unless 'import as112' is configured under redistribute.
- **dhcp-server** `container`: DHCP server settings
  DHCP server settings. Ze speaks DHCPv4 only (RFC 2131 and RFC 2132), so every address leaf under this container is IPv4. The server binds one listener for each name in listen-interface, and every listener answers for every configured subnet.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable DHCP server
    Enable the DHCP server. Left false, the plugin still parses and validates the config, and it binds no socket and builds no handler. A commit that sets it true rebuilds one handler for each subnet and binds the listeners again.
  - **listen-interface** `string[]`: Interfaces to serve DHCP on
    Interfaces to serve DHCP on. Ze binds one UDP listener for each name in the list. A name that fails to bind is logged as an error and skipped. When no name binds, the server logs that it is not serving and answers nothing.
  - **pxe** `container`: PXE boot server settings (RFC 4578)
    PXE boot server settings (RFC 4578). Ze adds these options only when the client vendor class in option 60 starts with PXEClient:. An ordinary DHCP client sees none of them. With pxe enabled, a commit also requires tftp-server, bootfile-bios and bootfile-uefi.
    - **boot-script-url** `string`: HTTP URL for iPXE boot script (sent as option 67 to iPXE clients)
      HTTP URL for the iPXE boot script. Ze sends it as option 67 only to a client whose user class in option 77 starts with iPXE. That reply carries option 60 and option 67 alone, so the iPXE client receives no option 66, no option 43 and no siaddr. A commit rejects a URL that does not start with http:// or https://, and one longer than 255 characters.
    - **bootfile-bios** `string`: Boot file path for BIOS clients (option 67)
      Boot file path for BIOS clients, sent as option 67. Ze sends it whenever the first client architecture in option 93 is any value other than 7 (RFC 4578 Section 2.1). An absent or malformed option 93 reads as architecture 0, which is BIOS, so this path is the fallback.
    - **bootfile-uefi** `string`: Boot file path for UEFI clients (option 67)
      Boot file path for UEFI clients, sent as option 67. Ze sends it only when the first client architecture in option 93 is 7, which is UEFI x64 (RFC 4578 Section 2.1). Every other architecture receives bootfile-bios.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable PXE boot option injection
      Enable PXE boot option injection. Set true, a commit also requires tftp-server, bootfile-bios and bootfile-uefi, and it names the missing one. Left false, Ze adds no PXE option even for a client that identifies itself as PXEClient.
    - **tftp-server** `string`: TFTP server IP address for PXE boot (option 66, siaddr)
      TFTP server IP address for PXE boot. Ze writes the address into the siaddr field of the reply (RFC 2131 Section 4.3.1) and its text form into option 66 (RFC 2132 Section 9.9). The address has to be IPv4. An iPXE client receives neither, because boot-script-url answers it instead.
  - **shared-network <name>** `list`: Named network grouping of subnets
    Named network grouping of subnets. The name is a label for the operator, and Ze puts it on no packet. Ze sorts the groups by name and builds one handler for each subnet in that order. A request is answered by the first handler that accepts it.
    - **subnet <prefix>** `list`: Subnet with address pool and options
      Subnet with address pool and options. Each subnet becomes one handler with its own address pool and lease table. A request that carries no relay address, no client address and no requested address matches every subnet. The first handler with a free address answers it.
      - **default-router** `string`: Default gateway address (option 3)
        Default gateway address, sent as option 3. Ze also uses it as the DHCP server identifier of this subnet, in option 54. With no default-router the identifier falls back to the start address of the first range, and then to the network address of the prefix. A REQUEST that names a different server identifier is left unanswered.
      - **dns-server** `string[]`: DNS server addresses (option 6)
        DNS server addresses, sent as option 6. Write them in preference order, because Ze sends them in the order it reads them. A commit rejects more than 63 addresses, which is what one DHCP option holds, and it rejects an address that is not IPv4.
      - **domain-name** `string`: Domain name for clients (option 15)
        Domain name for clients, sent as option 15. Ze sends the string as it is written. A commit rejects a value longer than 255 characters, which is the most one DHCP option holds.
      - **lease-time** `uint32`: Lease duration in seconds
        Lease duration in seconds, 60 to 604800, default 86400. Ze sends it as option 51. It also sends the renewal time T1 as half of it, and the rebinding time T2 as seven eighths of it. RFC 2131 Section 4.4.5 states those two fractions. The lease table drops a binding after the same time.
      - **range <name>** `list`: Named dynamic address pool range
        Named dynamic address pool range. A subnet holds 10 ranges at most. Ze sorts them by start address and rejects a commit where two of them overlap. Ze allocates in that order.
        - **start** `string`: First allocatable address
          First allocatable address, and the address is allocatable. It has to fall inside the subnet prefix, and it has to be less than or equal to stop. A commit names which of the two rules it broke.
        - **stop** `string`: Last allocatable address
          Last allocatable address, and the address is allocatable. It has to fall inside the subnet prefix. A range of one address is written with the same value in start and stop.
      - **static-mapping <name>** `list`: Static MAC-to-IP binding
        Static MAC-to-IP binding. Ze answers a client whose MAC address matches with the mapped address, and it never consults the dynamic pool for that client. A mapped address that falls inside a range is marked in the pool, so no other client is offered it.
        - **ip-address** `string`: Fixed IP address for this client
          Fixed IP address for this client. It has to fall inside the subnet prefix, and a commit rejects an address outside it. The address does not have to fall inside a range. When it does, Ze marks it allocated so the dynamic pool never offers it to another client.
        - **mac-address** `string`: Client MAC address (xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx)
          Client MAC address. Ze reads the colon form aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, the hyphen form and the dotted form. Ze matches the value against the client hardware address of the request. A mapping with no mac-address is rejected at commit.
- **geodns** `container`: GeoDNS server: per-source-IP DNS answers
  GeoDNS answers a query from the client address rather than from the name alone. A `source` entry maps a client prefix to a `host-set`, and the longest prefix that holds the client address wins. The same name can then answer a different address to each client. Ze is authoritative for the `zone` entries only, and it serves no AXFR.
  - **client-ip-source** `enumeration`: Where the client IP used for source selection is read from
    edns0-then-packet, the default, reads the address from the EDNS0 client-subnet option (RFC 7871) and falls back to the packet source address. packet ignores the option and always reads the packet source. edns0 reads only the option. A query with no option then matches no `source` prefix, so a name the zone owns draws an empty NOERROR answer.
    - `edns0`: Use only the EDNS0 client-subnet option (RFC 7871); no answer without it
    - `edns0-then-packet`: Prefer EDNS0 client-subnet, fall back to the packet source IP
    - `packet`: Use the UDP/TCP packet source IP
  - **default-ttl** `uint32`: Default record TTL in seconds when a host omits its own.
    Default record TTL (seconds) when a host omits its own. The range is 1 to 2147483647 (RFC 2181 section 8). A zero default is not allowed.
  - **doh** `container`: DNS-over-HTTPS listener (DoH, RFC 8484).
    DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH, RFC 8484) listener. It reuses the tls container's certificate material. It binds the configured listener IPs on 'listen-port' at 'path'.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the DNS-over-HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).
      The default is false, so geodns binds no DNS-over-HTTPS listener. A true value binds every `listener` IP on `listen-port` at `path`. DoH takes the certificate material of the `tls` container, so it needs no `tls/enabled`. A certificate that does not load starts no secure listener, and the cleartext listeners stay bound.
    - **listen-port** `port`: TCP port for the DoH HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).
      The DoH listener binds this TCP port on every `listener` IP. A commit with the value 0 is refused. Move the port when a web server already holds 443 on the same address, because the second bind of one address and port fails.
    - **path** `string`: HTTP request path the DoH endpoint answers on (RFC 8484 URI Template); defaults to /dns-query.
      The DoH endpoint answers this path alone. An empty value keeps the default /dns-query. RFC 8484 section 3 states that 'The DoH client is configured with a URI Template [RFC6570]'. A client MUST therefore be told a path that is not the default.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the GeoDNS server
    The default is false, so geodns binds no listener and answers no query. A true value binds each `listener` entry for UDP and TCP, and it binds the DoT and DoH listeners that are enabled. A false value unbinds every listener.
  - **host-set <name>** `list`: Named, reusable set of host records; referenced by source entries
    A host set is one answer set. Ze picks the set for a query from the client address, through the `source` prefix that matches it. One set can serve several source prefixes. The same hostname can appear in several sets with a different address in each. That is what makes the answer depend on the client.
    - **host <name>** `list`: A hostname and its records
      One entry holds one name and the records Ze answers for it inside this set. A commit is refused when the entry carries no address and `type` is not SRV. It is also refused when `type` and the address family disagree.
      - **address** `ip-address[]`: One or more A/AAAA addresses (v4 => A, v6 => AAAA when type omitted)
        Each entry becomes one A record or one AAAA record for the host, and one query answers all of them. Ze refuses the commit for a host with no entry here, unless `type` is SRV.
      - **srv** `container`: SRV record fields (when type is SRV)
        Ze reads this container only when `type` is SRV. All four leaves are then required, and a commit that omits one is refused with 'need priority weight port target'. An SRV host answers one record, and `address` on it is ignored.
        - **port** `uint16`: SRV port
          The value is the TCP or UDP port the service listens on at `target`. The range is 0 to 65535. Ze copies the number into the record and checks nothing about it.
        - **priority** `uint16`: SRV priority
          RFC 2782 states that 'A client MUST attempt to contact the target host with the lowest-numbered priority it can reach'. That text is in the section 'The format of the SRV RR'. Targets that share a priority are ordered by `weight`. The range is 0 to 65535.
        - **target** `string`: SRV target hostname
          The value is the hostname that runs the service. Ze adds the trailing dot when the value has none. A commit is refused when the name breaks the length bounds RFC 1035 sets. Ze adds no address record for the target, so a client resolves that name in a second query.
        - **weight** `uint16`: SRV weight
          RFC 2782, 'The format of the SRV RR', calls the weight 'a relative weight for entries with the same priority'. The same text states that 'Larger weights SHOULD be given a proportionately higher probability of being selected'. Use 0 when one target has no selection to do. The range is 0 to 65535.
      - **ttl** `uint32`: Record TTL; defaults to default-ttl when unset
        The value is the TTL in seconds of every record of this host. An unset leaf takes `default-ttl`. 0 is permitted here and refused on `default-ttl`, and it asks a resolver to cache the answer for no time. The range is the TTL range RFC 2181 section 8 sets.
      - **type** `enumeration`: Record type; omit to auto-detect A vs AAAA per address
        An unset leaf reads each `address` entry on its own, and answers A for an IPv4 address and AAAA for an IPv6 address. A refuses the commit for an IPv6 address, and AAAA refuses it for an IPv4 address. SRV reads the `srv` container and ignores `address`.
        - `A`: Answer an A record for each address, and refuse an IPv6 address at commit.
        - `AAAA`: Answer an AAAA record for each address, and refuse an IPv4 address at commit.
        - `SRV`: Answer an SRV record from the srv container, and ignore the address list.
  - **listener <name>** `list`: UDP and TCP listen endpoints for geodns.
    UDP+TCP listen endpoints. Each named entry binds one IP (IPv4 or IPv6) and one port. Repeat the same port for a dual-stack pair. Ze defaults to 127.0.0.1:5300 and ::1:5300 when no entry is configured. The ze:listener marking enables config-time port-conflict detection across services.
    - **ip** `ip-address`: Listen IP address
      The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
    - **port** `listener-port`: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned
      The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses.
  - **nameserver** `ipv4-address[]`: Nameserver IPv4 addresses; ns1..nsN.<zone> A glue is synthesised (max 9)
    Ze builds one NS record for each entry, named ns1.<zone> to nsN.<zone> in list order, and one A glue record beside it. The glue name is synthesized and never configured. A commit is refused when a zone is long enough to make nsN.<zone> break the length bounds RFC 1035 sets. The records go in the Answer of an NS query and in the Authority of every other answer.
  - **soa** `container`: SOA record fields (synthesised; geodns serves no AXFR)
    Ze builds the SOA record of each zone from these leaves. It serves no AXFR, so no secondary acts on `refresh`, `retry` and `expire`, and those three only carry their value in the record. `minimum` is the one field an answer depends on, because Ze stamps it as the TTL of the SOA record and as its MINTTL.
    - **contact** `string`: Responsible-party mailbox label (SOA RNAME), e.g. hostmaster
      The value becomes the RNAME field of the SOA record. A value with no dot is read as the mailbox local part under the zone, so the default builds hostmaster.<zone>. A value that holds a dot is used as a whole domain name, with the trailing dot added.
    - **expire** `uint32`: SOA expire seconds
      The value goes into the EXPIRE field of the SOA record, in seconds. It tells a secondary when to stop the service of a zone it can no longer refresh. geodns serves no AXFR, so no secondary acts on it, and the value changes no answer Ze gives.
    - **minimum** `uint32`: SOA minimum, the negative-cache TTL in seconds.
      SOA minimum, the negative-cache TTL in seconds. The range is 0 to 2147483647. The field is stamped as the SOA record's own TTL, so the RFC 2181 section 8 TTL range bounds it.
    - **mname** `string`: Primary nameserver (SOA MNAME). Defaults to ns1.<first-zone> when unset.
      The value becomes the MNAME field of the SOA record. Ze adds the trailing dot when the value has none. An unset leaf makes Ze build ns1.<zone> for each zone it serves, so the name follows the zone the query asked for. A commit is refused when the name breaks the length bounds RFC 1035 sets.
    - **refresh** `uint32`: SOA refresh seconds
      The value goes into the REFRESH field of the SOA record, in seconds. It tells a secondary how long to wait before it checks the serial again. geodns serves no AXFR, so no secondary acts on it, and the value changes no answer Ze gives.
    - **retry** `uint32`: SOA retry seconds
      The value goes into the RETRY field of the SOA record, in seconds. It tells a secondary how long to wait after a failed refresh. geodns serves no AXFR, so no secondary acts on it, and the value changes no answer Ze gives.
    - **serial** `uint32`: SOA serial used when serial-mode is fixed
      Ze reads this leaf only when `serial-mode` is fixed, and it then serves the value unchanged. The other two modes compute the serial and ignore the leaf. In fixed mode you own the increase after each change, under the serial arithmetic RFC 1982 defines.
    - **serial-mode** `enumeration`: How the 32-bit SOA serial is generated
      auto-epoch, the default, takes the Unix time in seconds at commit. It raises that by one when the result is not more than the previous serial, so two commits in one second still increase. auto-datetime builds YYYYMMDDnn (RFC 1912), and the 32-bit field leaves two counter digits, so it holds 100 revisions in one day. fixed serves the `serial` leaf unchanged.
      - `auto-datetime`: YYYYMMDDnn (RFC 1912); capped at 100 revisions/day by the 32-bit serial
      - `auto-epoch`: max(Unix seconds at commit, previous serial + 1); strictly increases at any rate
      - `fixed`: Use the serial leaf verbatim
  - **source <prefix>** `list`: Maps a client-IP prefix to a host-set.
    Maps a client-IP prefix to a host-set. The longest prefix wins. 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 are the catch-all external default.
    - **host-set** `string`: Name of the host-set to answer for clients matching this prefix
      The value names a `host-set` entry. A commit that names an unknown set is refused with 'references unknown host-set', and a source with no value here is refused as well. A client this prefix matches is answered from that set alone.
  - **tls** `container`: DNS-over-TLS listener and the certificate material shared with DoH.
    DNS-over-TLS (DoT, RFC 7858) listener and the certificate material shared with DoH. When the listener is enabled, DoT binds the configured listener IPs on 'listen-port'. When cert-file and key-file are unset, Ze uses an ephemeral self-signed certificate, which a strict client cannot validate.
    - **cert-file** `string`: Path to the PEM server certificate presented on DoT and DoH.
      Path to the PEM server certificate presented on DoT and DoH. Leave this leaf and key-file unset to select an ephemeral self-signed certificate.
    - **certificate** `string`: Name of the PKI store certificate to serve on DoT and DoH.
      Name of the certificate in the PKI store to serve on DoT and DoH. The listeners send the leaf certificate and every intermediate certificate the store entry holds. This leaf and cert-file/key-file are mutually exclusive, and setting both is a configuration error. The PKI store lives in the hub process, so a geodns plugin started as an external process cannot resolve the name. The secure listeners then do not start, and Ze logs the error. Cleartext DNS is unaffected.
    - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable the DNS-over-TLS listener (RFC 7858).
      The default is false, so geodns binds no DNS-over-TLS listener. A true value binds every `listener` IP on `listen-port`, beside the cleartext endpoints. When the certificate material does not load, Ze logs the error and starts no secure listener. The cleartext listeners stay bound.
    - **key-file** `string`: Path to the PEM private key matching cert-file. Must be set together with cert-file.
      The value is the path to the PEM private key of `cert-file`, and the two go together. Ze re-reads the pair on each commit, so a rotated key is picked up with no restart. This leaf and `certificate` are mutually exclusive, and a commit that sets both is refused. Leave both this leaf and `cert-file` unset to select an ephemeral self-signed certificate.
    - **listen-port** `port`: TCP port for the DoT listener; the RFC 7858 well-known 'domain-s' port is 853.
      The DoT listener binds this TCP port on every `listener` IP, and it uses no UDP. A commit with the value 0 is refused. Move the port off 853 only when a client can be told the new one, because a DoT client uses 853 by default.
  - **zone** `string[]`: Zones served, as fully qualified domain names.
    Zones served (FQDN). A query name must be one of these, or a name inside one, compared label by label. A name outside every zone draws REFUSED.
- **image-server** `container`: HTTP image server for PXE provisioning
  The server answers three paths under /install: the disk image, the boot files of the installer, and the zefs database the target starts with. Ze registers a path only when the leaves that feed it are set, so a path with nothing behind it answers 404.
  - **boot-directory** `string`: Directory containing installer kernel, initrd, iPXE config
    Ze serves the files of this directory under /install/boot/. An empty leaf registers no such path, and a client then gets 404. Ze builds /install/boot/boot.ipxe itself, and only when listen-interface names an interface whose address it can resolve.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable image server
    The default is false. When the leaf is true, Ze refuses the configuration unless image-directory or boot-directory names a directory. The plugin binds the port when the configuration is applied, and a bind that fails is reported in the log.
  - **image-directory** `string`: Directory containing gokrazy disk images
    Ze serves the files of this directory under /install/image/. An empty leaf registers no such path, and a client then gets 404. A request that reaches the path while the directory holds no image gets 503.
  - **listen-interface** `string[]`: Interfaces to serve on
    Ze resolves the IPv4 address of EVERY interface named here and binds listen-port on each one, as the TFTP server and the DHCP server do with the same leaf. With no interface named, Ze binds the port on every address of the host. An interface that does not resolve is named in the log and skipped, and the interfaces that do resolve still serve. When no interface binds at all, Ze logs 'no interfaces bound' and the image server serves nothing. Ze builds /install/boot/boot.ipxe only for a listener bound to an interface address, and the script names the address the client reached.
  - **listen-port** `uint16`: HTTP listen port
    The default is 80 and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze binds this port on the IPv4 address of each listen-interface. With no interface named, Ze binds the port on every address of the host.
  - **rescue-auth** `string`: Salted argon2id of the installer rescue token, as '<saltHex>:<digestHex>'.
    Ze emits the value on the installer kernel cmdline, as ze.rescue-auth, and the installer checks it before it opens the rescue shell. An empty value makes the installer fail closed, so a fatal error opens no shell. The PXE network carries this value unauthenticated, so it MUST commit only to a dedicated rescue token, and never to the admin password.
  - **ssh-password-hash** `string`: Bcrypt hash of admin password (written to served zefs)
    Ze refuses a value that bcrypt cannot read, so the target never gets a database with an unusable password. Only the hash reaches the served zefs database, so the cleartext password does not cross the PXE network.
  - **ssh-username** `string`: Admin username for installed target (written to served zefs)
    Ze writes this name and the password hash into a zefs database, and serves that database at /install/database.zefs. The target reads it and gets its first administrator. Write ssh-username and ssh-password-hash together, because Ze refuses one without the other.
- **tftp-server** `container`: Read-only TFTP server (RFC 1350)
  The server answers a read request on UDP port 69 and refuses every write request, so no client can put a file on this host. Ze accepts octet mode alone, and answers any other mode with an illegal operation error. Ze negotiates the blksize option of RFC 2348 and the tsize option of RFC 2349, and it does not support the windowsize option.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable TFTP server
    The default is false. When the leaf is true, Ze refuses the configuration unless root-directory names a directory. A configuration that names no listen-interface binds no socket, and Ze then logs that the server does not serve.
  - **listen-interface** `string[]`: Interfaces to serve TFTP on
    Ze opens one UDP socket for each interface of this list and binds the socket to that interface with SO_BINDTODEVICE. A logical interface name is resolved to its kernel device first. An interface that fails to bind is logged, and the others keep their socket.
  - **max-transfers** `uint16`: Maximum concurrent TFTP transfers
    The default is 10 and the range is 1 to 1000. The count is shared by every listener of the server. Over the limit Ze answers the read request with a TFTP error that carries the text service unavailable, and the transfers already open keep running.
  - **root-directory** `string`: Directory to serve files from
    Ze resolves each requested file under this directory and follows every symbolic link first. A file that lands outside the directory gets an access violation error, so a client cannot read the rest of the disk. The leaf is required when enabled is true.

## static

*Provided by `static` ([ze-static-cmd.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/static/yang/ze-static-cmd.yang), [ze-static-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/plugins/static/yang/ze-static-conf.yang))*

Static route configuration.

Ze programs each route into the kernel through netlink, or into the VPP dataplane, and marks it with the static protocol number. A route the backend cannot program is skipped and logged, and the rest of the section still applies. Only a forward route in the default table reaches the redistribute bus, where BGP can announce it.

- **table <name>** `list`: A named routing table that holds static routes.
  A named routing table grouping. The table name is resolved to a kernel table ID through the routing-table registry. Use 'default' for the main routing table.
  - **route <prefix>** `list`: A static route entry.
    The prefix is the key, so one table holds one entry for each prefix. Ze compares every leaf of the entry at a reload, the description included, and reprograms the route when one of them changed.
    - **action** `choice`: What to do with matching packets.
      One case is required. Ze stops the load for a route that names none of next, blackhole and reject, and it names the prefix in the error. Only the forward case reaches the redistribute bus.
      - **discard** `case`: Drop the packet and tell the sender nothing.
        The case holds the blackhole container, and the presence of that container selects the action. Ze installs the route with the kernel blackhole type, so the kernel drops the packet and answers nothing.
        - **blackhole** `container`: Drop the packet and send no ICMP message to the sender.
          The sender sees a timeout rather than a refusal, so a traceroute stops at this hop with no reply. Use reject when the sender SHOULD learn the destination is unreachable.
      - **forward** `case`: Send the packet on toward a next hop.
        The case holds the next container, which carries gateway next hops and interface next hops. Two or more next hops of either kind become one ECMP route. A redistribute consumer sees this case alone.
        - **next** `container`: Forward action. Contains gateway and interface next-hops that may be combined for ECMP.
          Ze reads the hop list and the interface list, and joins the two into one set of next hops. A route whose next container holds neither one stops the config load. One next hop becomes a plain route, and two or more become a multipath route.
          - **hop <address>** `list`: Forward via gateway. Multiple entries produce ECMP with traffic distributed by weight.
            The gateway address is the key, so one route holds one entry for each gateway. Ze shares the traffic between the entries in proportion to their weights. An entry can name its own BFD profile, and a next hop whose BFD session goes down leaves the group.
            - **bfd-profile** `string`: BFD profile name for this next-hop, from the bfd/profile list.
              BFD profile name (from bfd/profile list). When the BFD session to this next-hop goes down, Ze removes the next-hop from the ECMP group. Ze then reprograms the route with the remaining active next-hops.
            - **interface** `string`: Outgoing interface. Required when the next-hop is a link-local IPv6 address.
              Ze resolves the name to a kernel interface index and sets it on the route. A link-local IPv6 gateway needs it, because the same address can exist on every link. A name that resolves to no interface skips this one route, which show static routes then reports with its reason.
            - **weight** `uint16`: ECMP weight of this next-hop, 1 by default.
              ECMP weight. A higher value receives proportionally more traffic. The default of 1 gives equal distribution.
          - **interface <name>** `list`: Forward through the interface only, with no gateway address.
            Forward through the interface only, with no gateway address. This form serves point-to-point links, such as PPPoE and GRE tunnels, where the next-hop is implicit. Multiple entries can coexist with gateway next-hops for mixed ECMP.
            - **weight** `uint16`: ECMP weight. Higher values receive proportionally more traffic.
              The range is 1 to 65535, and Ze reads 0 as 1. The weight counts only against the other next hops of the same route. A route with one next hop ignores it.
      - **unreachable** `case`: Drop the packet and answer the sender.
        The case holds the reject container, and the presence of that container selects the action. Ze installs the route with the kernel unreachable type, so the kernel answers with ICMP destination unreachable.
        - **reject** `container`: Drop the packet and send an ICMP unreachable to the sender.
          The sender learns at once rather than waiting for a timeout, which is what separates this from blackhole. The reply itself costs a packet per dropped packet.
    - **description** `string`: Operator note for this route.
      The note reaches show static routes and nothing else. It is not sent to the kernel, and no filter reads it. Ze compares the note at a reload, so a change to the note alone reprograms the route. The length is 0 to 255 characters.
    - **metric** `uint32`: Route metric. Used as kernel route priority (lower is preferred) and carried in redistribute.
      Ze writes the value into the netlink route priority. The kernel prefers the lower priority when two routes cover the same prefix. 0 leaves the attribute out, so the kernel applies its own default. The redistribute event carries the same value.
    - **tag** `uint32`: Opaque tag Ze attaches to this route for policy and redistribution.
      Ze prints the value in the tag field of show static route and in the config diff. A redistribute import rule can select routes by tag: write the same value in a tag leaf under redistribute destination <proto> import static. When Ze redistributes the route into OSPF, it writes the value into the External Route Tag of the AS-external LSA, and the tag on the route wins over the tag configured for the source. Ze writes the value into no kernel route, because Linux has no route tag attribute. A change to tag alone re-applies the route, because the config diff compares the field.

## storage

Storage device management

The container holds the smart block alone. Ze reads it at config load and at each reload, and starts or stops the health manager to match.

- **smart** `container`: SMART disk health monitoring and self-test scheduling
  Ze polls each ATA and NVMe device it finds, and turns SMART on for a device that has it off. A reading past a threshold raises a warning or an error on the report bus, and a reading back under the threshold clears it. show storage smart prints the last reading of each device.
  - **check-interval** `uint32`: Health poll interval in seconds
    1800 seconds, which is 30 minutes, is the default, and the range is 60 to 86400 seconds. Ze polls once when the manager starts, and then at each interval. Every temperature test and every self-test decision happens on that poll, so this interval bounds how late an alert can arrive.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable SMART monitoring on all detected ATA/NVMe devices
    false is the default, and nothing else under this container is read while the leaf holds false. Ze reads the leaf as false unless it holds exactly true. A change to false at a reload stops the poll loop, and clears every warning and error this component raised.
  - **self-test** `container`: Periodic SMART self-test scheduling
    Ze decides at each health poll whether a test is due, so check-interval bounds how close to the wanted time a test can start. Ze starts no test on a device that is already running one, and tries again at the next poll.
    - **long** `container`: Extended self-test schedule
      Ze starts the extended test at a poll where three conditions hold. The weekday matches the day leaf, the time of day has passed, and the interval since the last test has passed. The extended test takes a weekday of its own, and the short test does not.
      - **day** `enumeration`: Preferred day of week for extended self-tests
        The seven weekday names are the accepted values, and sunday is the default. Ze reads the weekday from the local time of the appliance. The extended test starts on that day alone, whatever the interval leaf holds.
        - `friday`: Run the extended self-test on a Friday.
        - `monday`: Run the extended self-test on a Monday.
        - `saturday`: Run the extended self-test on a Saturday.
        - `sunday`: Run the extended self-test on a Sunday, the default.
        - `thursday`: Run the extended self-test on a Thursday.
        - `tuesday`: Run the extended self-test on a Tuesday.
        - `wednesday`: Run the extended self-test on a Wednesday.
      - **interval** `string`: Interval between extended self-tests, for example 7d
        The last letter names the unit: h for hours, d for days, m for minutes and s for seconds. A bare number is read as seconds. 7d is the default. A shorter interval still waits for the day leaf, so the test runs once in that week.
      - **time** `string`: Preferred time of day for extended self-tests (HH:MM)
        Ze starts the test at the first poll at or after this time on the named day. The clock is the local time of the appliance. 03:00 is the default. Ze skips the extended test while a short test is still running, and tries again at the next poll.
    - **short** `container`: Short self-test schedule
      Ze starts the short test at a poll where two conditions hold. The interval since the last test has passed, and the time of day has passed. The short test needs no weekday, and the extended test does.
      - **interval** `string`: Interval between short self-tests, for example 24h
        The last letter names the unit: h for hours, d for days, m for minutes and s for seconds. A bare number is read as seconds. 24h is the default, and Ze keeps the default and logs a warning for a value it cannot read.
      - **time** `string`: Preferred time of day for short self-tests (HH:MM)
        Ze starts the test at the first poll of the day at or after this time, and only when the interval has also passed. The clock is the local time of the appliance. 02:00 is the default.
  - **temperature** `container`: Temperature alert thresholds in degrees Celsius
    Ze reads the temperature at each poll and compares it against the three leaves. A device that reports 0 degrees is read as having no reading, and Ze then raises nothing for it.
    - **critical** `uint8`: Temperature above which a critical error is raised
      A reading at or above this value raises the temp-critical error, and clears the temp-high warning. 55 degrees is the default. Ze does not check that critical is more than informational, so a critical value at or under informational hides the informational warning completely.
    - **difference** `uint8`: Temperature change threshold for rate-of-change alerts
      Ze compares the reading against the reading of the previous poll. A rise of this many degrees or more raises the temp-rising warning, and a smaller rise clears it. The first poll of a device raises nothing, because no previous reading exists. The range is 1 to 50 degrees, and 4 is the default.
    - **informational** `uint8`: Temperature above which an informational warning is raised
      A reading at or above this value raises the temp-high warning, and a lower reading clears it. 45 degrees is the default. Ze tests the critical value first, so this warning never appears while the reading is also at or above critical.

## sysctl

*Provided by `sysctl` ([ze-sysctl-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/sysctl/yang/ze-sysctl-conf.yang))*

Kernel tunable management.

A setting entry applies to the host, and a profile entry applies to the interface units that name the profile. Ze validates a key it knows against the type and the range of that key. Ze accepts a key it does not know, and the kernel then refuses a value it cannot take.

- **profile <name>** `list`: A named collection of kernel tunables that Ze applies together to interface units.
  A user-defined profile overrides a built-in profile that has the same name.
  - **setting <name>** `list`: Kernel tunables in this profile.
    The list holds 50 entries at most. Ze applies these settings to each interface unit that names the profile, and it replaces <iface> in each key with the name of that unit. One profile therefore serves every interface.
    - **value** `string`: Value to set for this key.
      The leaf is mandatory, so Ze refuses a profile setting with no value. Every interface unit that names this profile gets the same value, because only the key carries the <iface> placeholder.
- **setting <name>** `list`: A kernel tunable that Ze sets persistently.
  The name uses kernel-native naming, for example net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding.
  - **value** `string`: Value to set for this key.
    The leaf is mandatory, so Ze refuses a setting with no value. Ze writes the text into the /proc/sys file of the key. A key Ze knows is checked first: a bool key takes 0 or 1, and a range key takes an integer inside its own bounds.

## system

System-level settings

The container holds the system-wide settings. This module attaches the local user accounts under authentication, and the command authorization profiles under authorization.

- **archive <name>** `list`: Named config archive destinations.
  Each entry names one destination, and Ze writes a copy of the config to every entry its trigger fires for.
  - **filename** `string`: Filename format with token substitution.
    The tokens are {name} for the config basename, {host}, {domain}, {date} as YYYYMMDD, {time} as HHMMSS, and {archive} for the block name. Ze appends .conf.
  - **location** `string`: Archive destination URL (file://, http://, https://).
    A file:// URL writes to the local filesystem. An http:// or https:// URL uploads the config with an HTTP request.
  - **on-change** `boolean`: Time-based only: skip if config unchanged since last archive.
    With true, Ze skips a daily or hourly archive when the config did not change since the last one. The leaf changes nothing for the commit trigger and the manual trigger.
  - **timeout** `string`: HTTP upload timeout, in Go duration format, for example 30s.
    Ze gives up on an upload that passes this timeout. The format is the Go duration format, such as 30s or 2m.
  - **trigger** `enumeration`: When to archive.
    The triggers are commit, manual, daily and hourly.
    - `commit`: Archive on every config commit.
    - `daily`: Archive once per day.
    - `hourly`: Archive once per hour.
    - `manual`: Archive only on explicit request.
- **authentication** `container`: System authentication settings
  System authentication settings. The user list under it holds the local accounts, which the local AAA backend reads. That backend runs after TACACS+ in the chain, so it answers when the remote server is unreachable. A configuration with no user rejects every local login.
  - **radius** `container`: RADIUS servers for operator login over SSH, web and MCP (RFC 2865).
    This block is separate from the L2TP subscriber RADIUS path, which lives under the l2tp root.
    - **auth-method** `enumeration`: Credential the Access-Request carries for an operator login.
      RFC 2865 Section 4.1 and RFC 3579 Section 3.3 Note 1 permit one credential and never two, so ze sends exactly one. Select chap only when the RADIUS server holds the operator password in cleartext. RFC 2865 Section 2.2 states that 'CHAP requires that the user's password be available in cleartext to the server so that it can encrypt the CHAP challenge and compare that to the CHAP response. If the password is not available in cleartext to the RADIUS server then the server MUST send an Access-Reject to the client.' A server that stores password hashes cannot verify CHAP and rejects every login. With pap the password is recoverable from a captured request by anyone who holds the shared secret, because Section 5.2 hides it with a reversible XOR. The two eap values run a full RADIUS/EAP conversation: ze answers EAP itself, as the peer, with the password the operator typed, and the server drives it through Access-Challenge packets. eap-md5 carries the same cleartext-password requirement as chap. eap-mschapv2 needs the server to hold the NT hash instead, which is what an Active Directory backed server holds.
      - `chap`: Send a CHAP-Password digest with the challenge in CHAP-Challenge.
      - `eap-md5`: Run an EAP MD5-Challenge conversation inside EAP-Message attributes.
      - `eap-mschapv2`: Run an EAP MS-CHAPv2 conversation inside EAP-Message attributes.
      - `pap`: Send the password in a User-Password attribute, hidden with the shared secret.
    - **default-profile** `string[]`: Ze authorization profiles used when the Access-Accept carries no profile-attribute.
      This leaf is optional. Leave it unset when the RADIUS server always names a profile through profile-attribute. When the server does not name one, and no default is set here, the login names no profile and is denied. Ze never authorizes a user it cannot attach a profile to.
    - **profile-attribute** `enumeration`: Access-Accept reply attribute that names the user's ze authorization profiles.
      Filter-Id is the only value. RFC 2865 Section 5.25 says of Class that 'the client MUST NOT interpret the attribute locally', so ze cannot read a profile name out of Class.
      - `filter-id`: RADIUS Filter-Id (11), RFC 2865 Section 5.11
    - **retries** `uint8`: Transmit attempts per server before failover
      The value counts the transmissions Ze sends to one server, and not the retransmissions after the first. With the default 3, Ze sends the Access-Request and retransmits it twice before it moves to the next server. The range is 0 to 10, and a configured 0 reaches the client as 3, because the client reads 0 as unset. The budget that bounds one login can then cancel the exchange partway through those transmissions. The login falls through to the local accounts, which is the answer a slow server gets too. Read timeout for the wait between the transmissions.
    - **server <address>** `list`: RADIUS servers, tried in configured order
      Ze sends the Access-Request to the first server, and it moves to the next one when that server does not answer. The order is the config order, because the list is ordered-by user. Each server gets a new Identifier, a new Request Authenticator, and the User-Password hidden again under the key of that server. RFC 2865 Section 4.1 requires the new Request Authenticator: 'The Request Authenticator value MUST be changed each time a new Identifier is used.' Where every server fails, the AAA chain moves on to the local accounts, so an unreachable server never locks the operator out. A row that carries no key builds no RADIUS backend at all, rather than a shorter server list.
      - **key** `string`: RADIUS shared secret (RFC 2865).
        RFC 2865 Section 3 states that the secret MUST NOT be empty (length 0). An empty secret lets an attacker forge packets.
      - **port** `uint16`: UDP authentication port (default 1812)
        1812 is the port officially assigned to RADIUS. RFC 2865 Section 3 states that 'Exactly one RADIUS packet is encapsulated in the UDP Data field, where the UDP Destination Port field indicates 1812 (decimal).' The range is 1 to 65535. Ze joins this port to the server address and resolves the pair as udp4. This block sends Access-Requests only, so it addresses the authentication port, and no accounting port is configured here.
    - **source-address** `ip-address`: Source IP for outbound RADIUS requests
