          - `eap-mschapv2`: EAP-MSCHAPv2: this peer proves its password by challenge and response.
          - `eap-tls`: EAP-TLS, Type 13 (RFC 5216): this peer authenticates with a certificate.
          - `pre-shared-secret`: Both ends prove the same secret, taken from the pre-shared-secret leaf.
          - `x509`: Sign AUTH with the named certificate and validate the remote one against ca-certificate.
        - **pre-shared-secret** `string`: Pre-shared key ($9$-encoded).
          Ze reads the leaf when the mode is pre-shared-secret, and when the mode is an EAP method that carries a password. The $9$ wrapper is removed first, and the pre-shared-secret-encoding leaf then decides whether the result is ASCII text or hexadecimal digit pairs.
        - **pre-shared-secret-encoding** `enumeration`: How to read the pre-shared-secret value.
          RFC 7296 Section 2.15 requires the management interface to accept both an ASCII string and a hex encoding of the shared secret. Set this to hex to supply the secret as hexadecimal digit pairs, which is the way to configure a secret holding non-printable octets. The encoding is stated here and is never guessed from the value. A secret such as abcdef0123456789 is both valid ASCII and valid hex, so reading it as hex would silently change an existing secret. A hex value with an odd length or a non-hexadecimal character is refused at commit rather than read as ASCII.
          - `ascii`: Read the secret as ASCII text, one octet for each character.
          - `hex`: Read the secret as hexadecimal digit pairs, two digits for each octet.
        - **remote-id** `string`: Identity the remote endpoint must assert.
          When it is set, Ze refuses an IKE_AUTH whose ID payload names another identity. Comparable types are ID_IPV4_ADDR, ID_IPV6_ADDR, ID_FQDN, ID_RFC822_ADDR, ID_KEY_ID, and ID_DER_ASN1_DN, and an address value accepts the two address types alone. A distinguished name is compared in RFC 4514 string form, and it binds against the certificate subject exactly, octet for octet. A value can name ONE peer or a SET of peers. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.3.1 requires both forms of Peer Authorization Database entry. A set is written with the hierarchy separator in front, and it admits the identities BELOW it and not the value itself: '.example.com' admits vpn.example.com, '@example.com' admits gateway@example.com, and ',ST=MA,C=US' admits every distinguished name whose top relative distinguished names are ST=MA,C=US. An address entry takes the same CIDR prefix the traffic-selector leaves take, so '10.0.0.0/24' admits every address in that block. ID_KEY_ID is always compared exactly, because an opaque octet string has no hierarchy to cut. The certificate binding stays per peer whichever form is used. A peer admitted by a set must still assert an identity its own certificate carries, so a set never widens what one certificate proves. When it is empty Ze checks no identity, so every certificate the ca-certificate issued authenticates as this peer. Set it whenever that authority issues to more than one client.
        - **remote-id-type** `enumeration`: The one IKE ID type the remote endpoint CAN assert.
          The one IKE ID type the remote endpoint CAN assert, and when absent any type Ze CAN compare, which is the historical behavior. When it is set Ze refuses every other type, so a peer asserting ID_FQDN with the text of a configured mail address is refused. RFC 7296 Section 4 requires that it be possible to configure Ze to accept a PKIX certificate where the identity passed is ID_KEY_ID. An opaque key id corresponds to no certificate field, so Ze cannot derive that binding and refuses it by default. Setting this leaf to key-id is the operator stating that a chain to ca-certificate plus the exact key id IS the intended binding. It governs what Ze ACCEPTS, and the type Ze sends still follows the shape of local-id.
          - `der-asn1-dn`: ID_DER_ASN1_DN, the DER-encoded subject name of a certificate.
          - `fqdn`: ID_FQDN, a fully qualified domain name.
          - `ipv4-address`: ID_IPV4_ADDR, an IPv4 address in four octets.
          - `ipv6-address`: ID_IPV6_ADDR, an IPv6 address in sixteen octets.
          - `key-id`: ID_KEY_ID, an opaque octet string no certificate field can bind.
          - `rfc822-address`: ID_RFC822_ADDR, a mail address such as user@example.com.
        - **session-resumption** `boolean`: Let an EAP-TLS exchange with this peer resume an earlier one.
          RFC 9190 Section 2.1.3 leaves resumption to each end: 'It is up to the EAP-TLS peer to use resumption', and 'the EAP-TLS server MAY choose to require a full handshake'. This leaf is that choice, and it covers both roles of this peer. With it true, an authentication that follows an earlier one skips the certificate exchange and reuses the session the ticket carries. Ze still checks the cached chain against the current ca-certificate and crl before it accepts the session, on both roles, so a revoked or expired certificate is refused on a resumed authentication as it is on a full one. With it false every authentication runs a full handshake. Ze still SENDS a session ticket, because RFC 9190 Section 2.1.2 makes that a MUST with no condition on it; the ticket is simply never accepted back. Changing this leaf, the certificate, the ca-certificate or the crl discards every ticket ze holds for this peer.
        - **x509** `container`: X.509 certificate references, deprecated in favor of the direct leaves.
          X.509 certificate references (deprecated, use the direct leaves). Ze reads a leaf here only when the direct leaf of the same name is empty. A name set here therefore meets the same requirement the direct leaf meets, and it is checked against the PKI store the same way.
          - **ca-certificate** `string`: Name of the CA certificate in the PKI store.
            Ze reads it only when the direct ca-certificate leaf is empty. It then satisfies the trust anchor that every EAP mode and X.509 require.
          - **certificate** `string`: Name of the device certificate in the PKI store.
            Ze reads it only when the direct certificate leaf is empty. It then satisfies the certificate that every EAP mode and X.509 require.
      - **connection-type** `enumeration`: Whether to initiate or wait for the remote peer.
        With `initiate` Ze starts the IKE_SA_INIT exchange toward remote-address. With respond Ze starts nothing and waits. Ze matches an unsolicited IKE_SA_INIT to a respond peer when the source address of the datagram equals its remote-address. A respond peer that names no remote-address therefore matches nothing.
        - `initiate`: Start the IKE_SA_INIT exchange toward remote-address.
        - `respond`: Start nothing and wait for an IKE_SA_INIT whose source is remote-address.
      - **esp-group** `string`: Reference to an ESP group name.
        The group MUST be declared under vpn ipsec esp-group, and commit refuses a name no group carries. It supplies the ESP proposals Ze offers for this peer's Child SAs and the lifetime those SAs run under.
      - **ike-group** `string`: Reference to an IKE group name.
        The group MUST be declared under vpn ipsec ike-group, and commit refuses a name no group carries. It supplies the IKE proposals, the IKE SA lifetime and the Dead Peer Detection timers of this peer.
      - **local-address** `string`: Local endpoint IP address.
        The value is an IP address literal. Ze reads it with net.ParseIP, so an interface name here resolves to nothing and the peer cannot build a Child SA. Name the interface under vpn ipsec interface instead, and Ze fills this leaf from the first IPv4 address of that interface.
      - **mode** `enumeration`: Encapsulation mode for this peer's Child SAs.
        Encapsulation mode for this peer's Child SAs. RFC 7296 Section 1.3.1 states the default itself: 'Except when using this option to negotiate transport mode, all Child SAs will use tunnel mode.' Ze asks for transport mode by sending USE_TRANSPORT_MODE with the Child SA request, and the peer can decline. A declined request establishes a tunnel-mode Child SA unless transport-required is set. Transport mode constrains the traffic selectors. RFC 7296 Section 2.23.1 requires exactly one IP address in TSi and in TSr, so every traffic-selector prefix under this peer must be a single host, and a vti binding is refused because an XFRM interface carries tunnel encapsulation.
        - `transport`: Protect the payload and keep the outer IP header (RFC 4301 transport mode).
        - `tunnel`: Encapsulate the whole packet (RFC 4301 tunnel mode).
      - **policy-priority** `uint32`: Rank of this peer's Security Policy Database entries, lowest searched first.
        Where this peer's Security Policy Database entries sit in the operator's ordering of that database. A LOWER value is searched FIRST, in Ze and in the Linux kernel. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: 'The ordering requirement arises because entries often will overlap due to the presence of (non-trivial) ranges as values for selectors. Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy.' The same section binds this interface: it 'MUST support (total) ordering of these entries, as seen via this interface'. Two peers whose traffic selectors overlap, 0.0.0.0/0 on both for example, describe the same traffic. Give the one that must win the lower value. Peers that share a value are ordered by whichever established last, which is what every peer did before this leaf existed, so the default 2000 keeps an unordered configuration installing exactly what it installed before. The range starts above 100, which is where the IKE control-plane bypass sits. A peer entry at or above that rank captures the IKE exchange that builds and rekeys the very SA it protects, and the tunnel could then never renegotiate. It ends at 2147483647, the largest rank Ze can carry to a dataplane.
      - **remote-address** `string`: Remote endpoint IPv4 address or DNS hostname.
        Ze resolves the value with net.ResolveUDPAddr over udp4 and sends IKE to port 500 there, so an IPv6 literal is refused with "ike: resolve remote". Ze builds the NAT detection hashes of RFC 7296 Section 2.23 from this value. It sends none when the value is not an address literal. An unsolicited IKE_SA_INIT reaches a respond peer only when its source address equals this leaf, character for character.
      - **traffic-selector <number>** `list`: The traffic this peer's Child SAs carry.
        The traffic this peer's Child SAs carry, and the policy RFC 7296 Section 2.9 narrows a peer's proposal against. When no entry is present the peer accepts whatever the remote endpoint proposes, which is the behavior of every configuration written before this list existed. Adding an entry restricts the peer: a proposal Ze cannot narrow to a non-empty subset of these entries is answered with TS_UNACCEPTABLE. RFC 7296 Section 2.9 permits several selectors, so this is a list.
        - **local** `container`: The local side of the selector pair (TSi when Ze initiates, TSr when Ze responds).
          The prefix under it is mandatory once a traffic-selector entry exists, and commit refuses an entry that leaves it out. The port under it takes any unless the protocol leaf names a protocol that carries ports.
          - **port** `union`: Local port of the selector.
            Local port of the selector. RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 requires the port fields to be 0 and 65535 whenever the protocol is 0 or defines no port, so a value other than any needs the protocol leaf to name a protocol that has ports.
            - `any`: Every port. RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 encodes it as start 0, end 65535.
          - **prefix** `ip-prefix`: Local traffic the Child SA carries.
            The value is a CIDR prefix, and Ze installs it as the local selector of the kernel policy. Under mode transport the prefix MUST cover exactly one address, a /32 or a /128. RFC 7296 Section 2.23.1 requires one IP address in TSi and in TSr, so commit refuses anything wider there.
        - **protocol** `uint8`: IP protocol number the selector matches.
          IP protocol number the selector matches, such as 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP. Zero matches every protocol, which is RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1's 'protocol 0'.
        - **remote** `container`: The remote side of the selector pair (TSr when Ze initiates, TSi when Ze responds).
          It obeys the rules the local container states. Ze narrows the peer's proposal against the pair of prefixes, and it answers TS_UNACCEPTABLE when no non-empty subset remains.
          - **port** `union`: Remote port of the selector.
            It follows the same rule as the local port: a value other than any needs the protocol leaf.
            - `any`: Every port. RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 encodes it as start 0, end 65535.
          - **prefix** `ip-prefix`: Remote traffic the Child SA carries.
            The value is a CIDR prefix, and Ze installs it as the remote selector of the kernel policy. The single-address rule the local prefix states applies here as well under mode transport.
      - **transport-required** `boolean`: Delete the SA when the peer declines transport mode.
        Whether a peer that declines transport mode is unacceptable. RFC 7296 Section 1.3.1: 'If the responder declines the request, the Child SA will be established in tunnel mode. If this is unacceptable to the initiator, the initiator MUST delete the SA.' Only the operator knows whether it is unacceptable, so this leaf carries that decision. When it is true and the response omits USE_TRANSPORT_MODE, Ze deletes the SA rather than run a tunnel-mode Child SA the operator did not ask for. When it is false the SA stays up in tunnel mode, which is the safe default. It applies only when mode is transport.
      - **vti** `container`: Virtual Tunnel Interface binding.
        The interface itself is declared under interfaces xfrm, where the if-id leaf carries the identifier a bound security association must match. Ze joins the two nowhere, so every Child SA is installed with if_id 0.
        - **bind** `string`: VTI interface name to bind this peer's traffic to.
          Route-based IPsec encrypts the traffic the routing table forwards into the named XFRM interface. Commit refuses a name beside mode transport, because an XFRM interface carries tunnel-mode encapsulation. No code maps the name to the if-id of that interface today. The Child SA is installed with if_id 0, and the binding carries no traffic.

## vpp

*Provided by `vpp` ([ze-vpp-conf.yang](https://github.com/ze-software/ze/blob/main/internal/component/vpp/yang/ze-vpp-conf.yang))*

VPP data plane configuration.

Ze reads this subtree at startup and writes /etc/vpp/startup.conf from it, then starts /usr/bin/vpp. A change committed later logs "config reload requires daemon restart to take effect" and does not reach VPP until the daemon restarts. The enabled leaf is false by default, so every other leaf here changes nothing until you set it to true.

- **api-socket** `string`: GoVPP binary API Unix socket path.
  Ze writes this path into the socksvr section of startup.conf and then connects to it through GoVPP. The path MUST be absolute, MUST NOT contain "..", and MUST be 108 characters or less, which is the Unix socket path limit. Under external true Ze writes no startup.conf, so this leaf is the only setting Ze needs to reach a VPP process another supervisor started. Ze retries the connection 10 times, one second apart, inside a 30-second budget.
- **cpu** `container`: VPP CPU pinning configuration.
  These leaves write the cpu section of startup.conf, and the main-core leaf pins the VPP main thread. The workers leaf asks for a count, and Ze takes those cores from the set the kernel isolated, which it reads from /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated. The worker-cores leaf names the cores instead, and it MUST NOT be set beside workers. The poll-sleep leaf sits here for the operator, and Ze emits it in the unix section, because that is where VPP reads poll-sleep-usec. Omit every leaf to let VPP place its own threads, and Ze checks a placement leaf you set at commit. Ze refuses a core the host does not hold, a worker core that is also main-core, and a worker count the host cannot satisfy.
  - **main-core** `uint8`: CPU core for VPP main thread. Omit for automatic assignment.
    Ze writes this core number into the cpu section of startup.conf as main-core. The core is excluded from the worker set, so the main thread and a worker never share a CPU. Omit the leaf and VPP picks the main core itself, and Ze still counts the worker list from core 1. A core the host does not hold online is refused at commit.
  - **poll-sleep** `string`: Fixed sleep between VPP main-loop polls, in whole milliseconds.
    Fixed sleep between VPP main-loop polls, expressed in whole milliseconds, which is the only accepted unit, for example 10ms. Ze emits it as unix { poll-sleep-usec N } in startup.conf, where 1ms is 1000 microseconds. Omit the leaf for VPP's default, where the workers busy-poll at 100% CPU with no sleep, and the latency is lowest. Set a non-zero value up to 100ms on a shared or dev host, to trade latency for idle CPU. An explicit 0ms is emitted and equals the default.
  - **worker-cores** `string`: Explicit CPU core list for the VPP worker threads.
    Ze writes these cores into the corelist-workers line of the cpu section in startup.conf, and writes no line when neither leaf is set. The syntax is the one the kernel uses for isolcpus: single cores, ranges, or both, as in 2-4 or 2,4,6. Set this leaf when the isolated set holds cores to keep for something else, and omit it to derive the cores from workers. It MUST NOT be set beside workers, because the two are separate answers to the same question, and Ze refuses a config that carries both. A core the host does not hold online, a core that is also main-core, and a core listed twice are each refused at commit. Cores outside the kernel's isolated set are accepted, and the vpp-cpu-isolation doctor check reports them.
  - **workers** `uint8`: Number of VPP worker threads. Omit for automatic (one per available core).
    Ze turns this count into the corelist-workers line of the cpu section in startup.conf, and the worker-cores leaf names those cores instead. Ze takes the cores from the set the kernel isolated at boot, lowest first, with main-core excluded. Isolated 2-4 with main-core 2 and workers 2 therefore emits corelist-workers 3-4. When the kernel isolated no core, the list is contiguous and starts one core after main-core, so 4 workers with main-core 1 emits corelist-workers 2-5. The vpp-cpu-isolation doctor check then reports that the workers share their CPUs with Linux. A count the host cannot satisfy is refused at commit, and a value of 0 emits no line, which is what an absent leaf does.
- **dpdk** `container`: DPDK NIC configuration.
  Every NIC listed here is unbound from its kernel driver and bound to vfio-pci before VPP starts, so Linux loses the interface. Ze saves the original driver name and rebinds it when the daemon stops. Under external true Ze binds nothing, because the external supervisor owns that step. An empty list emits no dpdk section in startup.conf.
  - **interface <pci-address>** `list`: DPDK-managed network interface.
    The list key is the PCI address, so this list holds one entry for each NIC. Ze loads the vfio, vfio_pci and vfio_iommu_type1 kernel modules, then binds each listed address to vfio-pci. A bind failure on one NIC unbinds every NIC Ze bound in the same pass, and VPP does not start.
    - **name** `string`: Short interface name (e.g. xe0, e1). Used in ze CLI and config.
      Ze writes this name into the dev entry of the dpdk section in startup.conf, so VPP calls the interface by it. The name is 1 to 15 characters of letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and dot, and a hyphen or a dot MUST NOT come first. Omit the leaf and Ze writes no name line, so VPP picks the interface name itself.
    - **rx-queues** `uint8`: Number of receive queues. Omit for VPP default.
      Ze writes this count into the dev entry of the dpdk section as num-rx-queues. An explicit 0 is written out, so it is not the same as an absent leaf. Omit the leaf and the line is absent, which leaves VPP on its own default. Ze does not compare the count against the queues the NIC holds.
    - **tx-queues** `uint8`: Number of transmit queues. Omit for VPP default.
      Ze writes this count into the dev entry of the dpdk section as num-tx-queues. An explicit 0 is written out, so it is not the same as an absent leaf. Omit the leaf and the line is absent, which leaves VPP on its own default. Ze does not compare the count against the queues the NIC holds.
- **enabled** `boolean`: Enable VPP integration, so Ze manages the VPP lifecycle.
  Enable VPP integration. When this leaf is true, Ze manages the VPP lifecycle. Ze generates startup.conf, binds the DPDK NICs, starts the VPP process, and connects through GoVPP.
- **external** `boolean`: Let an external supervisor own the VPP process, false by default.
  When this leaf is true, Ze does not exec or supervise the VPP process, generate startup.conf, or bind DPDK NICs. The external supervisor owns all of that. Ze only connects through GoVPP to api-socket. Use this leaf for systemd-managed VPP, for a container sidecar deployment, or for the `le test vpp` stub harness. The default is false, where Ze owns the VPP lifecycle.
- **lcp** `container`: Linux Control Plane plugin settings.
  Linux Control Plane plugin. The plugin creates TAP mirrors in Linux for VPP interfaces. A routing daemon such as ze BGP can then use Linux TCP on a VPP-managed NIC.
  - **auto-subint** `boolean`: Auto-create sub-TAPs for dot1q/QinQ sub-interfaces.
    When this leaf is true, Ze writes lcp-auto-subint into the linux-cp section of startup.conf. A dot1q or QinQ sub-interface created in VPP then gets its own Linux sub-TAP. When it is false, Ze omits the line, so a sub-interface has no mirror in Linux and only its parent interface does. The default is true, and lcp enabled MUST also be true before Ze writes the line.
  - **enabled** `boolean`: Enable LCP plugin in VPP.
    When this leaf is true, Ze enables linux_cp_plugin.so and linux_nl_plugin.so in startup.conf, and writes the linux-cp and linux-nl sections. When it is false, no other lcp leaf reaches startup.conf and the netns leaf is not validated. The default is true. LCP gives each VPP interface a TAP mirror in Linux, so a routing daemon binds an ordinary Linux socket.
  - **netns** `string`: Network namespace for LCP TAP interfaces. Routing daemons run in this namespace.
    Ze writes this name into the linux-cp section of startup.conf as default netns. VPP then creates the TAP mirrors under /var/run/netns/NAME. An EMPTY value is valid, and Ze then omits the line. It is the one value that leaves the TAPs in the namespace Ze runs in. An absent leaf is not the same as an empty one, because Ze seeds the default "dataplane" when the leaf is absent. With any name, Ze binds BGP in its own namespace and cannot bind on an LCP TAP address, which the doctor check vpp-lcp-netns reports. A name with a path separator, a space or an unprintable character is refused at commit. VPP truncates a name at a space, so the namespace it then opens under /var/run/netns/ does not exist.
  - **sync** `boolean`: Sync VPP state changes (link, MTU, IP) to Linux TAP mirrors.
    When this leaf is true, Ze writes lcp-sync into the linux-cp section of startup.conf. A link, MTU or address change made in VPP then reaches the Linux TAP mirror. When it is false, Ze omits the line and the two sides drift apart. The default is true, and lcp enabled MUST also be true before Ze writes the line.
- **memory** `container`: VPP memory and buffer configuration.
  These three leaves decide how much hugepage memory VPP asks the host for. The ze doctor check adds the main heap, the buffer memory and the stats segment together. It warns when the host reserved less hugepage memory than that sum. The hugepage-size leaf decides which page size VPP asks for, and it also governs the stats segment.
  - **buffers** `uint32`: Number of packet buffers per NUMA node. 128000 is proven for full DFZ at 10G.
    Ze writes this count into the buffers section of startup.conf as buffers-per-numa, beside a fixed default-data-size of 2048 bytes. So the pool costs the count multiplied by 2048 bytes on each NUMA node, and the default 128000 costs 250 MiB. A value of 0 is refused at commit with "vpp: memory buffers must be > 0".
  - **hugepage-size** `enumeration`: Hugepage size for VPP buffers.
    The two accepted values are 2M and 1G. For 1G Ze writes page-size 1G into both the buffers section and the statseg section of startup.conf. For 2M Ze writes page-size default-hugepage-size instead, which takes whatever the kernel holds as its default hugepage size. The ze doctor check warns when you select 1G on an amd64 CPU with no pdpe1gb flag, because the kernel then reserves no 1G page.
    - `1G`: Write page-size 1G into the buffers and statseg sections of startup.conf.
    - `2M`: Write page-size default-hugepage-size, which takes the kernel's default hugepage size.
  - **main-heap** `string`: VPP main heap size (e.g. 512M, 1G, 1536M). Production with full DFZ: 1536M.
    Ze writes this size into the heapsize section of startup.conf as main-heap-size. The value MUST be digits followed by M or G, so 1536M is accepted and 1.5G is refused at commit. The ze doctor check counts this size toward the hugepage memory it expects the host to have reserved.
- **plugins** `container`: Optional VPP plugins to load.
  Optional VPP plugin enablement. startup.conf uses 'plugin default { disable }', so Ze loads only the always-on plugins and the plugins toggled on here. The always-on plugins are dpdk, plus linux-cp when lcp is enabled.
  - **wireguard** `boolean`: Load wireguard_plugin.so for the vpp interface backend.
    Load wireguard_plugin.so so the vpp interface backend can program WireGuard tunnels. The tunnels are configured as interface wireguard under backend vpp.
- **stats** `container`: VPP stats segment configuration.
  The stats segment is the shared memory area VPP writes its counters into. Ze connects to it separately from the binary API and reads it for Prometheus metrics, at the interval poll-interval sets. A failed stats connection logs "vpp: stats connection failed, telemetry disabled" and leaves the rest of the VPP integration running.
  - **poll-interval** `uint16`: Stats polling interval in seconds.
    Stats polling interval in seconds. The interval controls how often Ze reads VPP's stats segment for Prometheus metrics.
  - **segment-size** `string`: Stats segment shared memory size.
    Ze writes this size into the statseg section of startup.conf as size. The value MUST be digits followed by M or G, so 512M and 1G are accepted and 512MB is refused at commit. The page size of the segment comes from memory hugepage-size and not from this leaf. The ze doctor check counts this size toward the hugepage memory it expects the host to have reserved.
  - **socket-path** `string`: Stats segment Unix socket path.
    Ze writes this path into the statseg section of startup.conf as socket-name, and the telemetry poller connects to it to read VPP's counters. The path MUST be absolute, MUST NOT contain "..", and MUST be 108 characters or less, which is the Unix socket path limit. This is a different socket from api-socket, which carries the binary API.
